questions.explanation: Le flic → le policier; les fringues → les vêtements; la clope → la cigarette; le gosse → l'enfant (in Québec, say les enfants: les gosses is vulgar there). Le médecin is the neutral word for le toubib, la voiture for la bagnole.

questions.stem: You are turning a team-chat message into a formal email. Which features must change? Select all that apply.
choices: a negation without ne (je sais pas)
a full stop at the end of a sentence
questions.explanation: On, the dropped ne, ça and questions by intonation all mark informal French; a formal email uses nous, ne … pas, cela and inversion or est-ce que. Full stops belong to every register.

questions.stem: Name the people around "moi" in this workplace diagram.

image.alt: A diagram with a young employee, moi, in the centre and four numbered figures: one above on a raised platform holding a folder, reached by an arrow marked vous; one on the right at a desk and one on the left next to a ball, both reached by arrows marked tu; one below behind a shop counter, reached by an arrow marked vous.

questions.explanation: Vous goes up to the manager (le supérieur hiérarchique, with the folder) and to the customer (la cliente, behind the counter); tu goes to the colleague at the next desk and to the teammate at the sports club (le coéquipier, with the ball).

questions.stem: "Tu pars quand ?" Which version is formal?
questions.explanation: Formal French puts the question word first and inverts: Quand partez-vous ? Vous partez quand ? is the same spoken question with vous; Quand vous partez ? is informal; Quand est-ce vous partez ? is missing que (quand est-ce que vous partez ?).

questions.stem: A friend says about a concert: "C'était trop bien !" What does she mean?
choices: It was too good to be true.
It was too much for her.
questions.explanation: Among younger speakers trop means "very": trop bien = really good. It's not a complaint.

questions.stem: "J'ai pas faim." What does it mean?
questions.explanation: Spoken French drops ne; pas alone carries the negation: je n'ai pas faim.

questions.stem: "Moi, mon frère, sa voiture, elle est en panne." What has broken down?
questions.explanation: Three topics are stacked (moi, mon frère, sa voiture) and the pronoun elle takes up the last one: la voiture de mon frère est en panne.

questions.stem: Which is the written version of "Les soirées chez Karim, j'y vais plus"?
choices: Je ne vais plus aux soirées chez Karim.
Je vais plus aux soirées chez Karim.
Je ne vais pas aux soirées chez Karim.
Je n'y vais plus aux soirées chez Karim.
questions.explanation: Put the noun back where y was and restore ne: je ne vais plus aux soirées. Without ne the sentence is still spoken; ne … pas changes the meaning (plus = no longer); and keeping y beside the noun repeats it.

questions.stem: You hear "chuis" in a voice message. What is it?
questions.explanation: Chuis is the reduced form of je suis in fast speech: the e of je drops and j + s fuse into a ch sound.

questions.stem: What does "quoi" do at the end of "Il est gentil, mais un peu lent, quoi."?
choices: It asks the listener a question.
It shows the speaker is angry.
It sums up and closes the speaker's turn.
It means "what" and expects an answer.
questions.explanation: At the end of a statement, quoi sums up, like "you know" or "I mean". The question word quoi (what) is a different use.

questions.stem: "C'est loin, hein ?" What does "hein" do here?
choices: It asks the listener to agree.
questions.explanation: Hein at the end asks for agreement, like "right?" or "isn't it?". On its own, Hein ? is a blunt "what?".

questions.stem: "Il y avait genre vingt personnes." What does "genre" mean here?
questions.explanation: Genre before a number is an approximation (about, like). It is informal and mostly used by younger speakers.

questions.stem: "On va au resto ce soir ? – Carrément !" What does the answer mean?
questions.explanation: Carrément (like grave and c'est clair) is strong informal agreement.

questions.stem: Which word is an informal word for water or rain?
questions.explanation: La flotte is informal for water or rain (il tombe de la flotte); it also means a fleet. La pluie is the neutral word for rain, la flûte a flute and la fontaine a fountain.

questions.stem: "J'ai répondu au pif." How did the speaker answer?
questions.explanation: Le pif is informal for the nose, and au pif means at random, at a guess.

questions.stem: "Il s'est pointé à minuit." What did he do?
choices: He pointed at the clock at midnight.
questions.explanation: Se pointer is informal for to turn up. Pointer without se is to clock in at work, which is a different verb use.

questions.stem: Listen to the voice message. Where is Inès?

audio.text: Salut Léa, c'est Inès. Bon, ben, chuis devant le resto, y a personne. T'es où ? Rappelle-moi, quoi.

questions.explanation: Chuis devant le resto = je suis devant le restaurant: she is outside the restaurant. Y a personne means nobody (Léa included) has turned up yet.

questions.stem: Listen to the podcast extract. What is the speaker complaining about?

audio.text: Franchement, le groupe WhatsApp, c'est devenu la galère : y a cinquante messages par jour et personne répond aux vraies questions.

choices: Nobody writes in the group any more.
Too many messages, and nobody answers the real questions.
questions.explanation: Y a cinquante messages par jour et personne répond aux vraies questions: fifty messages a day and nobody answers the real questions. C'est devenu la galère = it has become a hassle.

questions.stem: Write "Je sais pas" in careful written French.
questions.explanation: Restore ne: je ne sais pas. Je ne sais, with ne alone, is also correct in formal French (lesson 03).

questions.stem: Match each discourse marker to what it usually does.
questions.explanation: Ben hesitates (Ben, je sais pas); c'est clair agrees; genre before a number approximates (genre vingt personnes); bref sums up and closes a topic.

questions.stem: Which of these are reduced forms that you hear but shouldn't write in an essay? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Chuis (je suis), t'as (tu as), y a (il y a) and p't-être (peut-être) are reduced spoken forms. Il y a is the full written form.

questions.stem: The transcript under the sound wave is written in full. Which reduced form do you hear in each shaded stretch?

image.alt: A sound wave with four numbered shaded stretches. Underneath, the message in full: Salut, je suis devant le resto, tu as vu l'heure ? Il n'y a plus de place, il faut qu'on se grouille.

questions.explanation: In order: je suis → chuis; tu as → t'as; il n'y a → y a (ne and il both drop); il faut que → faut que. Nobody says peut-être or je ne sais pas in this message.

questions.stem: Put the words in order to write "Ce film, je l'ai adoré" without dislocation.
questions.explanation: Undo the dislocation: the noun goes back to the object position and the pronoun l' disappears: J'ai adoré ce film.

questions.stem: "Sans doute a-t-il raison." What does it mean?
choices: He's right, without a doubt in his mind.
questions.explanation: In modern French sans doute means probably, not "without a doubt" (that is sans aucun doute). The inversion a-t-il is the formal word order after sans doute.

questions.stem: Complete in careful written French, with aussi meaning "therefore": "Le budget manquait ; aussi ___ reporté le projet."
questions.explanation: After aussi meaning "therefore", careful writing inverts; with a noun subject that is complex inversion: le ministère a-t-il. Without inversion, aussi at the head reads as "also". The -t- is needed between a and il.

questions.stem: Complete: "Rares ___ les traités ratifiés aussi vite."
questions.explanation: Rares sont + noun subject: the verb agrees with les traités (plural) and is in the indicative.

questions.stem: Which is correct?
choices: Telle est la position de notre gouvernement.
Tel est la position de notre gouvernement.
Telle sont la position de notre gouvernement.
Tels est la position de notre gouvernement.
questions.explanation: Tel agrees with the subject that follows: la position is feminine singular, so telle est.

questions.stem: Which verb can be negated with ne alone in formal French? "Je n'___ y croire."
questions.explanation: Ne alone works with cesser, oser, pouvoir and savoir + infinitive: je n'ose y croire. With aimer, espérer or croire, standard French needs pas.

questions.stem: The ambassador says: "Je ne saurais accepter une telle proposition." What does she mean?
choices: I don't know how to accept such a proposal.
I didn't know I had accepted the proposal.
I couldn't possibly accept such a proposal.
I won't know until tomorrow whether I accept.
questions.explanation: The conditional of savoir with ne alone is a firm, polite refusal: I could not possibly accept.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Ce texte ne signifie pas nullement un recul.
Ce texte signifie nullement pas un recul.
Ce texte n'est nullement pas un recul.
Ce texte ne signifie nullement un recul.
questions.explanation: Nullement replaces pas: ne … nullement. It is never combined with pas.

questions.stem: Which phrase is correct in formal French?
questions.explanation: After comme, a noun subject may follow the verb with simple inversion and no hyphen. A pronoun subject can't be inverted here (comme elle le rappelait), and complex inversion isn't used after comme. The normal order, comme l'ambassadrice le rappelait, is also correct.

questions.stem: "Le traité est signé. Encore faut-il qu'il soit ratifié." What does the second sentence mean?
choices: Still, it has to be ratified.
It has already been ratified twice.
Once again it has been ratified.
questions.explanation: Encore at the head of the clause with inversion means "but then, even so": encore faut-il que + subjunctive = it still has to …

questions.stem: How is "solennel" pronounced?
questions.explanation: The first e of solennel (and of la solennité) is pronounced like a: so-la-nel, so-la-ni-té.

questions.stem: "L'accord sera signé demain, du moins le croit-on à l'ambassade." What does "du moins le croit-on" add?
choices: a minimum: the embassy believes it at the very least
a decrease: the embassy believes it less and less
a doubt: nobody at the embassy believes it
a correction: that's what the embassy believes, at least
questions.explanation: Du moins corrects or limits what was just said: or at least, that's what they believe. In writing it takes inversion (le croit-on).

questions.stem: Which sentence says correctly that the president arrived in the morning?
choices: Arrivée dans la matinée, la présidente a été accueillie par le chef du protocole.
Arrivée dans la matinée, le chef du protocole a accueilli la présidente.
Arrivé dans la matinée, la présidente a été accueillie par le chef du protocole.
Arrivée dans la matinée, on a accueilli la présidente.
questions.explanation: A participle in apposition refers to the subject of the main clause: arrivée … la présidente. With le chef du protocole or on as the subject, the sentence says that they arrived; and arrivé without -e doesn't agree with la présidente.

questions.stem: What is "la préséance"?
choices: the presence of the head of state
the order of precedence at an official event
questions.explanation: La préséance decides who enters first, sits where and speaks when: l'ordre de préséance.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio item. What is still uncertain?

audio.text: La cheffe d'État norvalienne est arrivée ce matin pour une visite officielle de deux jours. Le traité de coopération sera signé demain ; reste à savoir si le Parlement le ratifiera avant l'été.

choices: whether the head of state has arrived
whether the treaty will be signed tomorrow
whether parliament will ratify the treaty before the summer
how long the visit will last
questions.explanation: Reste à savoir si le Parlement le ratifiera avant l'été: it remains to be seen whether parliament will ratify it before the summer. The arrival, the signing date and the two-day visit are stated as facts.

questions.stem: Listen to two diplomats disagreeing. What does the second one say?

audio.text: Je ne saurais accepter cette clause. – Nous n'avons nullement l'intention de vous l'imposer, mais elle protège vos étudiants.

choices: They insist on keeping the clause.
They are withdrawing from the treaty.
They have no intention of imposing the clause.
questions.explanation: Nous n'avons nullement l'intention de vous l'imposer = we have no intention whatsoever of imposing it on you; the speaker then gives a reason for the clause.

questions.stem: Complete with a formal adverb meaning "in no way", other than nullement: "Nous n'avons ___ l'intention de nous retirer."
questions.explanation: Ne … aucunement, like ne … nullement, is a formal negation: we have no intention whatsoever of withdrawing.

questions.stem: Put the parts in order to write, formally: "The minister is probably right."
questions.explanation: Sans doute at the head of the clause, then complex inversion with a noun subject: the noun, the verb, the repeating pronoun (a-t-il), then the rest.

questions.stem: Which sentences use ne alone correctly in formal French? Select all that apply.
choices: Il ne cesse de pleuvoir depuis lundi.
Si je ne m'abuse, la séance est levée.
questions.explanation: Ne alone works with cesser and oser + infinitive and in the fixed phrase si je ne m'abuse. Travailler and manger need pas: il ne travaille pas le lundi, il ne mange pas de viande.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this state-visit scene.

image.alt: A state-visit scene with six numbered parts: two people shaking hands behind a table; an open document on the table; a group of three people in dark suits on the left; a woman with a sash and a folder in front of them; a man with an earpiece and a clipboard on the right; a row of seated guests in the background between two flags.

questions.explanation: The two heads of state shake hands over the treaty; the ambassador (with the sash) stands in front of her delegation; the head of protocol, with his earpiece and clipboard, watches; the seated guests are the dignitaries.

questions.stem: Complete: "Le virement a été ___ le 3 mars."
questions.explanation: Effectuer goes with a payment or a transfer: effectuer un virement. You accomplir a task, élaborer a plan and exercer a profession.

questions.stem: Complete: "Elle ___ le métier de correctrice depuis vingt ans."
questions.explanation: Exercer un métier: to work in a profession. Effectuer is for payments and operations, comporter for parts of a whole, détenir for a record, rights or power.

questions.stem: Complete: "Le roman ___ trois parties."
questions.explanation: Comporter (to comprise) replaces avoir for the parts of a whole: le roman comporte trois parties. (Compte trois parties would also work; it isn't offered.)

questions.stem: Which phrase is a pleonasm?
questions.explanation: Prévoir already means to foresee, to plan in advance, so à l'avance repeats it. The other three are normal phrases.

questions.stem: How do you correct "Ils ont collaboré ensemble pendant dix ans"?
choices: Ils ont collaboré ensemble durant dix ans.
Ensemble, ils ont collaboré pendant dix ans.
Ils ont collaboré pendant dix ans.
Ils ont ensemble collaboré pendant dix ans.
questions.explanation: Collaborer already includes "together", so ensemble goes. Moving it or changing pendant to durant keeps the pleonasm.

questions.stem: Which word is a hyperonym of "le roman", so that it can replace it later in a text?
questions.explanation: L'ouvrage (or le livre) is a more general word that covers le roman. A chapter and a preface are parts of a novel, and la nouvelle (a short story) is another kind of text, not a more general word.

questions.stem: Which description of "au jour d'aujourd'hui" is most accurate?
choices: Common in speech, but usage guides criticise it as a pleonasm: avoid it in writing.
A formal phrase recommended for essays.
A grammatical error that nobody actually says.
questions.explanation: Au jour d'aujourd'hui repeats jour; it is frequent in speech, often for emphasis or as a joke, and criticised by usage guides. In writing, aujourd'hui or à l'heure actuelle.

questions.stem: Which version is lightest while keeping the meaning of "Le livre que l'auteur qui a reçu le prix a publié est épuisé"?
choices: Le livre que l'auteur qui a reçu le prix a publié, il est épuisé.
Le livre publié par l'auteur primé est épuisé.
Le livre qui est le livre que l'auteur primé a publié est épuisé.
L'auteur qui a reçu le prix, son livre qu'il a publié est épuisé.
questions.explanation: A participle (publié par) and an adjective (primé, prize-winning) replace the two relative clauses. The other versions add a dislocation or extra relatives and stay heavy.

questions.stem: In publishing, what is "une coquille"?
questions.explanation: Une coquille is a misprint or typo; in other contexts it is a shell (une coquille d'œuf).

questions.stem: The editor writes: "Il faudrait étoffer votre conclusion." What should the author do?
questions.explanation: Étoffer = to flesh out, to give more substance. To shorten would be raccourcir or alléger.

questions.stem: Which noun goes with "dresser"?
questions.explanation: Dresser une liste (or un bilan, un constat): to draw up. Effectuer un virement, exercer un métier, détenir un record.

questions.stem: Which phrase is redundant?
questions.explanation: Car en effet uses two connectors for the same cause. Car or en effet alone is enough.

questions.stem: What makes a text concise?
choices: It uses nouns instead of verbs wherever possible.
It is as short as possible, whatever is lost.
It says a lot in few words, with no empty phrases or repetition.
questions.explanation: Concision is a quality: no padding (il est important de noter que, au niveau de), no redundancy, but nothing important lost. A paragraph of noun groups without verbs is dense, not concise.

questions.stem: Listen to the editor's message. What did she find in chapter two?

audio.text: Bonjour, ici Hélène Marchal. J'ai relu votre deuxième chapitre : le style est fluide, mais j'ai recensé une dizaine de répétitions. Pourriez-vous m'envoyer la version révisée avant vendredi ?

questions.explanation: J'ai recensé une dizaine de répétitions: she listed about ten repetitions. She says the style is fluide (it flows).

questions.stem: Listen to two editors disagreeing about a title. What does the second one care about most?

audio.text: Ce titre est trop long, il nous faut quelque chose de plus percutant. – Je ne suis pas d'accord : il est long, mais il est clair, et c'est ce qui compte.

questions.explanation: Il est long, mais il est clair, et c'est ce qui compte: for the second editor, clarity matters most. The first wants something punchier (plus percutant).

questions.stem: Replace the all-purpose verb with a precise one: "faire une liste" → "___ une liste" (infinitive).
questions.explanation: Dresser une liste, établir une liste or rédiger une liste. Recenser can also replace the whole phrase (recenser les erreurs = list the errors), but it takes the things listed as its object, not une liste.

questions.stem: Match each all-purpose phrase to the precise verb that replaces its verb.
questions.explanation: Effectuer un virement, détenir un record, énoncer une règle, élaborer un plan. Comporter is for parts (le livre comporte trois parties) and alléger is to lighten.

questions.stem: Which are pleonasms? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Monter already means going up, voire already means "or even" (voire même is common but criticised), and chance is by definition unforeseen. Prévoir un budget and descendre l'escalier repeat nothing.

questions.stem: Which fault has the editor marked in each numbered box?

image.alt: A manuscript page with four numbered boxes in the margin, each linked to a mark in the text: 1 to the circled word mmer, 2 to the circled sentence Le temps était froid ce matin-là after Il faisait froid, 3 to the circled phrase monter en haut, 4 to a long sentence with several relative clauses underlined with a wavy line.

questions.explanation: Mmer for mer is a typo (une coquille); the second sentence repeats the first (une redondance); monter en haut is a pleonasm; the long sentence with three relatives is heavy (la lourdeur). Concision is a quality, not a fault.

questions.stem: In Liège, who is "la bourgmestre"?
questions.explanation: Le bourgmestre, la bourgmestre is the mayor in Belgium (le maire, la maire in France). The word comes from Dutch.

questions.stem: A colleague in Brussels writes: "Je ne sais pas venir demain." What does she mean?
choices: She doesn't know whether she'll come tomorrow.
She doesn't know how to get there tomorrow.
questions.explanation: In Belgium savoir is used for pouvoir (ability, possibility): je ne sais pas venir = je ne peux pas venir. In France the sentence would mean she doesn't know how to come.

questions.stem: A friend in Montréal asks: "Tu viens-tu ?" What is the second "tu"?
questions.explanation: In informal Québec French, -tu after the verb marks a yes/no question: Tu viens-tu ? = are you coming? Recognise it; you don't need to use it.

questions.stem: Friends in Lausanne invite you "pour le dîner". When should you arrive?
questions.explanation: In Switzerland, Belgium and Québec le dîner is the midday meal and le souper the evening meal.

questions.stem: What is "une votation"?
choices: a vote by the people on a question, in Switzerland
an election of a mayor in France
a vote of the Belgian parliament
questions.explanation: La votation is the Swiss word for a popular vote on a law or an initiative, as against une élection, which chooses people.

questions.stem: "Il fait moins vingt, mets ta tuque !" What should you put on?
questions.explanation: La tuque is the Québec word for a woolly hat (le bonnet in France).

questions.stem: In Québec, you say "Merci !" and hear "Bienvenue !". What does it mean?
questions.explanation: In Québec bienvenue answers merci, where France says de rien or je vous en prie.

questions.stem: Which body applies the Charte de la langue française?
choices: the Délégation à la langue française
the Conseil de la langue française et de la politique linguistique
the Office québécois de la langue française
questions.explanation: The OQLF applies Québec's Charte de la langue française (1977). The DLF is Swiss, the Académie French, and the Conseil advises the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles.

questions.stem: Since when has Switzerland's Délégation à la langue française existed?
questions.explanation: The DLF was created in 1992 and works under the CIIP. 1961 is the creation of Québec's Office de la langue française, 1977 the Charte de la langue française, 2002 the year the Office became the OQLF.

questions.stem: A Belgian says "mon GSM". What would most people in France say? Give the noun with its article.
questions.explanation: Le portable (A2) in France; le natel in Switzerland, le cellulaire or le cell in Québec. Le mobile and le smartphone are also heard in France.

questions.stem: Match each word to where it is used.
questions.explanation: La panosse (floorcloth) and la votation are Swiss; le bourgmestre (mayor) is Belgian; la tuque is from Québec.

questions.stem: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.
choices: The written standard is shared by France, Belgium, Switzerland and Québec.
Regional words such as septante are informal.
Huitante is used everywhere in French-speaking Switzerland.
In Belgium, le dîner is the midday meal.
questions.explanation: The written standard is shared; septante is Belgian (and Swiss); le dîner is lunch in Belgium. Regional words like septante belong to every register in their area, and huitante is heard only in some cantons (Vaud, Valais, Fribourg).

questions.stem: "La votation aura lieu le 9 juin. Pour le stand, il nous faut nonante chaises et une panosse." Where was this written?
questions.explanation: Nonante alone could be Belgian, but la votation and la panosse are Swiss.

questions.stem: Listen to the message. Which country is the speaker most probably from?

audio.text: Salut Thomas, je passe chez toi tantôt, vers cinq heures. Appelle-moi sur mon GSM si tu n'es pas là.

questions.explanation: Tantôt for "later today" and le GSM for the mobile phone are both Belgian.

questions.stem: You want your manager to approve next year's budget. Which subject line is best?
questions.explanation: A subject line says what the email is about and, if needed, what is asked. Question, Urgent !!! and Bonjour tell the reader nothing.

questions.stem: You write to the accounts department of a company where you know nobody. Which greeting fits?
questions.explanation: Madame, Monsieur, is the standard greeting when you don't know who will read the message. Salut and coucou are informal; cher ami is for someone you know well.

questions.stem: Which closing is the commonest in everyday professional emails?
questions.explanation: Cordialement (or Bien cordialement) is the neutral professional closing. The others are for friends.

questions.stem: "Je vous mets en copie de ce message." What does the writer do?
choices: She forwards you an old message.
questions.explanation: Mettre quelqu'un en copie = to copy someone in (Cc). En copie cachée (Cci) is bcc.

questions.stem: Which sentence is a polite reminder?
choices: Je constate votre silence et j'en tire les conséquences.
Sauf erreur de ma part, je n'ai pas encore reçu votre réponse.
questions.explanation: Sauf erreur de ma part (unless I'm mistaken) leaves room for a lost message and accuses no one. The others reproach, are informal, or threaten.

questions.stem: How does a note de service differ from an email to one person?
choices: It has a header and no greeting or closing formula.
It starts with Madame, Monsieur and ends with a signature.
It is written by employees to their manager.
questions.explanation: A note de service goes from management to staff, with a header (De, À, Date, Objet), an impersonal style and no greeting or closing.

questions.stem: What is the item "Questions diverses" on an agenda?
choices: questions sent in advance to the director
the main item of the meeting
a list of frequently asked questions
questions.explanation: Questions diverses (any other business) usually closes the agenda.

questions.stem: Which tense rule applies to minutes?
choices: Present or passé composé, the same one throughout.
Any tense, changing with the speaker.
questions.explanation: Minutes use the present (La directrice rappelle que …) or the passé composé (La directrice a rappelé que …): choose one and keep it.

questions.stem: The secretary's note reads "Décidé : on coupe les déplacements." Which sentence belongs in the minutes?
choices: On coupe les déplacements, c'est décidé.
J'ai trouvé qu'on devait couper les déplacements.
Il est décidé de réduire les frais de déplacement.
questions.explanation: Minutes are impersonal and factual: il est décidé de + infinitive, with a precise noun (les frais de déplacement). On, dislocation and the secretary's opinion don't belong.

questions.stem: Complete the usual formula for an attachment: "Vous trouverez ___ le compte rendu de la réunion."
questions.explanation: Vous trouverez ci-joint le compte rendu (ci-joint before the noun doesn't agree). En pièce jointe and en annexe are also correct.

questions.stem: Put the parts of this email in order.
choices: Objet : demande de devis, traduction d'un rapport
Pourriez-vous nous adresser un devis pour la traduction de notre rapport ?
questions.explanation: Subject line, greeting, the request, the closing, then the signature.

questions.stem: What should the minutes of a working meeting contain? Select all that apply.
choices: the people present and those excused
the actions: who does what, by when
every joke made during the meeting
the secretary's personal opinion of each speaker
questions.explanation: Minutes record the facts of the meeting: date, place, participants, decisions and actions. They report decisions, not every remark, and never the writer's opinions.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this email.

image.alt: An email window with five numbered boxes on the right, linked to: the Cc line, the subject line, the greeting Bonjour Madame Diallo, the closing Bien cordialement, and a paper clip with the file name ordre-du-jour.pdf.

questions.explanation: The Cc line shows who is copied in (en copie); the subject line is l'objet; Bonjour Madame Diallo is the greeting (la formule d'appel); Bien cordialement is the closing (la formule de politesse); the file with the paper clip is the attachment (la pièce jointe).

questions.stem: Listen to the voicemail. What is the caller offering?

audio.text: Bonjour, j'ai le regret de vous informer que la réunion de travail de jeudi est annulée. En revanche, nous pouvons vous proposer un appel vendredi à 14 heures.

choices: a phone call on Friday at 2 p.m.
nothing: the meeting is simply cancelled
questions.explanation: En revanche, nous pouvons vous proposer un appel vendredi à 14 h: the bad news comes first (the Thursday meeting is cancelled), then an alternative.

questions.stem: Match each slang word to its neutral equivalent.
questions.explanation: Chelou, zarbi, vénère and la teuf are verlan of louche, bizarre, énervé and fête; la thune is old argot for money. Le père is the neutral word for le daron.

questions.stem: A teenager says a film was "chanmé". What does she think of it?
questions.explanation: Chanmé is verlan of méchant, which in slang can mean terrific: chanmé is praise.

questions.stem: "On a perdu en finale, j'ai le seum." How does the speaker feel?
questions.explanation: Avoir le seum = to be gutted, bitter (slang, usually traced to an Arabic word for poison).

questions.stem: "Mes darons veulent pas que je sorte." Who doesn't want the speaker to go out?
questions.explanation: Les darons = parents (le daron, dad; la daronne, mum): an old argot word now used by teenagers.

questions.stem: How was "meuf" made from "femme"?
choices: A vowel sound was added (fa-meu), the syllables were swapped and the last vowel dropped.
It is the feminine of mec.
It comes from an English word.
questions.explanation: Verlan works on sounds: femme becomes fa-meu, swapped to meu-fa, then meuf. Reversing the letters would give nonsense.

questions.stem: What is reverlanisation?
choices: the spread of verlan into dictionaries
reversing a verlan word again once it is too common
questions.explanation: When a verlan word becomes too widespread, speakers reverse it again: meuf → feumeu, beur → rebeu.

questions.stem: Why does slang age so fast?
choices: Dictionaries ban slang words after ten years.
Slang words are always replaced by English ones.
Once everyone uses a word, it no longer marks the group, which replaces it.
questions.explanation: Slang marks belonging; when parents, advertisers and learners use a word, the group drops it. Chébran (verlan of branché) now sounds like the 1980s.

questions.stem: In which situation is the word "meuf" least risky?
choices: among close friends who use it themselves
describing a colleague to your manager
talking to a woman you have just met
questions.explanation: La meuf is everyday among young people who use it, but said of a woman you don't know, or to her, it can sound disrespectful; in writing at work it is out of place.

questions.stem: Which language does the slang verb "chouraver" (to steal) come from?
questions.explanation: Chouraver is the classic Romani loan in French slang. Arabic gave toubib, kif and seum; English gave chiller.

questions.stem: What is the verlan of "bizarre"?
questions.explanation: Bi-zarre has two syllables: swap them and you get zar-bi, zarbi.

questions.stem: Which of these words are verlan? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Chelou (louche), vénère (énervé) and la teuf (fête) are verlan. La thune and le daron are old argot words, not reversed words.

questions.stem: Listen to the message. What was the speaker's problem?

audio.text: Hier c'était la teuf chez Yanis, trop chanmé, mais j'avais plus une thune pour le taxi.

choices: He had no money left for a taxi.
questions.explanation: J'avais plus une thune pour le taxi = I didn't have a penny left for the taxi. The party itself was trop chanmé (brilliant).

questions.stem: Give the neutral word for the slang "la thune", with its article.
questions.explanation: La thune (slang) and le fric (informal) both mean l'argent, money.

questions.stem: What did "argot" originally mean?
choices: the secret language of thieves and beggars
the language of the royal court
questions.explanation: L'argot first meant the secret language of thieves and beggars; today it is any group's slang.

questions.stem: Complete the notice: "Que personne ne ___ avant la fin de la séance." (sortir)
questions.explanation: With no main verb, que + subjunctive gives an order about a third person: "Que personne ne sorte" (nobody is to leave). "Sort" and "sortira" are indicative, "sortirait" conditional: none of them can follow this que.

questions.stem: What does "Qu'à cela ne tienne" mean in: "Le comité ne se réunit qu'en mai ? Qu'à cela ne tienne, nous lui écrirons."?
choices: That is out of the question.
Never mind, that is no obstacle.
questions.explanation: "Qu'à cela ne tienne" (a frozen subjunctive of tenir à, to depend on) brushes an obstacle aside: the committee doesn't meet until May, never mind, we'll write to it. "It all depends on that" is the literal trap: the phrase says the opposite.

questions.stem: What does "Le comité n'a rien décidé, que je sache." mean?
choices: As far as I know, the committee hasn't decided anything.
I hope the committee hasn't decided anything.
The committee mustn't decide anything without my knowledge.
I'd like to know whether the committee has decided anything.
questions.explanation: "Que je sache" is a set subjunctive meaning "as far as I know", very often with a negative statement. It expresses neither a hope nor a request for information.

questions.stem: A friend tells you he is starting a miracle diet. You answer: "Grand bien te fasse !" What are you most likely expressing?
questions.explanation: "Grand bien vous (te) fasse" (much good may it do you) can be a sincere toast, but in reply to a miracle diet it is ironic: the speaker doesn't believe in it. It is neither a warning nor an apology.

questions.stem: What does "Qu'un seul donneur se retire, et l'essai s'arrête." mean?
choices: If even one donor withdraws, the trial stops.
One donor has withdrawn, so the trial has stopped.
So that no donor withdraws, the trial is stopping.
Only one donor may withdraw before the trial stops.
questions.explanation: Que + subjunctive followed by "et" + a consequence is a formal hypothesis: the same as "Si un seul donneur se retire, l'essai s'arrête". Nothing has happened yet, so "has withdrawn" is wrong, and there is no idea of purpose.

questions.stem: Complete: "Qu'il ___ d'accord ou non, il devra signer le formulaire." (être)
questions.explanation: An alternative with que … ou non takes the subjunctive, because neither possibility is asserted: "Qu'il soit d'accord ou non". "Est" and "sera" are indicative, "serait" conditional.

questions.stem: Complete: "Certains volontaires abandonnent, soit qu'ils n'aient pas compris l'information, soit qu'ils ___ peur des effets secondaires." (avoir)
questions.explanation: Soit que … soit que gives two possible causes and takes the subjunctive in both halves: "soit qu'ils aient peur". "Ont" and "avaient" are indicative, "auraient" conditional.

questions.stem: Complete: "Comme le comité était divisé et qu'il ___ des données, la décision a été reportée." (manquer)
questions.explanation: The que stands for a repeated "comme", and it keeps comme's mood: the indicative. The first clause is in the imparfait, so "qu'il manquait". "Manquât" and "ait manqué" are subjunctives (only si allows that switch), and "manquerait" is a conditional.

questions.stem: In careful written French, which form usually completes the second clause? "Si le comité donne son accord et que les fonds ___ disponibles, l'essai commencera en mars."
questions.explanation: After si, a substitute que traditionally takes the subjunctive, and careful writing still prefers it: "et que les fonds soient disponibles". The indicative "sont" is also accepted and very common, so it is not offered here. "Seront", "seraient" and "étaient" don't fit either pattern.

questions.stem: Which statement about "Si le patient accepte et qu'il aille bien / qu'il va bien, il rentrera chez lui" is right?
choices: Only the indicative is correct, because si takes the indicative.
Both are correct: the subjunctive is more formal, the indicative very common.
Only the subjunctive is correct; the indicative is a mistake.
Neither is correct: the second clause must repeat si.
questions.explanation: A que replacing si may take the subjunctive (careful, traditional) or the indicative (accepted, very common). The OQLF describes the subjunctive as usual and the indicative as accepted. Repeating si is possible but not required.

questions.stem: In "Les associations se plaignent de ce que les familles ne sont pas consultées", what is "de ce que"?
choices: A relative meaning "of what": they complain about what the families said.
A comparison: they complain more than the families do.
A formal way to introduce the cause of the complaint; both moods occur after it.
A condition: they will complain if the families aren't consulted.
questions.explanation: After verbs of feeling built with de (se plaindre de, s'étonner de), "de ce que" introduces the cause. It is more formal than que, and both the indicative (a fact, as here) and the subjunctive occur after it.

questions.stem: What does "Puissent ces recherches aboutir !" mean?
questions.explanation: Puisse / puissent + infinitive, with inversion and no que, is a literary wish (recognition only): may this research succeed! It is neither a statement of possibility nor a question.

questions.stem: What is "le consentement éclairé"?
choices: Consent given by the family alone
Informed consent, given after clear information
A signed form with no explanation
questions.explanation: Éclairé means informed: the person has understood the information, especially the risks, before agreeing. Presumed consent (le consentement présumé) is a different thing.

questions.stem: What does "encadrer" mean in "La loi encadre strictement la recherche sur l'embryon"?
questions.explanation: Encadrer here is to regulate, to set limits around an activity (close to réglementer). It doesn't ban or fund it; the picture-frame sense doesn't fit a law.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio item. What does its second sentence mean?

audio.text: Le comité d'éthique de l'hôpital Saint-Aubin a reporté sa décision. Qu'un seul des membres s'y oppose, et l'essai ne pourra pas commencer. Réponse attendue en mai.

choices: The trial needs the support of only one member.
If even one member objects, the trial can't start.
questions.explanation: The item says "Qu'un seul des membres s'y oppose, et l'essai ne pourra pas commencer": a formal hypothesis with que + subjunctive. Nobody has objected yet; the committee simply postponed its decision until May.

questions.stem: Listen to two people disagreeing. What does the second speaker think?

audio.text: — Qu'on l'autorise ou non, cet essai fera débat. — Justement : qu'on attende encore, et des enfants perdront la vue.

choices: Waiting longer would cost children their sight, so the trial shouldn't be delayed.
The trial should be stopped because it is too risky.
The debate doesn't matter because the law has decided.
The trial should wait until more data are available.
questions.explanation: The first speaker says the trial will be debated whether it is allowed or not ("Qu'on l'autorise ou non"). The second answers with a hypothesis: "qu'on attende encore, et des enfants perdront la vue": if we wait any longer, children will lose their sight.

questions.stem: Complete the two set phrases: "Advienne que ___ !" (come what may) and "Pas que je ___." (not that I know of)
questions.explanation: Both are frozen subjunctives: "Advienne que pourra" (advenir; pourra is the future of pouvoir, part of the fixed phrase) and "pas que je sache" (savoir, subjunctive sache).

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "If even one donor withdraws, the trial stops."
questions.explanation: Qu'un seul donneur se retire, et l'essai s'arrête. The que-clause with the subjunctive comes first, then et and the consequence.

questions.stem: Match each set phrase with its meaning.
choices: Whether you like it or not
questions.explanation: Each is a frozen subjunctive with no main verb. "Whether you like it or not" would be "que vous le vouliez ou non", an alternative clause.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct in careful written French? Select all that apply.
choices: Bien que l'essai soit prometteur et qu'il ait reçu des fonds, il reste fragile.
Puisque l'essai a commencé et qu'il soit financé, il faut le poursuivre.
Qu'il le veuille ou non, il devra signer.
Qu'il vient ou qu'il ne vient pas, la séance commencera.
questions.explanation: "Que personne ne sorte" is an independent subjunctive. After bien que, the substitute que keeps the subjunctive (qu'il ait reçu). "Qu'il le veuille ou non" is an alternative in the subjunctive. After puisque the que keeps the indicative (qu'il est financé), and an alternative needs the subjunctive (qu'il vienne ou non).

questions.stem: Name the use of the subjunctive in each numbered box.

image.alt: Four boxes with their headings blanked and numbered. Box 1: Qu'il patiente ! Que personne ne sorte ! Box 2: Advienne que pourra. Qu'à cela ne tienne. Box 3: Qu'un seul donneur se retire, et l'essai s'arrête. Box 4: Puisse-t-il guérir ! Plût au ciel qu'il fût là !

questions.explanation: Box 1 gives orders for a third person; box 2 holds frozen phrases; box 3 is a hypothesis followed by et and its consequence; box 4 holds literary wishes with inversion or the imperfect subjunctive (recognition only).

questions.stem: Complete: "Hier, le chef de chantier m'a dit que la tranchée ___ encore ouverte, mais on l'a rebouchée ce matin."
questions.explanation: After a past main verb, an action at the same time takes the imparfait: "était". The present "est" can stay only for something still true, and the trench has been filled in since. "Sera" and "serait" put it in the future.

questions.stem: In a past narrative about a dig that ended long ago, complete: "L'archéologue pensait qu'on ___ d'autres tombes plus au nord."
questions.explanation: A later action seen from a past main verb takes the conditionnel présent, the future of the past: "trouverait". "Trouvera" would only work if the finding were still ahead of us now; "trouvait" and "a trouvé" don't express a later event.

questions.stem: Complete: "On m'a appris que des pilleurs ___ le site la nuit précédente."
questions.explanation: The looting came before the moment of being told, so the plus-que-parfait: "avaient pillé". "La nuit précédente" confirms it. "Pillaient" is same-time background, "pilleraient" a later event, and "ont pillé" ignores the past main verb.

questions.stem: In modern French, complete: "Le préfet a exigé qu'on ___ les travaux." (suspendre)
questions.explanation: Exiger que takes the subjunctive, and modern French uses the present subjunctive after a past main verb for the same time or later: "qu'on suspende". (Classical prose would write "qu'on suspendît"; it is not offered here.) The other choices are indicative or conditional.

questions.stem: Complete: "Le maire regrettait que les pilleurs ___ plus tôt."
questions.explanation: Regretter que takes the subjunctive, and the arrest that didn't happen comes before the regret ("plus tôt"), so the subjonctif passé: "n'aient pas été arrêtés". The other choices are indicative or conditional.

questions.stem: A novel published in 1900 has: "Je doutais qu'il fût venu." What would a modern writer put?
questions.explanation: "Qu'il fût venu" is a pluperfect subjunctive (classical concordance after a past verb). Modern French uses the subjonctif passé: "qu'il soit venu". "Qu'il vienne" loses the earlier time; douter que doesn't take the indicative or the conditional here.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il affirme ___ les pilleurs hier soir."
questions.explanation: The seeing comes before the claim, so the past infinitive: "avoir vu". Affirmer takes the infinitive directly, without de. "Voir" would be the same time; "qu'il voie" is wrong with the same subject.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ le site pendant dix ans, elle en connaissait chaque strate."
questions.explanation: The digging came before her knowledge, so the past participle form "ayant fouillé" (having dug). "Avoir fouillé" can't open the sentence on its own, "après" needs the past infinitive (après avoir fouillé), and "fouillée" is a passive participle.

questions.stem: Complete: "Si on avait fouillé plus tôt, on ___ aujourd'hui qui était enterré là."
questions.explanation: A mixed hypothetical: past condition (si + plus-que-parfait), present result ("aujourd'hui"), so the conditionnel présent: "saurait". "Aurait su" would put the result in the past and clash with aujourd'hui.

questions.stem: He is a careless man in general, and the digging is over. Complete so that the condition describes his permanent character: "S'il ___ prudent, il n'aurait pas creusé là."
questions.explanation: A permanent condition with a past result: si + imparfait, then the conditionnel passé: "S'il était prudent, il n'aurait pas creusé là." Si never takes the conditional or the subjunctive, and "est" would make it a real condition.

questions.stem: Which sentence keeps the present after a past verb because it states a general truth?
choices: Elle m'a dit qu'il est parti la veille.
On croyait que le sous-sol est vide.
Il pensait que les fouilles commencent le lendemain.
Le guide a rappelé que la céramique se conserve mieux que le bois.
questions.explanation: That pottery keeps better than wood is true at all times, so the present can stay after "a rappelé". In the other sentences the clause is tied to the past story (la veille, le lendemain, an old belief), so the tense must shift.

questions.stem: Compare "Il a rappelé que le site date du Néolithique" and "Il a rappelé que le site datait du Néolithique". Which statement is right?
choices: Both are correct; the present adds that the speaker vouches it is still true.
Only datait is correct after a past main verb.
Only date is correct, because it is a fact.
Date means that the site no longer exists.
questions.explanation: With a fact that is still true, both tenses are correct. The imparfait simply reports what he said; the present adds the speaker's own commitment that it is true now.

questions.stem: In a story told years later, complete: "Le chef a annoncé qu'ils ouvriraient le sarcophage ___." (He had said: "demain".)
questions.explanation: In a past narrative, time words shift with the tenses: demain becomes le lendemain (the next day). "La veille" is the day before, "hier" yesterday from today's point of view.

questions.stem: What does "mettre au jour" mean in "Un ouvrier a mis au jour le col d'une amphore"?
questions.explanation: Mettre au jour is to unearth, to bring to light. Mettre à jour (with à) means to update. Dater is to date; ensevelir or enfouir to bury.

questions.stem: What is "une découverte fortuite"?
choices: A fortunate discovery for the owner
questions.explanation: Fortuit means by chance, accidental: the amphora was found by a worker digging foundations. It doesn't mean fortunate, a common false friend.

questions.stem: Listen to the news item. When will the building work resume?

audio.text: Flash info. Sur le chantier du futur parking de Vaurenne, les archéologues ont mis au jour une nécropole antique. Le promoteur espérait que les travaux reprendraient en septembre ; ils ne reprendront qu'au printemps.

choices: Never: the car park is cancelled
questions.explanation: The developer hoped work would resume in September ("espérait que les travaux reprendraient en septembre": future of the past), but it will only resume in the spring ("ne reprendront qu'au printemps").

questions.stem: Listen to the lecture extract. What does the lecturer mean?

audio.text: Si l'on avait protégé ce site dans les années soixante-dix, nous saurions aujourd'hui bien plus de choses sur ses habitants.

choices: The site was protected in the 1970s, so we know a lot today.
The site wasn't protected in the 1970s, so we know less today.
The site will be protected soon, and we will learn more.
Nobody knows whether the site was ever protected.
questions.explanation: "Si l'on avait protégé ce site …, nous saurions aujourd'hui bien plus de choses" is a mixed hypothetical: an unreal past condition (it wasn't protected) with a present result (we know less now).

questions.stem: Complete for a past narrative: "Elle croyait qu'il ___ (venir) le lendemain." and "Il espérait ___ (finir) les fouilles avant juin." (finished before then)
questions.explanation: "Viendrait" is the future of the past after croyait. "Avoir fini" is the past infinitive: the finishing would be complete before June, seen from the hope.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "The guide explained that the cave had been discovered in 1940."
questions.explanation: Le guide a expliqué que la grotte avait été découverte en 1940. The discovery comes before the explanation, so the plus-que-parfait (here passive: avait été découverte, agreeing with la grotte).

questions.stem: Complete "Il a dit que …" for each time relation (main verb in the past).
questions.explanation: After a past main verb: imparfait (same time), plus-que-parfait (earlier), conditionnel présent (later: the future of the past), conditionnel passé (done before a later point). The future sera ignores the past main verb.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct in a past narrative in careful written French? Select all that apply.
choices: Je voulais qu'on protège le site.
Il exigeait que les fouilles soient terminées avant l'hiver.
Elle pensait qu'on trouvera d'autres tombes l'année suivante.
Ils espéraient avoir fini avant juin.
Il a affirmé voir les pilleurs la veille.
questions.explanation: Modern concordance uses the present subjunctive after a past verb (protège, soient terminées), and "avoir fini" is the right past infinitive. "Trouvera" should be "trouverait" (future of the past, with "l'année suivante"), and "voir" should be "avoir vu" (the seeing came first).

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in this section of a dig.

image.alt: A cross-section of the ground with four layers and four numbered markers: 1 on a tall jar with two handles, 2 on a stone coffin with a lid, 3 on small orange pottery shards in the second layer, 4 on the third layer itself.

questions.explanation: The tall two-handled jar is an amphora (l'amphore), the stone coffin a sarcophagus (le sarcophage), the shards are pottery (la céramique), and each band of earth is a layer (la strate). No looter or cave is shown.

questions.stem: In an obituary: "Deux ans plus tard, elle remportait le prix de la Ville de Lyon." What does the imparfait mean here?
choices: She was in the middle of winning the prize.
She used to win the prize every year.
She won the prize: one completed event, given weight.
She would have won the prize.
questions.explanation: After a time phrase, in writing, the imparfait narratif presents one completed event, like a final shot. It doesn't describe a background, a habit or an unreal event.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the présent historique?
choices: En 1895, les frères Lumière projettent leurs premiers films à Paris.
Le train part demain à 8 heures.
questions.explanation: The Lumière sentence tells a past event (1895) in the present: présent historique. The others are a general truth, a near future in speech, and a scheduled future.

questions.stem: At a counter, which sentence softens the request with the imparfait?
choices: Je voulais vous demander un renseignement.
questions.explanation: "Je voulais vous demander …" places the request in the past, which makes it less direct: the imparfait d'atténuation. The other three are direct (present, imperative) or even demanding.

questions.stem: A biography reads: "Elle quitte l'école à quinze ans. Elle ne le sait pas encore : vingt ans plus tard, elle exposera à Paris." Which translation of "exposera" fits?
questions.explanation: The futur historique jumps forward from a point inside a past story. English, telling the story in the past, needs "would": "twenty years later, she would exhibit in Paris". "Will" breaks the past narrative; the others give the wrong time or aspect.

questions.stem: The doorbell rings, and someone says: "Ce sera le facteur." What does the future express?
questions.explanation: This is the future of supposition: "that'll be the postman". The speaker is guessing about the present. B2's futur antérieur of supposition does the same for the past (Il aura oublié).

questions.stem: A parent says: "Tu rangeras ta chambre avant de sortir." What is the future doing?
questions.explanation: The futur injonctif gives an instruction that leaves no room for discussion, firmer than the imperative. It is not a prediction, and it softens nothing.

questions.stem: What does "Un pas de plus, et il tombait." mean?
choices: One more step and he would have fallen.
He was falling with every step.
He used to fall after one step.
He fell after one more step.
questions.explanation: The hypothetical imparfait describes what nearly happened: one more step and he would have fallen (but he didn't). It is not a habit, a background or a real fall.

questions.stem: Which statement about "Quand il a eu fini son tableau, il l'a signé." is right?
choices: It is a passé antérieur, the tense of written narrative.
It is a passé surcomposé: spoken and regional; careful writing says "Quand il a fini" or "Après avoir fini".
It is a mistake that no French speaker uses.
It is a plus-que-parfait of politeness.
questions.explanation: "A eu fini" has two auxiliaries: the passé surcomposé, heard in speech and in some regions, for recognition only. It is not a mistake nobody uses, and the passé antérieur would be "quand il eut fini".

questions.stem: Arriving at an office, someone says: "J'étais venu vous parler de mon projet." What does it mean?
choices: I had come a long time ago and left.
I came to talk about it, but I've changed my mind.
I'd like to talk to you about my project (said very politely).
I would have come if I had had a project.
questions.explanation: The plus-que-parfait d'atténuation softens a present purpose even more than the imparfait: the speaker has just arrived and wants to talk about the project.

questions.stem: What does "Elle s'est éteinte samedi, à l'âge de 94 ans." mean?
choices: She switched off her phone on Saturday.
She passed away on Saturday, aged 94.
questions.explanation: S'éteindre is a gentle, respectful way of saying "to die", common in obituaries; of a light or a fire, it means "to go out". Décéder is the administrative word.

questions.stem: What does "Le ministre est tombé en disgrâce après le scandale." mean?
choices: He fell ill after the scandal.
He resigned in protest after the scandal.
He was promoted after the scandal.
He lost favour after the scandal.
questions.explanation: La disgrâce is loss of favour with the powerful (tomber en disgrâce). It isn't illness, a protest or a promotion.

questions.stem: Which word means "a gift left in a will"?
questions.explanation: Le legs (verb léguer) is a bequest. La postérité is posterity, la consécration the crowning recognition of a career, le palmarès a list of prizes.

questions.stem: What is "un peintre autodidacte"?
questions.explanation: Autodidacte means self-taught: someone who learned without a teacher or school. It says nothing about self-portraits or solitude.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio item. What happened ten years after her first concert?

audio.text: La pianiste Hélène Morin s'est éteinte hier à quatre-vingt-sept ans. Née à Lille, elle donne son premier concert à neuf ans. Dix ans plus tard, elle remportait un grand concours international.

choices: She won a major international competition.
questions.explanation: "Dix ans plus tard, elle remportait un grand concours international": an imparfait narratif after a time phrase, telling one completed event. Her first concert was at nine; she died aged eighty-seven.

questions.stem: Listen to two people disagreeing. What does the second speaker think?

audio.text: — Ta biographie est entièrement au présent ? Ça fait roman. — Justement : le présent rend la vie plus vivante, et tous les journaux l'emploient.

choices: A biography should always be in the passé composé.
The present is a mistake in a biography.
The present makes the life more vivid, and the press uses it all the time.
Biographies should be written like novels, in the passé simple.
questions.explanation: The first speaker objects that a biography in the present "sounds like a novel". The second defends the présent historique: it makes the life more vivid, and every newspaper uses it.

questions.stem: Rewrite in the présent historique: "Elle est née en 1931 et elle a quitté l'école à quinze ans." → "Elle ___ en 1931 et elle ___ l'école à quinze ans."
questions.explanation: The présent historique puts each past verb in the present: "Elle naît en 1931 et elle quitte l'école à quinze ans." (1990 spelling: nait.)

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "Two years later, she won the prize." (imparfait narratif)
questions.explanation: Deux ans plus tard, elle remportait le prix. The time phrase opens the sentence, as it usually does with the imparfait narratif.

questions.stem: Match each sentence with the value of its tense.
left: Je voulais vous demander un service.
On sonne : ce sera le facteur.
En 1940, quatre adolescents découvrent la grotte.
questions.explanation: A softened request, one completed event after a time phrase, a guess about the present, and a past event told in the present. No sentence has two auxiliaries, so none is a passé surcomposé.

questions.stem: Which sentences use a tense to make a request more polite? Select all that apply.
choices: Je voulais vous demander un renseignement.
J'étais venu vous parler de ma mère.
questions.explanation: The imparfait and plus-que-parfait d'atténuation (voulais, étais venu) and the futur de politesse (demanderai) soften requests. The futur injonctif (rangeras) is a firm order, and the imparfait narratif (mourait) tells an event.

questions.stem: Name the tense used in each numbered part of the timeline.

image.alt: A timeline of a painter's life in four boxes with their tense names blanked and numbered. 1: 1931-1960, Elle naît en 1931. Elle quitte l'école. 2: 1964-1978, En 1978, un musée lui consacrait une rétrospective. 3: jump ahead, Ces planches seront exposées dans un musée. 4: 2026, Elle s'est éteinte samedi.

questions.explanation: naît, quitte: past events in the present (présent historique); consacrait after a date: one completed event (imparfait narratif); seront exposées: a jump forward from inside the story (futur historique); s'est éteinte: the news itself (passé composé).

questions.stem: What does "Il a sans doute raison." mean?
choices: He may be right, but I doubt it.
He is right, but nobody believes him.
questions.explanation: Sans doute means "probably", a classic trap. To say "without any doubt", French uses sans aucun doute or sans nul doute.

questions.stem: Which sentence commits the writer most strongly?
choices: Ce résultat est sans doute encourageant.
Il n'est pas exclu que ce résultat soit encourageant.
questions.explanation: Incontestablement (indisputably) is at the top of the scale. Sans doute is "probably", peut-être "perhaps", and il n'est pas exclu que only says it can't be ruled out.

questions.stem: In careful written French, complete: "Il n'est pas exclu que l'échantillon ___ trop petit."
questions.explanation: Il n'est pas exclu que expresses a possibility and takes the subjunctive: "soit". The indicative and the conditional don't follow it.

questions.stem: In careful written French, complete: "Il est peu probable que ce chiffre ___ exact."
questions.explanation: Il est peu probable que expresses doubt and takes the subjunctive: "soit". Compare il est probable que, which takes the indicative (il est probable que ce chiffre est exact).

questions.stem: Which statement about "Il semblerait que l'échantillon soit trop petit" and "… est trop petit" is right?
choices: Only the indicative is correct, because it is a fact.
Neither is correct: il semblerait que takes the conditional.
Both are correct; the subjunctive is the more usual choice.
questions.explanation: Il semblerait que, softer than il semble que, is found with both moods. The subjunctive is more usual; the indicative presents the impression as closer to a fact. Il me semble que takes the indicative.

questions.stem: Which sentence reports a claim without endorsing it?
choices: Le produit protège contre la grippe.
Il est certain que le produit protège contre la grippe.
Le produit protégerait contre la grippe.
Le produit a protégé des milliers de patients contre la grippe.
questions.explanation: The reportive conditional ("protégerait") presents the claim as someone else's: the product supposedly protects. The other sentences state it as a fact.

questions.stem: What does "ce prétendu remède" suggest?
choices: The writer doubts it is really a cure.
The cure has been officially approved.
questions.explanation: Prétendu (so-called, alleged) shows distance: someone claims it is a cure, and the writer doubts it. Présumé is the legal equivalent (le présumé coupable).

questions.stem: Which is correct in careful written French?
questions.explanation: Soi-disant never agrees: des soi-disant experts. Prétendu does agree: une prétendue étude. For things, many careful writers prefer prétendu, though soi-disant is common and accepted.

questions.stem: Complete: "Après vérification, l'information s'est avérée ___."
questions.explanation: S'avérer + adjective: the adjective agrees with the subject, l'information (feminine singular), so "fausse". "Faux" and "fausses" don't agree, and the adverb "faussement" can't follow s'avérer.

questions.stem: Where does "manifestement" go? Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: In a compound tense the adverb usually goes between the auxiliary and the participle: "Il s'est manifestement trompé." It can also open the sentence with a comma (Manifestement, il s'est trompé), but it doesn't trigger inversion as peut-être and sans doute can.

questions.stem: Which reporting verb shows the weakest commitment by the person reported?
questions.explanation: From strong to weak: affirmer > soutenir > estimer > penser > supposer. "Les auteurs supposent que …" reports only an assumption.

questions.stem: Which sentence is hedged appropriately for a scientific summary?
choices: Les écrans détruisent la mémoire des enfants.
Tout porte à croire qu'un usage excessif des écrans peut nuire à la mémoire des enfants, mais les études restent peu nombreuses.
Il est incontestable que les écrans détruisent la mémoire des enfants.
Il semblerait que les écrans puissent peut-être sans doute nuire à la mémoire.
questions.explanation: The hedged sentence uses one hedging phrase (tout porte à croire que), a modal verb (peut nuire) and a stated limit. Two choices overstate; the last stacks hedges until it says nothing.

questions.stem: What is "la vulgarisation scientifique"?
choices: The popularisation of science for the general public
The peer review of a study
questions.explanation: La vulgarisation explains science to the general public: un ouvrage de vulgarisation is a popular science book. It has nothing to do with vulgarity.

questions.stem: Which phrase marks information as unconfirmed?
questions.explanation: Sous toute réserve flags unconfirmed information. Selon toute vraisemblance means "in all probability", il y a lieu de "there is reason to", and incontestablement "indisputably".

questions.stem: Listen to the radio item. How sure is the station about the study being withdrawn?

audio.text: Selon nos informations, et sous toute réserve, l'étude aurait été retirée par la revue. Les auteurs n'ont pas encore réagi.

questions.explanation: "Sous toute réserve" and the reportive conditional ("aurait été retirée") both mark the information as unconfirmed. The authors haven't reacted yet.

questions.stem: Listen to two people disagreeing. What does the second speaker think?

audio.text: — C'est prouvé : le café fait vivre plus longtemps ! — Prouvé, c'est vite dit. Il semblerait qu'il y ait un lien, c'est tout.

choices: The study proves that coffee makes you live longer.
There may be a link, but nothing is proven.
questions.explanation: "Prouvé, c'est vite dit" (proven is a big word) rejects the first speaker's certainty, and "il semblerait qu'il y ait un lien, c'est tout" admits only a possible link.

questions.stem: Complete with the past participle of s'avérer: "L'hypothèse s'est ___ fausse."
questions.explanation: S'avérer takes être, and the participle agrees with the subject, l'hypothèse (feminine): "s'est avérée fausse".

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "Everything suggests that the link is real."
questions.explanation: Tout porte à croire que le lien est réel. Tout porte à croire que (everything suggests that) takes the indicative.

questions.stem: Match each adverb with the degree of certainty it expresses.
questions.explanation: Incontestablement is certain, manifestement says the conclusion is plain from what anyone can see, sans doute means probably (not 'without doubt'), and peut-être only possibly. None of them says impossible.

questions.stem: Which devices show that the writer is keeping a distance from a claim? Select all that apply.
choices: Le virus aurait été détecté dès mars.
Ses « preuves » tiennent en trois captures d'écran.
Il est certain que le virus a été détecté en mars.
Ce résultat est incontestablement le plus solide.
questions.explanation: The reportive conditional (aurait été détecté), prétendu and quotation marks of distance all attribute the claim to someone else. Il est certain que and incontestablement express the writer's own certainty.

questions.stem: Put each expression at its level on the certainty thermometer.

image.alt: A thermometer of certainty with five levels, each with a blank numbered box for an expression: 1 certain (il est certain que + indicatif), 2 very likely (tout porte à croire que + indicatif), 3 likely (il semble que + subjonctif), 4 possible (il n'est pas exclu que + subjonctif), 5 doubtful (il est peu probable que + subjonctif).

questions.explanation: Incontestablement is certain; selon toute vraisemblance very likely; sans doute (= probably) likely; peut-être possible; guère probable (hardly likely) doubtful. Soi-disant is a distancing word, not a degree of certainty.

questions.stem: When were the Lettres persanes first published?
questions.explanation: The Lettres persanes came out in 1721. Montesquieu was born in 1689, De l'esprit des lois appeared in 1748, and the 1758 edition, after his death, has 161 letters.

questions.stem: What did the title page of the first edition say?
choices: Cologne, at Pierre Marteau, a cover name: the book was printed in Amsterdam
questions.explanation: The book appeared anonymously with a false imprint, "Cologne, Pierre Marteau", a cover name used by many forbidden books; it was in fact printed in Amsterdam by the house of Jacques Desbordes.

questions.stem: What is an epistolary novel?
choices: A novel told entirely through letters between characters, with no narrator
A novel about the Church's epistles
A travel diary written by one narrator
questions.explanation: Un roman épistolaire tells its story through letters exchanged between characters. The reader builds the story from several points of view, with no narrator.

questions.stem: In the famous episode retold in the lesson, what happens when Rica dresses in European clothes?
choices: Parisians stare at him even more.
He is arrested for wearing a disguise.
Nobody notices him, until someone learns that he is Persian.
He decides to stay in Paris for ever.
questions.explanation: Dressed as a Persian, Rica is stared at everywhere; dressed as a European, he becomes invisible, until someone learns where he comes from and reacts with the famous astonished question about being Persian at all.

questions.stem: How does the book's satire mainly work?
choices: Through a foreign gaze that makes French customs look strange
Through direct attacks signed by the author
Through a narrator who comments on every letter
questions.explanation: Two Persians describe what the French take for granted, so French customs suddenly look as strange as distant ones. The reader laughs at the Persians, then sees himself.

questions.stem: What is the irony of Usbek's character?
choices: He hates Paris but never leaves it.
He condemns tyranny in his reflections but behaves as a despot in his seraglio.
He is a Frenchman pretending to be Persian.
He writes no letters at all.
questions.explanation: Usbek reflects wisely on justice and government in Paris, yet at home he orders the repression of his wives. The seraglio plot turns the satire back on him.

questions.stem: Which sentence presents the orientalism debate about the book fairly?
choices: Critics agree that the book is pure orientalist cliché.
Critics agree that the book has nothing to do with the East.
Said proved in 1721 that the book was orientalist.
Some critics see the seraglio as a cliché of the East; others see the Persians as a mirror held up to France.
questions.explanation: The lesson presents both readings, argued by serious critics, without taking a side. Said's Orientalism dates from 1978, not 1721.

questions.stem: Modernise: "Il fallut que je changeasse d'habit."
choices: Il a fallu que je change de vêtements.
Il fallait que je changeais de vêtements.
Il faudra que je change de vêtements.
Il a fallu que je changerais de vêtements.
questions.explanation: "Fallut" is the passé simple of falloir (modern: il a fallu), and "changeasse" an imperfect subjunctive, which modern French replaces with the present subjunctive: "que je change". Il faut que never takes the indicative or the conditional.

questions.stem: In "à peine fus-je entré dans un café qu'on me demanda mon avis", what is "fus-je entré"?
choices: A passé antérieur with inversion after à peine
questions.explanation: Fus entré is the passé antérieur of entrer (être in the passé simple + participle), inverted because à peine opens the clause. Modern French: "j'étais à peine entré dans un café qu'on m'a demandé …"

questions.stem: Complete: "Rica écrit en ___ à ses amis d'Ispahan."
questions.explanation: The language takes a small letter: le persan, écrire en persan. A capital is for the person (un Persan, une Persane); "persane" is the feminine adjective.

questions.stem: Modernise the subjunctive: "je doutai d'abord qu'elle fût de ta main" → "j'ai d'abord douté qu'elle ___ de ta main"
questions.explanation: "Fût" is the imperfect subjunctive of être (classical concordance after a past verb). Modern French uses the present subjunctive: "qu'elle soit de ta main".

questions.stem: Match each work with its year of publication.
questions.explanation: Montesquieu's Lettres persanes (1721) and De l'esprit des lois (1748), Rousseau's Julie (1761) and Laclos's Les Liaisons dangereuses (1782). 1789 is the Revolution, not one of these books.

questions.stem: Which features of classical prose should you recognise but not write in your own French? Select all that apply.
choices: the passé simple in a letter (je reçus, il partit)
the imperfect subjunctive after a past verb (qu'il fût)
the older pronoun position (je le veux voir)
the present subjunctive after il faut que (qu'il vienne)
the passé composé in a letter (j'ai reçu)
questions.explanation: The passé simple, the imperfect subjunctive and the older pronoun position are classical features, for recognition. The present subjunctive after il faut que and the passé composé in a letter are normal modern French.

questions.stem: Name the numbered places on the simplified map of the journey.

image.alt: A simplified map with four numbered red dots and no names: 1 in the north-west, 2 on the northern coast of a sea, 3 on the eastern coast of the same sea, 4 far to the south-east. A solid line joins 4 to 3, a dashed sea route joins 3 to 2, and a dotted line joins 2 to 1.

questions.explanation: The travellers leave Ispahan (4), cross Turkey to Smyrna (3), sail to Livorno (2) and go on to Paris (1). Venice and Bordeaux are not on the route.

questions.stem: What does "Il a démissionné par dépit." mean?
choices: He resigned in spite of everything.
questions.explanation: Le dépit is vexation after a disappointment or wounded pride: par dépit = out of pique. "In spite of" is en dépit de (B2), a different phrase.

questions.stem: Which feeling is the strongest?
questions.explanation: On the annoyance scale: l'agacement (mild) → l'irritation → l'exaspération (annoyance at its limit).

questions.stem: What does "Elle attendait les résultats avec appréhension." mean?
choices: She waited for the results with apprehension.
She waited for the results with relief.
She waited for the results in total despair.
questions.explanation: L'appréhension is worry felt before an event, milder than l'angoisse. It has nothing to do with understanding here.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je suis navré que vous ___ attendu si longtemps."
questions.explanation: Être navré que expresses a feeling and takes the subjunctive; the waiting came before, so the subjonctif passé: que vous ayez attendu.

questions.stem: Complete (same subject): "Je suis navré ___ cette triste nouvelle."
questions.explanation: With the same subject, a feeling takes de + infinitive: je suis navré d'apprendre. Que + subjunctive is for a different subject.

questions.stem: Which statement about "Le maire se réjouit de ce que les travaux ont commencé / aient commencé" is right?
choices: Both moods occur after de ce que, which is more formal than que.
Neither: se réjouir takes only an infinitive.
questions.explanation: After se réjouir de ce que, both moods are found: the indicative presents the cause as a fact, the subjunctive keeps the usual pattern of feelings. With plain que, the subjunctive is the rule.

questions.stem: What does "Le projet a été adopté, au grand dam de l'opposition." mean?
choices: The project was adopted, to the great relief of the opposition.
The project was adopted, much to the displeasure of the opposition.
The project was adopted with the opposition's great help.
The project was adopted after a great debate in the opposition.
questions.explanation: Au grand dam de means much to the displeasure (or harm) of. To the great relief of is au grand soulagement de.

questions.stem: Which sentence best suits a formal letter of regret?
choices: On est super déçus pour vous.
Nous sommes furieux que votre demande soit refusée.
Nous regrettons vivement que votre demande n'ait pu aboutir.
questions.explanation: A formal letter names the feeling precisely and moderately (regretter vivement) and uses formal syntax (n'ait pu, without pas). The others are informal or overstated.

questions.stem: What does "La nouvelle a suscité la consternation." mean?
choices: The news caused a mild irritation.
The news caused a lasting grudge.
questions.explanation: La consternation is shocked dismay at bad news. Joy, mild irritation (l'agacement) and a grudge (la rancune) are other feelings.

questions.stem: Which noun completes the usual fixed phrase "garder ___ à quelqu'un" (to hold a grudge against someone)?
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is garder rancune à quelqu'un. La rancœur is lasting resentment (garder une profonde rancœur envers quelqu'un), l'amertume bitterness, le dépit pique.

questions.stem: Complete: "Au grand ___ des familles, le pont a rouvert." (relief)
questions.explanation: Au grand soulagement de = to the great relief of. Soulagé (B1) is the adjective.

questions.stem: Match each feeling with its description.
choices: helplessness, not knowing what to do
bitterness that stays after a failure
questions.explanation: Worry before an event is l'appréhension, which isn't in the list.

questions.stem: Which words suit a formal letter of condolence or regret? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Profondément, vivement and nos sincères condoléances are precise and moderate. Furieux overstates, and super triste is informal.

questions.stem: Name the feelings in the numbered boxes of the scale.

image.alt: A scale of feelings from mild to strong, in three rows labelled Annoyance, Fear and Joy, with three empty boxes each. Marker 1: first box of Annoyance; 2: last box of Annoyance; 3: first box of Fear; 4: last box of Joy.

questions.explanation: Annoyance runs from l'agacement (mild) to l'exaspération; fear starts with l'appréhension; joy ends with l'allégresse. Bitterness and shocked dismay are not on these three scales.

questions.stem: Put the stages of Usbek and Rica's journey in order, from departure to arrival.
questions.explanation: They leave Ispahan in 1711, cross Turkey to Smyrna, sail to Livorno and reach Paris in 1712.

questions.stem: Put these feelings in order, from the mildest to the strongest.
questions.explanation: L'agacement is mild irritation; l'exaspération is annoyance pushed to its limit.

questions.stem: Which connector can answer the question? "Pourquoi le site ferme-t-il ? — ___ les commandes ont chuté."
questions.explanation: Only "parce que" answers "pourquoi ?": it gives the cause as new information. "Puisque" presents a cause the listener already accepts, "car" adds a justification after a statement, and "comme" puts background first, before a main clause; none of them can stand alone as an answer.

questions.stem: In which sentence does the writer suggest that the reason given is not the real one?
choices: La direction a supprimé la prime parce que les ventes stagnaient.
La direction a supprimé la prime sous prétexte que les ventes stagnaient.
Comme les ventes stagnaient, la direction a supprimé la prime.
La direction a supprimé la prime, car les ventes stagnaient.
questions.explanation: "Sous prétexte que" reports a reason someone gives and the writer doubts. "Parce que", "comme" and "car" all present the stagnating sales as the real cause.

questions.stem: What does this sentence say? "Les aides ne sont efficaces que dans la mesure où elles sont ciblées."
choices: The grants work because they have already been targeted.
The grants will be targeted once they work.
The grants work only as far as they are targeted.
The grants are targeted, but they don't work.
questions.explanation: With "ne … que", "dans la mesure où" can only mean extent: "only insofar as, only to the extent that". The grants are effective when, and as much as, they are targeted.

questions.stem: Which translation fits? "Dans la mesure où le contrat a déjà été signé, il est trop tard pour négocier."
choices: Although the contract has already been signed, there's still time to negotiate.
Until the contract has been signed, it's too late to negotiate.
