If the contract is ever signed, it will be too late to negotiate.
Since the contract has already been signed, it's too late to negotiate.
questions.explanation: Here "dans la mesure où" gives a cause, like "puisque": the contract is signed, so it is too late. The extent reading ("to the extent that the contract has been signed") makes no sense with a completed fact.

questions.stem: Complete so that the clause explains in what way the crisis is unprecedented: "Cette crise est inédite ___ elle touche tous les secteurs à la fois."
questions.explanation: "En ce sens que" + indicative (in that) explains in what way a claim is true. "Pour que" (purpose), "à moins que" (unless) and "jusqu'à ce que" (until) make no sense after "inédite".

questions.stem: Where would you most expect to read "Attendu que le locataire n'a pas réglé ses loyers, …"?
choices: In a text message to a friend
In a court ruling or another legal document
questions.explanation: "Attendu que" (whereas, given that) introduces the grounds of a legal or administrative decision. Recognise it in rulings, contracts and by-laws; don't use it in an essay.

questions.stem: Complete: "Sophie ne répond plus au téléphone. Si elle ne répond pas, ___ elle est partie en vacances."
questions.explanation: The explanatory "c'est que" goes from an observed fact (she isn't answering) to its likely explanation: "Si elle ne répond pas, c'est qu'elle est partie en vacances." After "si …", the other connectors don't fit the structure.

questions.stem: What does "tenir à" mean here? "Le succès de la région tient à la qualité de ses écoles."
questions.explanation: With a thing as its subject, "tenir à" means "to be due to, to come from". The B1 sense, "to be keen on", needs a person: "Je tiens à venir."

questions.stem: In standard French, complete: "Les recettes ont baissé ; il s'ensuit que le déficit ___ plus lourd que prévu."
questions.explanation: "Il s'ensuit que" states a logical consequence as a fact, so in an affirmative sentence it takes the indicative: "il s'ensuit que le déficit est plus lourd". "Soit" and "fût" are subjunctive forms; "être" is an infinitive.

questions.stem: What does "tant et si bien que" mean here? "Il a écrit à la mairie chaque semaine, tant et si bien qu'elle a fini par céder."
questions.explanation: "Tant et si bien que" + indicative gives a result that built up over time: he wrote every week, so much so that the town hall gave in. It is not a purpose ("pour que") or a condition.

questions.stem: In a literary text you read: "Plus de commandes, partant plus de travail." What does "partant" mean here?
questions.explanation: Literary "partant" means "hence, therefore" (= de là). It is for recognition only. It is not the present participle of "partir" here.

questions.stem: Complete: "Le gouvernement ___ la hausse du chômage à la crise mondiale."
questions.explanation: "Imputer qqch à qqch" means to attribute (usually blame): the government blames the rise in unemployment on the global crisis. "Induire" (to cause) takes no "à" here, "aboutir à" means to end in, and "se traduire par" needs "par".

questions.stem: Which sentence uses "se traduire par" correctly?
choices: La fermeture de l'usine s'est traduite par deux cents licenciements.
La fermeture de l'usine s'est traduite à deux cents licenciements.
La fermeture de l'usine a traduit par deux cents licenciements.
Deux cents licenciements se sont traduits la fermeture de l'usine.
questions.explanation: "Se traduire par" (to show up as, to result in) is pronominal and takes "par": the closure resulted in two hundred redundancies. The participle agrees with "la fermeture": "s'est traduite".

questions.stem: In paragraph 3 of the reading, why do some jobs that used to count as industrial now count as services?
choices: The factories were turned into offices.
Firms handed cleaning, catering and logistics to outside providers.
Workers retrained for jobs in tourism.
The Insee changed its definition of industry in 2025.
questions.explanation: The paragraph says firms entrusted cleaning, catering and logistics to "prestataires extérieurs", "tant et si bien que" those jobs are now counted in services: part of deindustrialisation is statistical.

questions.stem: In paragraph 5 of the reading, which figures does the article give from the Insee?
choices: A public deficit of 115.6 % of GDP and debt of 5.1 % of GDP in 2025
Unemployment of 5.1 % and debt of 115.6 % of GDP in 2024
A public deficit of 5.1 % of GDP in 2025 and public debt of 115.6 % of GDP at the end of 2025
Growth of 5.1 % and a deficit of 115.6 billion euros in 2025
questions.explanation: The article says: "le déficit public a atteint 5,1 % du PIB en 2025, et la dette publique 115,6 % du PIB à la fin de la même année" (Insee figures published in March 2026).

questions.stem: Listen to the news item. What reason does the management give for its decision?

audio.text: Flash économie. Le fabricant de vélos électriques Vélomax va délocaliser sa production en Europe de l'Est. La direction impute cette décision à la hausse des coûts de l'énergie. Les syndicats, eux, dénoncent un prétexte et redoutent plus de cent licenciements.

questions.explanation: The management "impute cette décision à la hausse des coûts de l'énergie": it attributes the decision to rising energy costs. The unions call that a pretext.

questions.stem: Listen to two economists. What does the second one think the fall in unemployment is mainly due to?

audio.text: — Si le chômage baisse, c'est que l'économie va mieux. — Pas forcément. La baisse tient surtout aux départs à la retraite : il y a tout simplement moins d'actifs.

choices: Retirements: there are fewer people of working age.
questions.explanation: The first speaker infers "c'est que l'économie va mieux". The second disagrees: "La baisse tient surtout aux départs à la retraite", so there are fewer working-age people. "Tenir à" = to be due to.

questions.stem: Complete with the connector meaning "in that": "La mesure est injuste, ___ elle pèse surtout sur les plus modestes."
questions.explanation: "En ce sens qu'elle pèse …" explains in what way the measure is unfair (in that). "Dans le sens où", common in speech, and the formal "en cela que" are also accepted; "en ce sens que" is the careful written form. Note the elision: "qu'elle".

questions.stem: Complete with the present of "induire": "La hausse des taux ___ une baisse de l'investissement."
questions.explanation: "Induire" is conjugated like "conduire": il induit, nous induisons, ils induisent; participle "induit".

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "If the factory is closing, it's because orders have collapsed."
questions.explanation: "Si l'usine ferme, c'est parce que les commandes se sont effondrées." "Si … c'est parce que" puts a known cause in focus.

questions.stem: In an affirmative sentence in standard French, which of these are followed by a clause in the indicative? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Dans la mesure où" (indicative or conditionnel), "en ce sens que", "il s'ensuit que" and "tant et si bien que" introduce facts and take the indicative. "Non que" (a rejected cause) and "pour que" (purpose) take the subjunctive.

questions.stem: Which connector goes in each numbered box?

image.alt: A chart of six boxes, each describing how a connector presents a cause, with the connector's place left blank and numbered.

questions.explanation: 1 puisque (already known or accepted), 2 parce que (new information, answers "why?"), 3 comme (first, as background), 4 car (a justification added afterwards), 5 sous prétexte que (a claim the writer doubts), 6 à force de (repetition). "Il s'ensuit que" and "tant et si bien que" introduce consequences, not causes.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses "tant s'en faut" correctly?
choices: Les objectifs sont largement atteints, tant s'en faut.
Les objectifs ne sont pas atteints, tant s'en faut.
Tant s'en faut, les objectifs sont dépassés.
Les objectifs sont atteints, et tant s'en faut.
questions.explanation: "Tant s'en faut" (far from it) reinforces a denial and usually closes the sentence: the targets are not met, far from it. After a positive statement it contradicts it.

questions.stem: In standard French, complete: "Certes, la taxe est impopulaire ; il reste qu'elle ___ les émissions."
questions.explanation: "Il reste que" (the fact remains that) states a fact, so it takes the indicative: "elle réduit". "Réduise" is the present subjunctive and "réduisît" the literary imperfect subjunctive.

questions.stem: What does "au demeurant" add here? "Cette réforme, au demeurant peu coûteuse, a été adoptée sans débat."
choices: which will only cost little later
which, despite everything, costs a lot
which costs little only at first
which, for that matter, costs little
questions.explanation: "Au demeurant" (formal) adds a point "for that matter": the reform was adopted without debate, and it costs little, too.

questions.stem: What does "cela dit" do in this pair of sentences? "Le projet est séduisant. Cela dit, son financement reste flou."
choices: It turns from a positive point to a reservation.
It gives the cause of the first sentence.
It repeats the first sentence in other words.
questions.explanation: "Cela dit" (that said) grants what has just been said and turns to a reservation. "Ceci dit" is also current; "cela dit" is the safer choice in an exam.

questions.stem: Complete with the correct concessive inversion: "___, la transition reste indispensable."
questions.explanation: "La transition" is feminine, so the adjective is "coûteuse" and the pronoun that anticipates it is "elle"; the verb is the subjunctive "soit". "Est-elle" is the indicative, which this inversion doesn't use.

questions.stem: Which sentence means the same as "Si ambitieux soit-il, ce plan reste flou"?
choices: Puisqu'il est si ambitieux, ce plan reste flou.
S'il est ambitieux, ce plan restera flou.
Si ambitieux qu'il soit, ce plan reste flou.
Ce plan est si ambitieux qu'il reste flou.
questions.explanation: "Si ambitieux soit-il" is the formal inversion of "si ambitieux qu'il soit" (however ambitious it may be). The other sentences give a cause, a condition or a consequence.

questions.stem: What does "pour autant que je sache" mean?
questions.explanation: "Pour autant que" + subjunctive limits a claim: "pour autant que je sache" = as far as I know. "Que je sache" (lesson 05) says the same.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il a perdu l'élection ; il ne renonce pas ___ à son projet."
questions.explanation: "Pour autant" (B2), an adverb with no clause, means "for all that": he lost, but he isn't giving up for all that. "Pour autant que" needs a clause in the subjunctive.

questions.stem: What does this sentence mean? "Tout en reconnaissant l'urgence climatique, le ministre refuse toute taxe nouvelle."
choices: Because he acknowledges the climate emergency, the minister rejects any new tax.
Although he acknowledges the climate emergency, the minister rejects any new tax.
Until he acknowledges the climate emergency, the minister will reject any new tax.
As soon as he acknowledged the climate emergency, the minister accepted a new tax.
questions.explanation: When the two actions don't sit well together, "tout en" + gérondif becomes a concession: while, although. Acknowledging an emergency and refusing a measure clash.

questions.stem: Which statement about "par contre" is accurate?
choices: It is a mistake in every register.
It is only used in Québec.
It is common and good authors use it, but "en revanche" is the safer choice in a formal essay.
The Académie française recommends it over "en revanche".
questions.explanation: Littré condemned "par contre", Gide defended it, and today the Académie says it can't be called a mistake, though it advises another adverb when one fits. Both are current; "en revanche" is the safe exam choice.

questions.stem: Which expression is the most formal way to say "far from it"?
questions.explanation: "Tant s'en faut" (like "loin s'en faut") is formal. "Loin de là" is neutral and right in most registers, which is why it isn't the most formal; "pas du tout" is everyday; "tu parles" is informal and ironic.

questions.stem: In paragraph 4 of the reading, on what condition does the economist support a higher carbon tax?
choices: If its revenue is given back to low-income households
If it only applies to large companies
questions.explanation: He supports it "pour autant que ses recettes soient reversées aux ménages modestes": provided that its revenue goes back to low-income households. "Pour autant que" + subjunctive expresses this restriction.

questions.stem: In paragraph 2 of the reading, what does the figure from the IPCC's 2023 synthesis report describe?
choices: Global surface temperature in 2011–2020 was 1.1 °C above that of 1850–1900.
Global temperature will rise by 1.1 °C by 2050.
Carbon neutrality was reached in 2020 in 1.1 % of countries.
questions.explanation: The text says global surface temperature "a dépassé de 1,1 °C, sur la période 2011-2020, celle de la période 1850-1900". The other choices change what was measured or when.

questions.stem: Listen to the exchange. What does the second speaker think of sobriety?

audio.text: — Certes, la sobriété a un coût social. Il n'en demeure pas moins qu'elle est la seule voie rapide. — Rapide, peut-être. Juste, loin s'en faut.

choices: It is both quick and fair.
It is neither quick nor fair.
It may be quick, but it is far from fair.
It is fair, but far too slow.
questions.explanation: The first speaker concedes a social cost and then holds his point ("il n'en demeure pas moins que"). The second grants "rapide, peut-être" but denies fairness: "Juste, loin s'en faut" (fair? far from it).

questions.stem: Listen to the news item. What is the brand accused of?

audio.text: L'association Terre vivante accuse la marque Nordik d'écoblanchiment : la marque vante un jean « responsable » tout en multipliant les collections.

choices: Polluting a river near its factory
Refusing to pay the carbon tax
Hiding its use of plastic packaging
Presenting itself as green while selling ever more clothes
questions.explanation: The association accuses the brand of "écoblanchiment" (greenwashing): it praises a "responsible" pair of jeans "tout en multipliant les collections", while launching ever more collections.

questions.stem: Complete the formal concessive inversion with one word: "Si ambitieuse ___-elle, cette loi ne suffira pas."
questions.explanation: "Si ambitieuse soit-elle": si + adjective + the subjunctive "soit" + the inverted pronoun. It means "however ambitious it may be".

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "Le coût est élevé ; il ___ que la mesure est utile." (the fact remains that)
questions.explanation: "Il reste que" + indicative: the fact remains that. Its more formal relative is "il n'en demeure pas moins que".

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "Admittedly, this plan is costly; it is still true that it is necessary."
questions.explanation: "Certes, ce plan est coûteux ; il n'en demeure pas moins qu'il est nécessaire." Grant with "certes", then hold your point with "il n'en demeure pas moins que" + indicative.

questions.stem: Match each phrase with its meaning.
questions.explanation: "Tant s'en faut" reinforces a denial; "au demeurant" adds a point; "cela dit" turns to a reservation; "pour autant que" + subjunctive restricts; "il reste que" + indicative keeps a point standing. "So much so that" is "tant et si bien que" (lesson 09).

questions.stem: Which of these are followed by a clause in the subjunctive? Select all that apply.
choices: il n'en demeure pas moins que
questions.explanation: "Pour autant que", "bien que" and "quoique" take the subjunctive. "Il reste que" and "il n'en demeure pas moins que" state a fact (indicative), and so does "sous prétexte que" (lesson 09).

questions.stem: "Le maire a présenté l'urbaniste aux habitants. Ce dernier a répondu à leurs questions." Who answered the questions?
choices: The mayor and the planner together
questions.explanation: "Ce dernier" refers to the last-named noun of the same gender and number. "Les habitants" is plural, so the last masculine singular noun is "l'urbaniste". The residents are "leurs".

questions.stem: "La ministre a reçu la maire de Lyon et son adjointe. Cette dernière a pris la parole." Who spoke?
questions.explanation: "Cette dernière" points to the last-named feminine singular noun: "son adjointe".

questions.stem: Complete: "Deux projets s'opposent : la piétonnisation et le tramway. ___ est moins chère, ___ est plus rapide."
questions.explanation: "Le premier … le second" means "the former … the latter", and each agrees with its noun: "la piétonnisation" (feminine, named first) → "la première"; "le tramway" (masculine, named second) → "le second".

questions.stem: Complete with a lexical anaphora: "Le conseil municipal a voté la végétalisation des cours d'école. ___ a été saluée par les parents."
questions.explanation: A nominalisation sums up the previous sentence: "a voté …" → "cette décision", feminine like "saluée". "Ce dernier" and "celui-ci" are masculine and would point to "le conseil municipal"; "ledit vote" is legal style and masculine.

questions.stem: Complete: "Le plan poursuit deux objectifs, ___ réduire la place de la voiture et créer des espaces verts."
questions.explanation: "À savoir" (namely) spells out what has just been announced: the two goals. "Somme toute" and "au bout du compte" conclude; "ledit" is a legal adjective.

questions.stem: Which kind of thematic progression is this? "La commune a racheté une friche. Cette friche accueillera un quartier mixte. Ce quartier associera logements et bureaux."
choices: Constant: every sentence has the same theme.
Linear: the new element of each sentence becomes the theme of the next.
Split: a general theme is divided into parts.
None: the themes jump without any link.
questions.explanation: "Une friche" (new in sentence 1) becomes the theme of sentence 2; "un quartier mixte" (new in sentence 2) becomes the theme of sentence 3. That is linear progression.

questions.stem: Which kind of thematic progression is this? "Saint-Aurèle a grandi par sa périphérie. Elle a perdu des terres agricoles. Elle cherche aujourd'hui à se densifier."
choices: Linear: the new element of each sentence becomes the theme of the next.
Split: a general theme is divided into parts.
Constant: every sentence has the same theme.
None: the themes jump without any link.
questions.explanation: All three sentences are about the town ("Saint-Aurèle … Elle … Elle"): a constant theme.

questions.stem: What is the job of a topic sentence?
choices: It sums up the whole text in its last line.
It gives a quotation to open the essay.
It links two sentences with a connector of cause.
It states the paragraph's one idea, usually at the start.
questions.explanation: At C1 a paragraph develops one idea, announced by its topic sentence; the rest explains, illustrates and limits it. In a synthesis, the topic sentences alone should show your plan.

questions.stem: Which sentence is punctuated as is usual in France?
choices: Le constat est simple : la ville s'étale.
Le constat est simple: la ville s'étale.
Le constat est simple : la ville s'étale .
Le constat est simple, : la ville s'étale.
questions.explanation: In France a space comes before the colon (and before ; ? !), but not before a full stop, and a colon doesn't follow a comma.

questions.stem: In a council decision you read: "La commune a acquis la parcelle B12 ; ___ parcelle sera aménagée en jardin." Which form fits?
questions.explanation: "Ledit" agrees like an article + adjective: "ladite parcelle" (feminine singular). "Lesdites" is plural, and "audit" is "à + ledit". It is legal style: in an essay, write "cette parcelle".

questions.stem: What does "somme toute" mean here? "Somme toute, le projet a tenu ses promesses."
questions.explanation: "Somme toute" (all in all, all things considered) sums up, often with a slightly concessive tone. "Moreover" is "en outre", "namely" is "à savoir".

questions.stem: In paragraph 3 of the reading, what does "Cette dernière" refer to?
questions.explanation: "Cette dernière" refers to the last-named feminine singular noun before it: "la mixité fonctionnelle" (the second principle). "La ville du quart d'heure" comes after it.

questions.stem: In paragraph 4 of the reading, what did residents of the nearby deprived neighbourhood fear?
choices: Gentrification: higher rents that would push them further out
The pedestrianisation of the main street
The loss of the town's farmland
A new heat island in the centre
questions.explanation: At the consultation they "ont dit craindre la gentrification": the rise in rents that the new district would bring might push them further away. The town answered by setting aside a third of the homes as social housing. It was the shopkeepers who feared pedestrianisation.

questions.stem: Listen to the lecture extract. Where is a paragraph's idea announced?

audio.text: Dans un texte bien construit, chaque paragraphe développe une seule idée. Celle-ci est annoncée dès la première phrase ; les phrases suivantes l'expliquent, l'illustrent et la nuancent.

choices: In the title of the text
questions.explanation: The lecturer says the idea "est annoncée dès la première phrase": that first sentence is the topic sentence, and the following ones explain, illustrate and qualify it.

questions.stem: Listen to the local radio item. Who can give their opinion until 30 June?

audio.text: Réunion de concertation ce soir à la mairie : le projet de requalification des anciens abattoirs sera présenté aux habitants. Ces derniers pourront donner leur avis jusqu'au trente juin.

choices: The members of the town council
questions.explanation: "Ces derniers pourront donner leur avis": "ces derniers" refers to the last-named masculine plural noun, "les habitants".

questions.stem: Complete with the words meaning "the latter": "La mairie a consulté l'architecte et la paysagiste ; ___ a proposé un grand parc."
questions.explanation: "Cette dernière" points to the last-named feminine singular noun, "la paysagiste". "Celle-ci" and, with exactly two people, "la seconde" are also right.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "The mayor met the town planner; the latter presented his plan."
questions.explanation: "Le maire a reçu l'urbaniste ; ce dernier a présenté son plan." "Ce dernier" refers to the last-named man, the planner.

questions.stem: Match each connector with what it does.
questions.explanation: "À savoir" (namely) spells out; "somme toute" (all in all) concludes; "en outre" (B1, moreover) adds; "c'est-à-dire" (that is) reformulates.

questions.stem: Which of these refer back to something already named in the text? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Ce dernier", "ledit", a summing-up noun like "cette décision" and "le second" are anaphora: they point back. "À savoir" and "somme toute" are connectors: they spell out and conclude.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this town plan.

image.alt: A simplified town plan with five numbered markers: on the old centre, on the pedestrian street crossing it, on empty industrial sheds by the river, on the ring of detached houses, and on a dashed arrow pointing out into the fields.

questions.explanation: 1 le centre ancien (dense old centre), 2 la rue piétonnière (the street with no cars), 3 la friche (abandoned industrial sheds), 4 le quartier pavillonnaire (the ring of detached houses), 5 l'étalement urbain (the town spreading into the fields). A "ville nouvelle" is a whole planned town, and an "îlot de chaleur" is a temperature effect, not something drawn here.

questions.stem: What does this sentence presuppose? "Le ministre a cessé de contredire le Premier ministre."
choices: The minister has never contradicted the Prime Minister.
The minister will contradict the Prime Minister again.
The Prime Minister used to contradict the minister.
The minister used to contradict the Prime Minister.
questions.explanation: "Cesser de" presupposes that the action happened before. The presupposition survives negation: "Il n'a pas cessé de le contredire" still takes it for granted.

questions.stem: Which sentence keeps the presupposition of "Paul a encore raté son train" (he has missed it before)?
choices: Paul a-t-il encore raté son train ?
Paul n'a jamais raté de train.
Paul a raté son train pour la première fois.
questions.explanation: A presupposition survives when a sentence becomes a question: "A-t-il encore raté son train ?" still takes it for granted that he has missed it before. The other sentences deny it or say nothing about it.

questions.stem: What does "même" presuppose here? "Même la porte-parole a reconnu l'erreur."
choices: She was the first to point out the error.
She was among the people least expected to admit it.
questions.explanation: "Même" presupposes that the person named was the least likely: others admitted the error, and so, surprisingly, did she.

questions.stem: At one in the morning, a host says to his guests: "Il est déjà une heure …" What is he most likely implying?
choices: It's time for them to leave.
He wants them to stay longer.
questions.explanation: This is an implication (sous-entendu): the words only give the time, and the situation does the rest. The host can always deny it ("I was just giving the time").

questions.stem: Which statement about presupposition and implication is true?
choices: An implication survives negation; a presupposition depends on the context.
Both are stated explicitly in the sentence.
Neither can ever be denied by the speaker.
A presupposition survives negation; an implication depends on the context and can be denied.
questions.explanation: A presupposition is carried by the sentence itself (it survives negation and questions). An implication comes from the words plus the situation, so the speaker can deny meaning it.

questions.stem: In a meeting, after you make a suggestion, a colleague answers: "Ce n'est pas faux." What does this most often signal?
choices: A reserved agreement: you have a point, but …
That your suggestion is a lie
questions.explanation: "Ce n'est pas faux" is litotes: saying less to mean more. It usually signals a reserved agreement, though in some contexts it is warm agreement, so listen to the tone. It never means "it's false".

questions.stem: After a three-hour delay, a passenger says: "Bravo, quelle ponctualité !" What is this?
choices: Litotes: saying less to mean more
Antiphrasis: saying the opposite of what one means
questions.explanation: The praise clashes with the facts (a three-hour delay), so it means the opposite: antiphrasis, the simplest form of irony.

questions.stem: What does this rhetorical question mean? "Qui pourrait s'opposer à plus de sécurité ?"
choices: The speaker wants to know who opposes security.
The speaker isn't sure about security.
questions.explanation: A rhetorical question is a statement in question form: it expects no answer and means "nobody could".

questions.stem: A crowd has gathered in the street. Which word gives it the most negative connotation?
questions.explanation: "Un attroupement" suggests a disorderly, possibly threatening crowd. "Un rassemblement" is neutral, and "une réunion" and "une assemblée" suggest something organised.

questions.stem: What does a stranger mean by "Vous auriez l'heure ?"
choices: Do you have time to talk?
Would you have had the time?
questions.explanation: This is politeness through indirectness: the conditional softens a plain request for the time.

questions.stem: Why is this headline ambiguous? "Le maire critique les habitants sans masque."
choices: "Critique" can be a noun or a verb.
"Sans masque" can describe either the mayor or the residents.
"Le maire" can mean the mother or the sea.
"Les habitants" can be singular or plural.
questions.explanation: Is the mayor criticising without wearing a mask, or criticising the residents who don't wear one? Rewritten clearly: "Le maire critique les habitants qui ne portent pas de masque."

questions.stem: Which sentence reports what a document implies, neutrally, as a synthesis requires?
choices: L'auteur a raison de dire que la réforme a échoué.
L'auteur dit clairement que la réforme a échoué.
L'auteur laisse entendre que la réforme a échoué.
Je pense que l'auteur insinue, à tort, que la réforme a échoué.
questions.explanation: "Laisser entendre que" reports an implication without judging it. "A raison" and "je pense … à tort" add an opinion, and "dit clairement" turns an implicit meaning into an explicit one.

questions.stem: In paragraph 2 of the column, why does the writer add that it is "toujours rassurant de le savoir"?
choices: To reassure readers that the government hides nothing
To thank the minister for his transparency
To accuse the journalists of inventing the story
To mock the minister for denying an accusation nobody had made
questions.explanation: Nobody had accused the minister of hiding anything, so his "rien à cacher" suggests the opposite. "Toujours rassurant" is ironic: it takes his denial literally to underline it.

questions.stem: In paragraph 1 of the column, what does "Mais qui pourrait reprocher à un ministre d'avoir trop simplifié ?" really mean?
choices: The plan made things more complicated, not simpler.
The minister deserves criticism for his courage.
questions.explanation: The forms doubled and the delays grew: the "simplification" complicated things. The rhetorical question pretends to defend the minister and says the opposite: antiphrasis.

questions.stem: Listen to the press conference. What do the minister's last words, "Pour l'instant", suggest?

audio.text: — Monsieur le ministre, allez-vous démissionner ? — Je n'ai jamais songé à quitter mes fonctions. Pour l'instant.

choices: That he is about to be promoted
questions.explanation: He says he has never thought of leaving office, then adds "pour l'instant" (for now). The addition implies that he might, which he could still deny.

questions.stem: Listen to two readers disagreeing. What does the second one think of the column?

audio.text: — Tu as lu la chronique sur le ministre ? C'est un portrait plutôt flatteur. — Flatteur ? Tu plaisantes : c'est du second degré du début à la fin !

choices: It is a flattering portrait of the minister.
It is a news report with no opinion.
It is ironic from start to finish, not flattering.
It is unclear and full of mistakes.
questions.explanation: The first reader takes it literally ("un portrait flatteur"). The second says it is "du second degré du début à la fin": not meant literally, ironic throughout.

questions.stem: Complete with the noun (one word) for what a sentence takes for granted: "Votre question repose sur un ___ discutable."
questions.explanation: "Le présupposé" is what a sentence takes for granted. The verb is "présupposer": "Votre question présuppose que nous avons échoué."

questions.stem: Match each notion with its example.
choices: Il a cessé de fumer. (He used to smoke.)
Ce n'est pas mal du tout. (It's very good.)
un régime, rather than un gouvernement
questions.explanation: Each example shows its notion. "Ver, verre, vert, vers" are homophones, the stuff of puns (honors lesson 12h1).

questions.stem: Which of these words or phrases trigger a presupposition? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Cesser de" (it happened before), "encore" (it happened already), "regretter que" (the fact is true) and "même" (the least expected) trigger presuppositions. "Peut-être" and "probablement" express degrees of certainty (lesson 08).

questions.stem: Name the three numbered levels of meaning.

image.alt: An iceberg: a sentence in a box above the water (marker 1), two sentences just below the surface (marker 2), and a question deep below, marked 'selon le contexte' (marker 3).

questions.explanation: 1 ce qui est dit: the sentence itself. 2 le présupposé: he made a mistake and was slow to admit it ("enfin"); it survives negation. 3 le sous-entendu: he can't be trusted, which depends on the context and can be denied.

questions.stem: Rewrite the ambiguous headline without ambiguity: put the words in order.
questions.explanation: "Sans apporter de preuve, le ministre attaque les journalistes." Fronting "sans apporter de preuve" makes clear that it is the minister who has no proof.

questions.stem: Which word is NOT pronounced like the others?
questions.explanation: "Le verre", "vert" and "le vers" are all pronounced [vɛʁ], like "le ver" (worm). "La vertu" (virtue) has two syllables.

questions.stem: Explain the joke: "Pourquoi le poète ne croque-t-il jamais de pommes ? — Parce qu'il préfère les vers."
choices: "Les vers" can be the worms in apples or the lines of poetry he writes.
Poets are known to dislike fruit.
"Croquer" can also mean to draw a sketch.
questions.explanation: The pun rests on two homophones: "le ver" (worm, which you find in apples) and "le vers" (line of poetry). The question makes you expect an answer about apples; the answer is about the poet's job.

questions.stem: Why is this headline a play on words? "Inondations : le maire se jette à l'eau."
choices: "Le maire" sounds like "la mer", the sea.
"Se jeter à l'eau" means "to take the plunge", and in a flood story it is also literal.
The mayor has really fallen into the river.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression "se jeter à l'eau" (to take the plunge, decide to act) is taken literally in a story about floods. Both meanings are present at once.

questions.stem: Which phrase is a spoonerism (contrepèterie) of "le bout du pain"?
questions.explanation: A contrepèterie swaps sounds between two words: "b" and "p" change places, so "le bout du pain" becomes "le pou du bain". Swapping whole words ("le pain du bout") is not a spoonerism.

questions.stem: What does a contrepèterie swap?
choices: Two whole words in a sentence
questions.explanation: It works on sounds, not spelling: "le pot de lait" becomes "le lot de paix" because "lait" and "paix" end in the same vowel, whatever their letters.

questions.stem: What is "la chute" of a joke?
choices: The punchline that changes the meaning of what came before
The moment the audience stops laughing
The first line that sets up the joke
questions.explanation: "La chute" (literally "the fall") is the punchline: the last turn that reveals the second meaning.

questions.stem: What does this sentence mean? "Interrogé sur son échec, il s'en est tiré par une boutade."
choices: Asked about his failure, he lost his temper.
Asked about his failure, he got out of it with a quip.
Asked about his failure, he gave a long explanation.
Asked about his failure, he refused to answer.
questions.explanation: "Une boutade" is a quick, witty remark, often one that sidesteps a serious question.

questions.stem: Which statement about Raymond Devos is accurate?
choices: He founded Le Canard enchaîné in 1915.
He was a press cartoonist known for caricatures of presidents.
He was born in Belgium to French parents and was known for wordplay and the absurd.
He hosted the radio programme Le Tribunal des flagrants délires.
questions.explanation: Devos (1922–2006) was born in Mouscron, Belgium, to French parents, and built monologues on words taken literally and pushed into the absurd. Le Tribunal des flagrants délires is linked to Pierre Desproges.

questions.stem: When did Le Canard enchaîné publish its first issue?
choices: In 1915, during the First World War
questions.explanation: The first issue appeared on 10 September 1915. The paper stopped after five issues and came back on 5 July 1916; it still appears every Wednesday.

questions.stem: What does this sentence mean? "Le dessinateur tourne en dérision les promesses électorales."
choices: The cartoonist turns election promises into a campaign.
questions.explanation: "Tourner qqch en dérision" = to make something look ridiculous. "La dérision" is mockery; "l'autodérision" is mocking yourself.

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "Elle parle de ses propres échecs avec beaucoup d'___." (self-mockery)
questions.explanation: "L'autodérision" (feminine) is mocking yourself, a much-valued trait in French public life.

questions.stem: Match each word with its meaning.
choices: a pun on words that sound alike
humour that follows a logic into nonsense
questions.explanation: "Un dessin animé" is an animated film: don't confuse it with "la caricature" or "le dessin de presse".

questions.stem: Each picture's name is pronounced [vɛʁ]. Which word goes with each?

image.alt: Four pictures in a row, each with a numbered marker: a worm coming out of an apple, a glass of water, a green leaf, and a page with lines of a poem.

questions.explanation: 1 le ver (worm), 2 le verre (glass), 3 vert (green), 4 le vers (line of poetry). Four spellings, one sound: the raw material of the calembour.

questions.stem: Which of these are pronounced exactly like "sans" [sɑ̃]? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Cent", "le sang" and "il sent" are all pronounced [sɑ̃]. "Le sens" is usually pronounced with a final s, [sɑ̃s], and "cinq" is [sɛ̃k].

questions.stem: What is ethos?
choices: The emotions the speaker stirs in the audience
The speaker's credibility and character as the audience sees them
The arguments and figures in the speech
The closing appeal of a speech
questions.explanation: Ethos is the proof that comes from the speaker; pathos comes from the audience's emotions, logos from the reasoning.

questions.stem: A speaker sets out figures, compares two policies and answers the main objection. Which proof is she relying on?
questions.explanation: Facts, figures, comparison and refutation are reasoning: logos. The exordium is a part of a speech, not a proof.

questions.stem: In the classical model, which part of a speech usually carries the strongest emotion?
questions.explanation: The peroration closes the speech, sums up and appeals to the audience: it is where pathos is usually strongest.

questions.stem: What does "un réquisitoire contre la réforme" mean in a newspaper?
choices: a scathing attack on the reform
a plea in favour of the reform
an official summary of the reform
questions.explanation: In court "un réquisitoire" is the prosecutor's speech; by extension, a fierce attack. Its opposite is "un plaidoyer", a plea for someone or something.

questions.stem: What does "Le député est monté à la tribune" mean?
choices: The deputy wrote an opinion piece.
The deputy went up to the rostrum to speak.
The deputy sat down in the public gallery.
The deputy climbed onto the roof.
questions.explanation: "Monter à la tribune" = to go up to the rostrum and take the floor in parliament. "Une tribune" in a newspaper is an opinion piece.

questions.stem: What was Victor Hugo's speech of 9 July 1849 about?
choices: Poverty, which he argued could be destroyed
questions.explanation: In the Assemblée législative, during a debate on public assistance, Hugo argued that poverty could not only be relieved but destroyed, with concrete descriptions of how the poorest Parisians lived.

questions.stem: What was the occasion of André Malraux's speech of 19 December 1964?
choices: The abolition of the death penalty
The opening of a new Assemblée nationale
The funeral of General de Gaulle
The transfer of Jean Moulin's ashes to the Panthéon
questions.explanation: Malraux, then minister of cultural affairs, spoke when Jean Moulin's presumed ashes were carried into the Panthéon, in de Gaulle's presence.

questions.stem: Which statement about Simone Veil's speech of 26 November 1974 is accurate?
choices: As minister of health, she presented the bill on the voluntary termination of pregnancy.
As minister of justice, she presented the bill abolishing the death penalty.
She gave it at the Panthéon in honour of a Resistance hero.
The law was adopted that night and made permanent at once.
questions.explanation: Veil, minister of health, presented the IVG bill. The Assemblée voted for it on 29 November 1974; the law of 17 January 1975 was passed for five years and made permanent by a law of 31 December 1979.

questions.stem: What did the law of 9 October 1981 do?
choices: It abolished the death penalty in France.
It gave women the right to vote.
questions.explanation: Robert Badinter, minister of justice, presented the bill on 17 September 1981; the Assemblée voted for it the next day, and the law of 9 October 1981 abolished the death penalty.

questions.stem: Which form is correct?
questions.explanation: "Haranguer" has an aspirated h, so "je" doesn't elide: "je harangue", "que je harangue". The auxiliary still elides: "j'ai harangué".

questions.stem: Complete with the past participle of "émouvoir": "Son témoignage a ___ toute la salle."
questions.explanation: "Émouvoir" is irregular: j'émeus, nous émouvons, ils émeuvent; participle "ému".

questions.stem: Put the five parts of a classical speech in the order given in this lesson.
questions.explanation: The opening wins attention (exorde), the facts are set out (narration), the arguments for are given (confirmation), the objections are answered (réfutation), and the speech closes with an appeal (péroraison).

questions.stem: Match each speech with its speaker.
questions.explanation: Hugo spoke in the Assemblée législative, Malraux at the Panthéon, Veil and Badinter in the Assemblée nationale. Raymond Devos was a humorist (lesson 12h1).

questions.stem: Type the French word, with its article, for the opening part of a classical speech.
questions.explanation: "L'exorde" is masculine (un exorde): the opening that wins attention and builds ethos.

questions.stem: Which of these are appeals to pathos? Select all that apply.
choices: Reminding the audience of the speaker's own experience
Refuting an objection point by point
questions.explanation: Suffering, pride and fear are emotions: pathos. Statistics and refutation are logos; the speaker's own experience builds ethos.

questions.stem: What does "Si tu crois qu'il va s'excuser, tu te mets le doigt dans l'œil" mean?
choices: If you think he's going to apologise, you're turning a blind eye.
If you think he's going to apologise, you're poking your nose in.
If you think he's going to apologise, you're completely wrong.
If you think he's going to apologise, you'll get hurt.
questions.explanation: Se mettre le doigt dans l'œil (informal) means to be completely wrong. It has nothing to do with eyes or with being hurt; the image is figurative.

questions.stem: Complete with the idiom as it is used in France: "Après trois défaites, l'équipe a ___."
questions.explanation: The idiom is jeter l'éponge (to throw in the towel). It is frozen: the determiner (l') and the verb (jeter) can't change, and in France the English towel doesn't replace the French sponge.

questions.stem: Which English idiom matches "Appelons un chat un chat"?
choices: Let's let the cat out of the bag.
Let's put the cat among the pigeons.
Let's call a spade a spade.
questions.explanation: Appeler un chat un chat means to speak plainly: to call a spade a spade. The French picture is a cat, the English one a spade. Letting the cat out of the bag is vendre la mèche.

questions.stem: Complete in standard French: "Elle s'est ___ le doigt dans l'œil."
questions.explanation: In se mettre le doigt dans l'œil, se is indirect and the direct object (le doigt) comes after the verb, so the participle doesn't agree: elle s'est mis le doigt dans l'œil, like elle s'est lavé les mains.

questions.stem: Which idiom is the most suitable in a formal essay on public policy?
choices: se mettre le doigt dans l'œil
mettre la charrue avant les bœufs
casser du sucre sur le dos de quelqu'un
questions.explanation: Mettre la charrue avant les bœufs is neutral and common in the press, so one well-placed use can work in an essay. The lesson labels the other three as informal: in an essay, use se tromper, critiquer or exagérer instead.

questions.stem: Complete: "Nous voulons tous mettre ___ grain de sel."
questions.explanation: The possessive in mettre son grain de sel follows the subject: je mets mon grain de sel, nous mettons notre grain de sel. Son only fits il, elle, on or chacun.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I couldn't remember"?
choices: J'ai eu un trou de mémoire.
questions.explanation: Un trou de mémoire is a memory blank. Faire chou blanc means to get no result (English "draw a blank" in that sense only), vendre la mèche is to give a secret away, and prendre la mouche is to take offence.

questions.stem: Why is the invented headline "Salon du fromage : les producteurs en font tout un fromage" a pun?
choices: It uses fromage twice to sound like a children's rhyme.
It replaces the idiom's usual word with fromage.
Fromage is literal (cheesemakers) and also part of the idiom for making a fuss.
The idiom normally means to make cheese.
questions.explanation: En faire tout un fromage means to make a mountain out of a molehill. Applied to cheesemakers, the literal word comes back to life: the headline says they're making a fuss, and it's about cheese.

questions.stem: What does "Son oncle a le bras long" mean?
choices: Her uncle works for the police.
Her uncle has friends in high places.
questions.explanation: Avoir le bras long is about influence and connections. Very generous is avoir le cœur sur la main; the idiom has nothing to do with the long arm of the law.

questions.stem: What does "Son silence m'a mis la puce à l'oreille" mean?
questions.explanation: Mettre la puce à l'oreille à quelqu'un is to make someone suspicious, to set alarm bells ringing. The thing that arouses suspicion is the subject.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses "ménager la chèvre et le chou" correctly?
choices: Elle ménage la chèvre et le chou : elle adore les animaux de la ferme.
En promettant des aides aux uns et des baisses d'impôts aux autres, le maire ménage la chèvre et le chou.
Il a ménagé la chèvre et le chou en refusant de parler à quiconque.
Nous avons ménagé la chèvre et le chou, alors la réunion a été très courte.
questions.explanation: Ménager la chèvre et le chou is to try to please both sides. The mayor promises something to each camp. The other sentences use it literally (farm animals) or for something unrelated (refusing to talk, a short meeting).

questions.stem: In the reading La réunion du lundi, who let the cat out of the bag (a vendu la mèche) at the meeting?
choices: Bertrand, the colleague who called the move an opportunity
questions.explanation: C'est Sophie, notre stagiaire, qui a fini par vendre la mèche: she innocently asked about the move to Lyon. The IT manager had told her, but he wasn't at the meeting.

questions.stem: At the end of the reading La réunion du lundi, how did management "couper la poire en deux"?
choices: The move will go ahead a year later than planned, and staff may work from home.
The move to Lyon was cancelled.
Half the team moved to Lyon in March.
The intern was hired instead of a manager.
questions.explanation: Couper la poire en deux is to split the difference: the move still happens (management's wish), but a year later and with remote work (the staff's wish).

questions.stem: Listen to the radio item. What has the candidate done?

audio.text: Coup de théâtre ce matin : après des semaines de sondages décevants, la candidate écologiste jette l'éponge. Elle appelle ses électeurs à soutenir la liste de gauche, qui a le vent en poupe.

choices: She has won the first round of the election.
She has withdrawn and asked her voters to back a list that is doing well.
She has taken her rivals to court.
She has joined a list that is losing ground.
questions.explanation: La candidate jette l'éponge = she throws in the towel (withdraws). La liste de gauche a le vent en poupe = it is on a roll, and she calls on her voters to support it.

questions.stem: Listen to two colleagues disagreeing. What does the second speaker mean?

audio.text: Tu exagères, ce n'est qu'un petit retard, tu ne vas pas en faire tout un fromage ! — Un petit retard ? C'est la troisième fois ce mois-ci. Pour moi, c'est la goutte d'eau qui fait déborder le vase.

choices: The delay is no big deal.
He wants to split the difference.
This delay is the last straw for him.
questions.explanation: The first speaker says don't make a fuss (tu ne vas pas en faire tout un fromage). The second answers that it's the third time this month: la goutte d'eau qui fait déborder le vase, the last straw.

questions.stem: Which sentences keep the idiom intact? Select all that apply.
choices: Elle lui a passé un sacré savon.
Ne tourne pas autour du pot.
Après l'échec, il a jeté une éponge.
Ils ont coupé la poire en deux.
Il a pris une mouche pour une remarque.
questions.explanation: Tense, pronouns, negation and an adjective like sacré can move inside an idiom. The determiners can't: it's jeter l'éponge and prendre la mouche, never une éponge or une mouche.

questions.stem: Complete the idiom with one word: "Désolé, je n'ai pas le temps : j'ai d'autres ___ à fouetter."
questions.explanation: Avoir d'autres chats à fouetter = to have other fish to fry. The word is chats, in the plural, after d'autres.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "Don't put the cart before the horse."
questions.explanation: Ne mets pas la charrue avant les bœufs. Negation wraps the verb (ne … pas) and the rest of the idiom stays as it is.

questions.stem: Match each idiom to its English equivalent.
choices: to have other fish to fry
to let the cat out of the bag
to be down in the dumps
questions.explanation: The French and English pictures differ (cats and fish, a fuse and a cat, angels and the moon), but the meanings match. To take offence is prendre la mouche.

questions.stem: Name the idiom behind each numbered picture.

image.alt: Six picture cards, numbered: a sponge flying into a boxing ring; a pear cut into two halves with a knife; a full vase with a drop falling and water running over; a sailing boat pushed by wind arrows from behind; a goat next to a cabbage; a cyclist bent low over his handlebars.

choices: la goutte d'eau qui fait déborder le vase
ménager la chèvre et le chou
avoir la tête dans le guidon
questions.explanation: Each picture shows an idiom's literal image: the sponge thrown into the ring, the pear cut in two, the drop that makes the vase overflow, the wind behind the stern, the goat and the cabbage, the cyclist with his head over the handlebars. No fly or flea is pictured.

questions.stem: Complete: "Les secouristes ont ___ preuve d'un grand courage."
questions.explanation: The support verb is faire: faire preuve de courage (to show courage). In a support-verb construction the verb can't be swapped, even for one that seems to mean the same (montrer).

questions.stem: Complete: "La commune ___ en œuvre le nouveau plan en janvier."
questions.explanation: The construction is mettre en œuvre (to implement); its noun is la mise en œuvre. Faire, prendre and donner don't combine with en œuvre.

questions.stem: What does "Le projet a fait l'objet de deux recours" mean?
choices: The project was the subject of two legal challenges.
The project's aim was to win two appeals.
questions.explanation: Faire l'objet de = to be the subject of, to undergo. Un recours is a legal challenge.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il faut remédier ___ retards du chantier."
questions.explanation: Remédier takes à: remédier à un problème. À + les = aux. Remédier with a direct object (remédier les retards) is a common mistake.

questions.stem: Which sentence contains an English calque to avoid?
choices: Le conseil va prendre une décision demain.
Le conseil va faire une décision demain.
Un élu a posé une question au maire.
questions.explanation: French prend une décision; faire une décision copies English "make a decision". Avoir lieu (to take place) and poser une question are the right partners.

questions.stem: What does "une hausse sensible des loyers" mean?
questions.explanation: In this collocation sensible means noticeable, appreciable. It is a false friend: sensible in English is raisonnable.

questions.stem: Complete with the usual intensifier: "Le syndicat a opposé un refus ___ à la proposition."
questions.explanation: Un refus catégorique is the habitual partner (a flat refusal). Battant goes with pluie, sensible with hausse or baisse, large with majorité.

questions.stem: What is "la mise en œuvre" of a reform?
questions.explanation: La mise en œuvre is the implementation: putting a decision or a plan into practice. Setting up a structure is la mise en place.

questions.stem: In paragraph 3 of the reading (le tramway de Montvalon), what does the opposition report (fait état de)?
choices: medieval remains under the market square
an extra cost of forty million euros
questions.explanation: L'opposition, qui fait état d'un surcoût de quarante millions d'euros: faire état de = to mention, to report formally. The remains are in paragraph 2, the shuttle in paragraph 4 and the new date in paragraph 5.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2 of the reading (le tramway de Montvalon), what held up the work?
choices: A vote against the project by the council
Archaeological digs and two legal challenges by residents
questions.explanation: La mise en œuvre s'est heurtée à des obstacles imprévus: medieval remains (six months of excavations) and deux recours d'habitants, during which the site couldn't move forward.

questions.stem: What does "Les questions des habitants avaient trait au stationnement" mean?
choices: The residents' questions were drawn up in the car park.
The residents' questions were about to be answered.
The residents' questions were ignored because of parking.
questions.explanation: Avoir trait à = to relate to, to concern. The subject is a thing (les questions).

questions.stem: Complete in careful written French: "Le maire a décidé de passer outre ___ l'avis des experts."
questions.explanation: Careful writing keeps à after passer outre: passer outre à une objection. In the press you'll also read passer outre l'avis, with no preposition, but de, sur and contre are never used.

questions.stem: What does "Le conseil a pris acte de la démission du trésorier" mean?
choices: The council formally took note of the treasurer's resignation.
The council refused the treasurer's resignation.
The council asked the treasurer to resign.
The council celebrated the treasurer's resignation.
questions.explanation: Prendre acte de = to take formal note of something, without necessarily approving or refusing it.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio item. What happened to the swimming-pool project?

audio.text: Le projet de piscine municipale s'est soldé par un échec : le conseil n'a pas donné suite à la pétition des habitants, faute de financement.

choices: It failed, and the council didn't act on the residents' petition.
It succeeded thanks to the residents' petition.
The pool will open next year.
The council found new funding for it.
questions.explanation: S'est soldé par un échec = ended in failure. Le conseil n'a pas donné suite à la pétition = the council didn't act on the petition, faute de financement (for lack of funding).

questions.stem: Listen to two people disagreeing. What does the second speaker claim?

audio.text: Votre plan porte atteinte au patrimoine du centre-ville ! — Au contraire, nous avons mis l'accent sur la préservation des façades.

choices: The plan harms the old town.
The plan puts the emphasis on preserving the façades.
The plan was drawn up without consultation.
questions.explanation: The first speaker accuses: votre plan porte atteinte au patrimoine (harms the heritage). The second replies: nous avons mis l'accent sur la préservation des façades (we put the emphasis on preserving them).

questions.stem: Which constructions are correct? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Faire face à, donner lieu à and tirer parti de are correct. Remédier takes à (remédier à un problème), and mettre l'accent takes sur (mettre l'accent sur la sécurité).

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "La région prend en ___ la moitié du coût des travaux."
questions.explanation: Prendre en charge = to cover (costs), to take charge of. La région prend en charge la moitié du coût.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "The meeting ended in failure."
questions.explanation: La réunion s'est soldée par un échec. Se solder par introduces a result; soldée agrees with la réunion.

questions.stem: Match each support verb to its meaning.
choices: to follow up, to act on
questions.explanation: To take advantage of is tirer parti de. The four others are formal support verbs, each with a fixed preposition.

questions.stem: Name the numbered stages of this public project.

image.alt: A timeline arrow with four numbered dots. Above them, from left to right: a document with a checklist, a calendar with coloured bars, a red tram on rails beside a crane, and a bar chart with a tick mark.

questions.explanation: First the specifications (le cahier des charges: the checklist), then the schedule of deadlines (l'échéancier: the bars on a calendar), the implementation (la mise en œuvre: the works), and the final review (le bilan: the results chart with a tick).

questions.stem: A woman writes her thesis alone, using the nous of modesty. Complete: "Nous sommes ___ que cette hypothèse doit être revue."
questions.explanation: With the nous of modesty the verb is plural (sommes), but the adjective agrees with the real author: one woman, so feminine singular, convaincue.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il importe que les données ___ vérifiées avant publication."
questions.explanation: Il importe que takes the subjunctive: il importe que les données soient vérifiées. With an infinitive, use il importe de vérifier les données.

questions.stem: Complete: "Il convient ___ distinguer deux cas."
questions.explanation: Il convient de + infinitive (one should, it is advisable to). Il convient que needs a conjugated verb in the subjunctive.

questions.stem: Which phrase presents an author's claim as established, rather than simply reporting it?
questions.explanation: Comme le montre adopts the claim: you agree that Dupont has shown it. Selon and d'après report a view neutrally, and pour Dupont means "in Dupont's view".

questions.stem: What does [sic] after a word in a quotation mean?
choices: The quotation has been shortened here.
The writer of the essay disagrees with the word.
The mistake is in the original text.
questions.explanation: Sic is Latin for "thus": the word was written this way in the original, and the error isn't yours. A cut is marked with […].

questions.stem: Source: "L'étalement urbain allonge les trajets quotidiens et rend la voiture indispensable aux ménages modestes" (Martin, 2018). Which sentence is an acceptable paraphrase?
choices: L'étalement des villes allonge les déplacements quotidiens et rend l'automobile indispensable aux familles modestes.
Comme le montre Martin (2018), plus une ville s'étend, plus les ménages aux revenus faibles dépendent de leur voiture.
L'étalement urbain rend la voiture indispensable aux ménages modestes.
Plus une ville s'étend, plus les ménages aux revenus faibles dépendent de leur voiture.
questions.explanation: A paraphrase changes the words and the structure and still names the source. Two of the other sentences reuse the source's wording without a reference, and the last one is reworded but hides where the idea comes from: all three are plagiarism.

questions.stem: Complete: "Elle soutiendra ___ mémoire de master en juin."
questions.explanation: Le mémoire (a dissertation) is masculine: son mémoire. La mémoire (memory) is feminine, which is why sa, la and une sound wrong here.

questions.stem: What does "Il a des a priori sur les jeunes" mean?
choices: He gives priority to young people.
He has studied young people for a long time.
He has privileges over young people.
He has preconceptions about young people.
questions.explanation: As a noun, un a priori is a preconception, an opinion formed before looking at the facts.

questions.stem: What does "Si les adultes s'y perdent, a fortiori les enfants" mean?
choices: If adults get lost, children are even more likely to.
If adults get lost, children won't.
Adults get lost before children do.
Adults get lost because of the children.
questions.explanation: A fortiori = all the more so, with even more reason. Children are even more likely to get lost.

questions.stem: Which formula introduces a definition?
questions.explanation: On entend par X … = by X we mean …: On entend par « ville moyenne » une commune de 20 000 à 100 000 habitants. The others admit a fact, stress importance or introduce a source.

questions.stem: What does "Cette question relève de la sociologie" mean?
choices: This question raises a sociological problem.
This question was raised by sociologists.
questions.explanation: Relever de = to come under, to be a matter of (a field, an authority).

questions.stem: In paragraph 1 of the reading (un mémoire sous le soupçon), why did the 30 % figure turn out to be misleading?
choices: The software had analysed the wrong dissertation.
The student had written the article herself.
Most of the matching passages were properly quoted or were titles in the bibliography.
The figure counted only the footnotes.
questions.explanation: A posteriori, il était trompeur: la plupart des passages signalés étaient des citations placées entre guillemets, avec leur note de bas de page, ou des titres de la bibliographie.

questions.stem: In paragraph 3 of the reading (un mémoire sous le soupçon), what happened to the student?
choices: She was expelled from the university.
Her viva was postponed; she rewrote the chapter and graduated.
She defended her dissertation on the planned date.
She was cleared because it was only a paraphrase.
questions.explanation: La soutenance a été reportée à septembre ; l'étudiante a réécrit le chapitre et a finalement obtenu son diplôme. The committee found limited plagiarism, not an acceptable paraphrase.

questions.stem: Listen to this extract from a lecture. What will the lecturer use first?

audio.text: Dans cette partie, nous nous appuierons sur des sources primaires : les registres paroissiaux du dix-huitième siècle et la correspondance des curés. Nous les compléterons, dans un second temps, par des travaux plus récents.

choices: primary sources: parish registers and priests' letters
questions.explanation: Nous nous appuierons sur des sources primaires : les registres paroissiaux … et la correspondance des curés. More recent work (des travaux plus récents) comes second (dans un second temps).

questions.stem: Listen to the announcement. What will happen to the proposals for papers?

audio.text: Le colloque des doctorants aura lieu le 14 mars. Les propositions de communication, d'une page au plus, sont à envoyer avant le 15 janvier ; elles seront soumises à une évaluation par les pairs.

choices: They will be published straight away.
They will be read by the dean alone.
They will be sent back in March.
questions.explanation: Elles seront soumises à une évaluation par les pairs = they will undergo peer review. March is the date of the conference itself.

questions.stem: Which follow standard French conventions for quoting? Select all that apply.
choices: « … », with a space inside each quotation mark
[…] to show that part of the quotation has been cut
[sic] after an error that is in the original
[sic] after a spelling mistake of your own
Quoting a whole paragraph without naming its author
questions.explanation: French uses « … » with spaces inside, […] for a cut and [sic] for an error in the original. Sic never excuses your own mistakes, and a quotation always names its source.

questions.stem: Complete with the Latin phrase meaning "with hindsight": "On ne peut juger cette décision qu'___."
questions.explanation: A posteriori = with hindsight, after the facts: on ne peut juger cette décision qu'a posteriori. It is usually written without accents.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "By 'medium-sized town' we mean a municipality of 20,000 to 100,000 inhabitants."
questions.explanation: On entend par « ville moyenne » une commune de 20 000 à 100 000 habitants. The term being defined comes straight after on entend par; the definition follows.

questions.stem: Match each Latin phrase to its meaning.
questions.explanation: In the broad sense is lato sensu. All these phrases are usually written without accents in French.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this page from a dissertation.

image.alt: A dissertation page headed 2. Méthodologie with five numbered markers: one above an opening French quotation mark, two under a cut shown as three dots in square brackets and under [sic], one beside a small raised number 1 after the closing quotation mark, and one beside the footnote at the bottom of the page.

choices: la note de bas de page
questions.explanation: The quotation opens and closes with guillemets; […] marks a cut; [sic] follows the misspelled trés, an error in the original; the small raised 1 is the note call (l'appel de note); and the reference at the bottom is the footnote (la note de bas de page).

questions.stem: Which word is the negative of "lisible" (legible)?
questions.explanation: The prefix in- becomes il- before l: illisible. It becomes im- before b, m, p (impossible) and ir- before r (irréversible).

questions.stem: What does "Ces réunions sont chronophages" mean?
choices: These meetings are held at regular times.
These meetings take up a lot of time.
questions.explanation: Chrono- (time) + -phage (that eats): chronophage = time-consuming.

questions.stem: In "énergivore" and "budgétivore", what does -vore mean?
questions.explanation: -vore (Latin) and -phage (Greek) both mean "that eats": an énergivore device eats energy, a budgétivore project eats budgets. That loves is -phile, that measures is -mètre.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: An acronym usually takes the gender of the first noun of its full name: l'Organisation des Nations unies, so feminine (intervenue). Before a vowel sound the article is elided: l'ONU.

questions.stem: Complete in standard written French: "Plusieurs ___ ont signé l'appel."
questions.explanation: Sigles normally don't change in the plural in writing: des ONG, des PDG. Only acronyms that have become ordinary words take s (des ovnis).

questions.stem: Which compound noun has the same plural in the traditional system and under the 1990 recommendations?
questions.explanation: The 1990 rule changes verb + noun and preposition + noun compounds (des porte-monnaies, des gratte-ciels, des après-midis). Noun + preposition + noun compounds keep their plural: des chefs-d'œuvre in both systems.

questions.stem: Which of these is an acronym, read as a word rather than letter by letter?
questions.explanation: L'Unesco is read as a word, so it is an acronym (l'acronyme). La SNCF, le PDG and la RATP are read letter by letter: they are sigles.

questions.stem: In the pair frêle / fragile, which is the learned word (mot savant)?
choices: frêle, borrowed almost unchanged from written Latin
fragile, borrowed almost unchanged from written Latin
both, because both come from Latin
neither, because both come from English
questions.explanation: Both come from Latin fragilis. Frêle came down through centuries of sound change (a popular word); fragile was borrowed later from written Latin (a learned word). Such pairs are doublets.

questions.stem: What does "un adolescent hyperconnecté" mean?
choices: a teenager who works with computers
a teenager who can't get online
a teenager who is always online
questions.explanation: Hyper- (over, too much) + connecté: always online.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 1 of the reading (la face cachée du nuage), what share of France's carbon footprint did digital technology account for in 2022, in the assessment published in January 2025?
questions.explanation: 4,4 % pour l'année 2022. The 2.5 % figure is for 2020, 46 % is the data centres' share of digital technology's footprint, and 45 % is the possible rise by 2030 in paragraph 2.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 1 of the reading, why does part of the rise come from method?
choices: The first study had counted only phones.
The second study used figures from another country.
The second study also counted data centres abroad that serve French users.
The first study had been published by another agency.
questions.explanation: La seconde étude a pris en compte, en plus, les centres de données situés à l'étranger qui servent les usages français: part of the rise reflects a wider count, not only more use.

questions.stem: What does "xénophobe" mean?
questions.explanation: Xéno- (foreign) + -phobe (who fears or hates). Afraid of closed spaces is claustrophobe; fond of France is francophile.

questions.stem: Listen to the news item. What will heat the swimming pool?

audio.text: Bonne nouvelle pour les nageurs : à partir de l'hiver prochain, la piscine municipale sera chauffée grâce à la chaleur récupérée sur les serveurs d'un centre de données voisin. Un projet moins énergivore, selon la mairie.

choices: heat recovered from a nearby data centre's servers
questions.explanation: La piscine municipale sera chauffée grâce à la chaleur récupérée sur les serveurs d'un centre de données voisin. The town calls the project moins énergivore.

questions.stem: Listen to the lecture extract. What does the lecturer explain?

audio.text: Le mot « biométrie » est formé de deux éléments grecs : « bio », la vie, et « métrie », la mesure. Il désigne donc, littéralement, la mesure du vivant.

choices: the two Greek elements of the word biométrie
the history of the word vie
questions.explanation: Bio (life) + métrie (measurement): la mesure du vivant, the measurement of living beings.

questions.stem: What is "une salle polyvalente"?
choices: a hall for political meetings only
questions.explanation: Poly- (many) + valent: polyvalent = versatile, multipurpose. The noun is la polyvalence.

questions.stem: Which plurals of "un porte-monnaie" are correct in France today? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Traditionally, des porte-monnaie (things that carry money); under the 1990 recommendations, des porte-monnaies (the last word takes s in the plural). Both are correct. The verb porte never takes s.

questions.stem: Write the antonym of "réversible" made with a prefix.
questions.explanation: In- becomes ir- before r: irréversible.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "These meetings have become very time-consuming."
questions.explanation: Ces réunions sont devenues très chronophages. Devenir takes être, so devenues agrees with réunions; chronophage takes an s in the plural.

questions.stem: Match each learned element to its meaning.
questions.explanation: That kills is -cide (insecticide). Chronophage, technocratie, xénophobie and francophile are built from the four others.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the word illisible.

image.alt: The word illisible split into three coloured boxes, il, lis and ible, each with a number underneath. Below, chronophage is shown as chrono plus phage.

questions.explanation: Il- is the prefix (in- before l), lis- the stem that carries the meaning (from lire), and -ible the suffix that makes an adjective of possibility.

questions.stem: In France, who must use an official term once it is published in the Journal officiel?
choices: the State's services, in their official documents
every French citizen, in speech and writing
questions.explanation: Publication binds the State's services. For everyone else it is a recommendation: in 1994 the Conseil constitutionnel struck out the part of the law that would have imposed official terms on private people and the media.

questions.stem: Which body examines the expert groups' proposals before the Académie française gives its opinion?
choices: the Office québécois de la langue française
the Commission d'enrichissement de la langue française
questions.explanation: Expert groups propose; the Commission d'enrichissement de la langue française examines; the Académie française gives its opinion; with the minister's agreement, the term is published in the Journal officiel.

questions.stem: In which year did the Journal officiel publish "infox" as the French equivalent of "fake news"?
questions.explanation: Infox (information + intoxication) was published on 4 October 2018, with information fallacieuse. 2003 is courriel, 2013 mot-dièse, 2020 divulgâcher and audio à la demande.

questions.stem: What term does the OQLF in Québec prefer for "hashtag"?
questions.explanation: France chose le mot-dièse (2013); the OQLF prefers le mot-clic, partly because the sharp sign (dièse) and the # are not quite the same symbol. Un mot-clé is a keyword.

questions.stem: How is "courriel" built?
questions.explanation: Courriel is a portmanteau word (mot-valise): it keeps the start of courrier and the end of électronique. It spread from Québec, where the OQLF promoted it in the 1990s, and was published in France in 2003.

questions.stem: What does the loi Toubon of 4 August 1994 require?
choices: French in situations such as product instructions, advertising and employment contracts, with translations allowed alongside
that English words be banned from advertising
that the media use only official terms
that every university course be taught in French, with no exception
questions.explanation: The law makes French compulsory in many situations without banning other languages next to it. It doesn't force the media to use official terms, and teaching has exceptions (international schools, some courses in foreign languages).

questions.stem: Why did "ordinateur" catch on while "mot-dièse" stayed rare?
choices: Ordinateur was imposed by law on everyone.
Mot-dièse is too long to say.
Ordinateur arrived before the English word was established; mot-dièse came years after hashtag.
questions.explanation: A term wins when it comes early, is short and fills a need. Ordinateur (1955) came first; by 2013 everyone already said hashtag. Mot-dièse was published in the Journal officiel, and no law imposes terms on private speakers.

questions.stem: Which two words make up "divulgâcher"?
questions.explanation: Divulguer (to reveal) + gâcher (to spoil): to spoil a story by revealing its plot. The person is un divulgâcheur.

questions.stem: How is "Mél." used in official French?
choices: as the everyday noun for an email
only as a symbol before an email address, like Tél.
as a verb meaning to email
as the Québec word for an email
questions.explanation: Mél. is a symbol placed before an address, like Tél. before a phone number. The noun is courriel.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio item. What does the new list recommend?

audio.text: Le Journal officiel publie ce matin une nouvelle liste de termes recommandés pour le vocabulaire du jeu vidéo. Les services de l'État devront les employer ; pour les joueurs, en revanche, il ne s'agit que de recommandations.

choices: a ban on English words in video games
new rules for the spelling of English words
a list of words the Académie has rejected
French terms for video games, to be used by public services
questions.explanation: Une nouvelle liste de termes recommandés pour le vocabulaire du jeu vidéo: les services de l'État devront les employer; pour les joueurs, il ne s'agit que de recommandations. Binding for the State, a recommendation for everyone else.

questions.stem: Type the official term used in France for "hashtag" (with its hyphen).
questions.explanation: Le mot-dièse (Journal officiel, 23 January 2013): plural les mots-dièse in FranceTerme. Québec prefers le mot-clic.

questions.stem: Match each English word to the official equivalent published in France.
questions.explanation: Infox (2018), audio à la demande and divulgâcher (2020), courriel (2003). Mot-clic is the OQLF's term for hashtag in Québec, not a term published in France.

questions.stem: Put the steps that make a term official in France in order.
choices: An expert group proposes a French equivalent and a definition.
The Commission d'enrichissement de la langue française examines it.
The Académie française gives its opinion.
The term is published in the Journal officiel.
The term is entered in the FranceTerme database.
questions.explanation: Experts propose, the Commission examines, the Académie gives its opinion, and with the minister's agreement the term is published in the Journal officiel, then entered in FranceTerme.

questions.stem: Which of these are portmanteau words (mots-valises)? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Infox (information + intoxication), courriel (courrier + électronique) and franglais (français + anglais) each keep a piece of two words. Ordinateur is a single derived word, and mot-dièse joins two whole words: a compound, not a blend.

questions.stem: What usually distinguishes a maxim from a proverb?
choices: A maxim often has a named author; a proverb is anonymous.
A maxim is always about the weather.
A maxim is always in Latin.
A maxim is always longer than a paragraph.
questions.explanation: A proverb is anonymous popular wisdom; a maxim is a rule of conduct or general truth, often by a named author such as La Rochefoucauld. Sayings about the weather are usually dictons.

questions.stem: In "Qui ne dit mot consent", what does "qui" mean?
questions.explanation: Qui without an antecedent means whoever: whoever says nothing consents. Modern French would say celui qui.

questions.stem: In "Qui ne dit mot consent", what does "ne … mot" mean?
questions.explanation: Ne … mot is an old negation, like ne … point: il ne dit mot = il ne dit rien.

questions.stem: Which English saying matches "Chat échaudé craint l'eau froide"?
questions.explanation: A scalded cat fears even cold water: after a bad experience we fear even what is harmless. Once bitten, twice shy.

questions.stem: Where does "Qui sème le vent récolte la tempête" come from?
choices: the Bible, the Book of Hosea
questions.explanation: The image of sowing the wind and reaping the storm goes back to the Book of Hosea (Osée). La Fontaine is linked to the bearskin proverb.

questions.stem: When was the first edition of La Rochefoucauld's Maximes published?
questions.explanation: Réflexions ou sentences et maximes morales appeared in Paris in 1665; La Rochefoucauld revised it until 1678. 1580 is Montaigne's first Essais, 1668 La Fontaine's first fables, 1721 the Lettres persanes.

questions.stem: What do La Rochefoucauld's Maximes find behind most of our virtues?
questions.explanation: The Maximes argue that self-love (l'amour-propre) and self-interest hide behind generosity, modesty and even friendship.

questions.stem: Which category best fits "Noël au balcon, Pâques au tison"?
choices: a maxim by a named author
a dicton, a popular saying about the weather
an idiom used inside a sentence
questions.explanation: Dictons are popular sayings, often about the weather and the seasons: a mild Christmas means a cold Easter.

questions.stem: Which of these is an adage?
choices: Noël au balcon, Pâques au tison.
Nul n'est censé ignorer la loi.
questions.explanation: An adage is an old maxim, often from law: ignorance of the law is no excuse. The second is a dicton about the weather, and the last two are idioms.

questions.stem: How should you use a proverb in the introduction of an essay?
choices: Use it as proof that your thesis is right.
Quote three proverbs to show your range.
Introduce it, then question it to lead to your problématique.
