questions.explanation: A proverb makes a good hook (amorce) if you treat it as a claim to test: introduce it (comme le dit le proverbe), then question it (mais est-ce encore vrai … ?).

questions.stem: When is "À bon entendeur, salut" said?
choices: at the end of a veiled warning
at the start of a formal letter
questions.explanation: À bon entendeur, salut = a word to the wise: it closes a warning, meaning "you've been told". L'entendeur is an old word for one who understands.

questions.stem: Complete the proverb: "Il n'y a pas de fumée sans ___."
questions.explanation: Il n'y a pas de fumée sans feu = there's no smoke without fire: a rumour usually has some truth in it.

questions.stem: Put the proverb in order.
questions.explanation: Il ne faut pas vendre la peau de l'ours avant de l'avoir tué: don't count your chickens before they hatch.

questions.stem: Match each proverb to its English equivalent.
left: L'habit ne fait pas le moine.
Qui sème le vent récolte la tempête.
Il n'y a pas de fumée sans feu.
choices: Don't judge a book by its cover.
Sow the wind, reap the whirlwind.
questions.explanation: A word to the wise is À bon entendeur, salut. The pictures differ (a monk's habit, a book cover), but the meanings match.

questions.stem: Which grammatical features are typical of French proverbs? Select all that apply.
choices: the generic present (Chat échaudé craint l'eau froide)
a noun with no article (Pierre qui roule n'amasse pas mousse)
qui meaning whoever (Qui ne dit mot consent)
the passé simple in every proverb
questions.explanation: Proverbs state timeless truths in the present, often drop the article and use qui = whoever. They are not in the passé simple, and they follow French, not English, word order.

questions.stem: Which sentence contains a proposition participiale (a participle with its own subject)?
choices: Le contrat signé, les travaux ont commencé.
Signant le contrat, la directrice a souri.
Fille d'ouvriers, elle a signé le contrat.
En signant le contrat, la directrice a souri.
questions.explanation: "Le contrat signé" has its own subject (le contrat), different from the main subject (les travaux). "Signant le contrat" is a detached participle and "En signant" a gérondif: both describe the main subject, la directrice. "Fille d'ouvriers" is an apposition (no verb).

questions.stem: Complete: "Une fois la décision ___, personne n'est revenu dessus."
questions.explanation: In a proposition participiale the participle agrees with its own subject: la décision (feminine singular), so "prise". "Prenant" would need a different construction; "pris" and "prises" have the wrong agreement.

questions.stem: In each sentence, the opening participle is meant to describe the speaker (je). Which sentence is correct in careful writing?
choices: Étant malade, le médecin m'a prescrit du repos.
Licenciée en mars, la direction ne m'a rien proposé.
Étant malade, j'ai consulté un médecin.
Arrivé en retard, le patron m'a fait une remarque.
questions.explanation: A participle at the head of the sentence describes the subject of the main verb. In "Étant malade, j'ai consulté un médecin" the sick person is je, the subject. The other three dangle: read as written, they say that the doctor was ill, that management was laid off and that the boss arrived late.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ses arguments étaient très ___."
questions.explanation: After "étaient très" you need an adjective that agrees with "arguments" (masculine plural): the adjectif verbal "convaincants", spelled with -c-. "Convainquant" (with -qu-) is the invariable participe présent, used with an object (convainquant le jury).

questions.stem: Complete: "Les jours ___ la grève, l'usine tournait au ralenti." (the days before the strike)
questions.explanation: Here the word takes an object (la grève), so it is the participe présent "précédant", invariable and spelled -ant. "Précédents" is the adjective (les jours précédents, the previous days), which cannot take an object; "précédants" doesn't exist.

questions.stem: Which phrase contains an adjectif verbal?
choices: fatiguant ses équipes par des réunions
les réunions fatiguant tout le monde
questions.explanation: "Des horaires fatigants" describes a quality and agrees (masculine plural), with the adjective spelling -gant. The others are verb forms that take an object (ses équipes, tout le monde): participe présent or gérondif, spelled -guant and invariable.

questions.stem: What does "Le temps pressant, nous avons écourté la visite" mean?
choices: Although time was short, we made the visit longer.
We hurried because the visit was short.
Because time was short, we cut the visit short.
The visit was short, so time passed quickly.
questions.explanation: "Le temps pressant" is a proposition participiale with its own subject (le temps): it gives the cause. "Écourter" means to shorten. The other translations reverse the cause or the meaning of écourter.

questions.stem: In paragraph 2 of the reading, what does the author say has happened since Marx's time?
choices: Workers now see the purpose of what they produce.
Constraint at work has often changed form rather than nature.
questions.explanation: "La servitude a parfois changé de forme plutôt que de nature": the examples are the order picker, the call-centre worker and the manager reading e-mail at midnight. The text says assembly lines have declined "dans bien des pays", not everywhere, and that the feeling of absurdity remains.

questions.stem: In paragraph 4 of the reading, which distinction does the author draw?
choices: between idleness that is chosen and idleness that is endured
between ancient and modern ideas of work
between manual work and intellectual work
questions.explanation: "Encore faut-il distinguer l'oisiveté choisie du désœuvrement subi": idleness by choice is a luxury, idleness forced on the unemployed is an ordeal. The ancients and Lafargue are examples, not the two sides of the distinction.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 5 of the reading, what did Finland's 2017–2018 trial show?
choices: The participants stopped looking for work.
The participants worked about as much as others but felt less anxious.
A basic income works for a whole society.
The participants worked much more than others.
questions.explanation: "Ceux-ci n'ont guère moins travaillé que les autres, ni beaucoup plus, mais ils se disaient moins anxieux." The author adds that a limited trial says nothing certain about a whole society.

questions.stem: Which best describes the author's stance in the reading?
choices: hostile to work in every form
a supporter of basic income for everyone
balanced, ending with a cautious answer of their own
questions.explanation: Paragraphs 2 and 3 set criticism against defence, 4 and 5 test the alternatives, and paragraph 6 gives an answer (the search for meaning may be the condition of effort), softened by "peut-être". So the essay is balanced but not neutral.

questions.stem: In the exam, what should you do first with a long texte d'idées?
choices: Look up every word you don't know.
Translate the first paragraph word by word.
Answer the questions in order during your first reading.
Skim the title, the first and last paragraphs and the first sentence of each paragraph to find the thesis.
questions.explanation: Skimming first gives you the subject, the thesis and the plan, so the detailed reading and the questions have a frame. Word-by-word reading from the first line is the commonest way to run out of time.

questions.stem: Complete with the adjective related to "négliger", agreeing with its noun: "Ces employés sont trop ___."
questions.explanation: The adjectif verbal of négliger is spelled -ent: négligent, négligents. "Négligeant" is the participe présent (négligeant leurs tâches), which is invariable and takes an object.

questions.stem: Put the steps of the reading's argument in the order the essay follows.
choices: work long seen as suffering; today people want meaning
work as a means of emancipation
the search for meaning as the condition of effort
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 asks the question; 2 gives the criticism (alienation); 3 the defence (emancipation); 4 distinguishes idleness; 5 tests basic income; 6 answers.

questions.stem: Match each participe présent to its adjectif verbal.
questions.explanation: These pairs differ in spelling: -quant / -cant, -ant / -ent. "Le différend" (with a d) is a noun meaning a dispute, not the adjective.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct in careful writing? Select all that apply.
choices: La réunion terminée, chacun est rentré chez soi.
Arrivée à Lyon, elle a trouvé un emploi.
Licenciée en mars, la direction ne m'a rien proposé.
Une fois le contrat signée, les travaux commenceront.
Ancien mineur, mon grand-père parlait peu de son travail.
questions.explanation: "La réunion terminée" agrees with its own subject; "Arrivée" and "Ancien mineur" describe the subject of the main verb (elle, mon grand-père). "Licenciée en mars, la direction …" dangles (management was not laid off), and "le contrat signée" has the wrong agreement: le contrat is masculine, so signé.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this long sentence.

image.alt: A long French sentence split into five coloured boxes, stacked and indented, with numbered markers above four of them: 1 above Le contrat signé; 2 above l'entreprise; 3 above the indented qui recrutait depuis un an; then, unnumbered, a embauché dix ingénieurs, joined to the second box by a dashed bracket; 4 above the indented parce que ses commandes avaient doublé.

questions.explanation: "Le contrat signé" has its own subject: a proposition participiale. "L'entreprise … a embauché dix ingénieurs" is the main clause, interrupted by the relative "qui recrutait depuis un an". "Parce que ses commandes avaient doublé" gives the cause. There is no apposition or adjectif verbal in this sentence.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio item. What do the first results show?

audio.text: Dans notre région, l'expérimentation d'un revenu de base pour les jeunes de dix-huit à vingt-cinq ans prendra fin en juin. Les premiers résultats, présentés hier, sont nuancés : les bénéficiaires ne travaillent ni plus ni moins qu'avant, mais ils déclarent avoir repris une formation plus souvent que les autres.

choices: The recipients work about as much as before but go back to training more often.
The trial will be extended to the whole country.
The young recipients have stopped working.
The recipients work much more than before.
questions.explanation: "Les bénéficiaires ne travaillent ni plus ni moins qu'avant, mais ils déclarent avoir repris une formation plus souvent que les autres." The trial ends in June; nothing is said about extending it.

questions.stem: Listen to two friends. What is the second speaker's main point?

audio.text: Le revenu universel, c'est payer les gens à ne rien faire. — Pas du tout : c'est leur laisser le choix de leur travail. — Avec quel argent ? — En partie avec celui qu'on dépense déjà en aides de toutes sortes.

choices: A basic income pays people to do nothing.
A basic income gives people a choice of work and could be partly paid for by existing benefits.
A basic income is far too expensive to consider.
All existing benefits should be abolished.
questions.explanation: The second speaker answers that a basic income is "leur laisser le choix de leur travail" and would be financed "en partie avec celui qu'on dépense déjà en aides de toutes sortes". Paying people to do nothing is the first speaker's claim.

questions.stem: Which opening belongs to a compte rendu rather than a résumé?
choices: Les écrans du soir privent les adolescents de sommeil.
Je pense que les écrans du soir privent les adolescents de sommeil.
Dans un article paru en mars 2026, la journaliste Claire Vidal montre que les écrans du soir privent les adolescents de sommeil.
Selon moi, les adolescents dorment trop peu.
questions.explanation: A compte rendu stands outside the text: it names the source and reports in the third person (la journaliste … montre que). A résumé speaks as the author ("Les écrans du soir privent …"). The openings with je and selon moi give an opinion, which neither exercise allows.

questions.stem: Which of these is a mistake in a résumé?
choices: keeping a keyword such as sommeil
questions.explanation: A résumé is written in the author's voice, so it never refers to the author. Keeping the order and the keywords and cutting anecdotes are exactly what it should do.

questions.stem: Which hyperonym best condenses "réseaux sociaux, jeux en ligne et vidéos en continu"?
questions.explanation: A hyperonym covers every item of the list: social networks, online games and streamed videos are all digital content. Each other choice names only one item.

questions.stem: Which phrase nominalises "parce qu'ils s'endorment plus tard"?
choices: à cause de s'endormir plus tard
questions.explanation: "En raison de" + noun keeps the neutral cause; the verb becomes a noun (l'endormissement) and the adverb an adjective (tardif). "Grâce à" introduces a good cause, which a later bedtime isn't; the other two are ungrammatical.

questions.stem: The text says: "Les chercheurs proposent deux explications possibles." Which reporting verb fits best?
questions.explanation: "Avancer" means to put forward a hypothesis, which is what the researchers do. "Déplorer" and "regretter" express regret; "prétendre" suggests doubt about the claim and takes que or an infinitive, not a noun here.

questions.stem: Which verb reports that an author regrets something?
questions.explanation: "Déplorer" (to deplore) reports the author's regret, as Dr Benali does: "Je déplore qu'on investisse …". "Souligner" is to stress, "exposer" to set out, "avancer" to put forward.

questions.stem: What is the plural of "le compte rendu"?
questions.explanation: Both words take an s: les comptes rendus (accounts that have been given).

questions.stem: Document 1 is 380 words long. About how long should a résumé of it be?
questions.explanation: A résumé usually takes about a quarter of the text: about 95 words for 380 (the lesson's model has 100). 380 words is no condensing at all; 40 words would lose the argument.

questions.stem: In paragraph 5 of document 1, why do the researchers refuse to blame screens outright?
choices: The study was too small to mean anything.
Their data show a link, not proof that screens cause the problem.
questions.explanation: "Leurs données établissent une corrélation, non une causalité": teenagers who already sleep badly may turn to their phones. The study followed 3,000 pupils, so size isn't the issue.

questions.stem: In paragraph 1 of document 2, what distinction does Dr Benali draw?
choices: between sport on Sundays and sport on weekdays
between working at home and at the office
between sitting too long and not exercising enough
questions.explanation: "Cette sédentarité est trop souvent confondue avec le manque d'activité physique. Ce sont pourtant deux choses distinctes": you can run three times a week and still be sedentary the rest of the time.

questions.stem: Which is the best reformulation of "Les adolescents qui utilisent un écran dans l'heure précédant le coucher s'endorment plus tard"?
choices: L'usage des écrans avant le coucher retarde l'endormissement des adolescents.
Les écrans empêchent les adolescents de dormir.
Les adolescents qui utilisent un écran dans l'heure avant le coucher s'endorment plus tard.
Les adolescents se couchent plus tard que les adultes.
questions.explanation: The good reformulation keeps the keywords (écrans, coucher, adolescents) and changes the structure (a noun subject, the verb retarder, the noun endormissement). "dans l''heure avant le coucher" is a copy with one word changed; "empêchent de dormir" distorts the claim; the comparison with adults says something else.

questions.stem: How does this app's editor count "l'homme"?
questions.explanation: The editor counts an elided word with the next as one word (and c'est-à-dire as one). Exam centres may count differently: follow the instructions on your paper.

questions.stem: Document 1 says the light of screens "retarderait" the secretion of melatonin. Which summary keeps the source's caution?
choices: La lumière des écrans bloque totalement la mélatonine.
La lumière des écrans retarde à coup sûr la mélatonine.
La lumière des écrans retarderait la sécrétion de mélatonine.
La lumière des écrans n'a aucun effet sur la mélatonine.
questions.explanation: The conditionnel marks a claim the article does not vouch for completely. A careful summary keeps it. "Bloque totalement" and "à coup sûr" overstate the claim; "aucun effet" contradicts it.

questions.stem: Type the plural of "le compte rendu": les ___
questions.explanation: Both words take an s: les comptes rendus.

questions.stem: Put the steps of Dr Benali's argument (document 2) in his order.
choices: sitting too long and not exercising are two different things
long sitting is harmful in itself
children sit most of the day too
overwork and poor sleep make it worse
employers and schools should invest in it
questions.explanation: The six paragraphs, in order: the distinction, the harm, children, the vicious circle with overwork, the good news, the call to employers and schools. A compte rendu follows this order.

questions.stem: Match each reporting verb to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Exposer sets out facts, avancer puts forward a hypothesis, soutenir maintains a thesis, souligner stresses a point, déplorer reports a regret. None of them means to deny (nier).

questions.stem: Which of these belong in a compte rendu of document 1? Select all that apply.
choices: the source and the author, named at the start
the anecdote about Léa, in full
the two explanations of the delay in falling asleep
the researchers' caution about cause and effect
questions.explanation: A compte rendu names its source, reports the steps of the argument (the two explanations) and keeps the author's caution. An illustrative anecdote is cut, and an opinion has no place.

questions.stem: Name the three exercises compared in this chart.

image.alt: A comparison chart with three numbered column headings and four rows. Sources: one text, one text, several documents. Voice: the author's, third person, neutral. Order: the author's, the author's, by ideas. Opening: no reference to the author; L'auteur montre que …; Les documents abordent ….

questions.explanation: Speaking as the author marks the résumé; the third person and "L'auteur montre que" the compte rendu; several documents organised by ideas the synthèse. An essai argumenté gives the writer's own opinion, which none of the three does.

questions.stem: Listen to the lecturer. What difference does she draw?

audio.text: Dans un résumé, vous écrivez à la place de l'auteur : vous gardez son ordre et ses proportions, mais vous ne dites jamais « l'auteur pense que ». Dans un compte rendu, au contraire, vous parlez de l'auteur à la troisième personne.

choices: A résumé is longer than a compte rendu.
A résumé changes the author's order; a compte rendu keeps it.
A compte rendu gives the writer's opinion; a résumé doesn't.
A résumé speaks as the author; a compte rendu speaks about the author.
questions.explanation: "Dans un résumé, vous écrivez à la place de l'auteur … Dans un compte rendu, au contraire, vous parlez de l'auteur à la troisième personne." Neither gives an opinion, and the résumé keeps the author's order.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio item. What do the authors of the study recommend?

audio.text: Selon une étude publiée ce matin, beaucoup d'adolescents dorment moins de huit heures par nuit en semaine. Les auteurs recommandent de couper les écrans une heure avant le coucher, mais refusent de parler d'interdiction.

choices: switching off screens an hour before bed, without a ban
banning phones from bedrooms by law
letting teenagers sleep in on weekdays
questions.explanation: "Les auteurs recommandent de couper les écrans une heure avant le coucher, mais refusent de parler d'interdiction."

questions.stem: Which plan suits a synthesis of the lesson's three documents?
choices: I. Document 1 II. Document 2 III. Document 3
I. Les atouts du numérique II. Ses risques III. Ses conditions
I. Ce que pensent les auteurs II. Ce que j'en pense
I. Résumé du document 1 II. Comparaison avec mon expérience
questions.explanation: A synthesis is planned by ideas, each part drawing on several documents. A plan document by document is a series of summaries, and any part about the writer's view or experience breaks the no-opinion rule.

questions.stem: Which sentence breaks the rules of the synthesis?
choices: Les pédiatres s'alarment de l'exposition précoce aux écrans.
Quant à l'association, elle insiste sur les inégalités.
Les pédiatres s'alarment, à juste titre, de l'exposition précoce aux écrans.
Les trois documents s'accordent à dire que l'outil ne suffit pas.
questions.explanation: "À juste titre" (rightly) is the writer's judgement. Reporting that the paediatricians are alarmed is neutral: it is their attitude, not the writer's.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ rapport de l'association, il insiste sur les inégalités."
questions.explanation: "Quant à" contracts with le into "quant au" (and with les into "quant aux"). "Rapport" is masculine singular, so "Quant au rapport".

questions.stem: Complete: "Les deux auteurs s'accordent ___ dire que l'outil ne suffit pas."
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is "s'accorder à dire que" (to agree in saying). "S'accorder sur" exists, but with a noun (s'accorder sur un point), not with dire.

questions.stem: How long is the DALF C1 synthesis in FEI's candidate manual (2022)?
questions.explanation: The manual gives 200 to 240 words for the synthesis; "at least 250 words" is the essay that follows. Formats change, so check FEI's current sample papers and your paper's instructions.

questions.stem: Which of these may a synthesis NOT include?
choices: an example you know from the news
a conclusion that answers the problématique
questions.explanation: Nothing from outside the documents, even a true example. Keywords may stay; naming the documents' genres and answering the problématique are part of the task.

questions.stem: Which is the best problématique for the lesson's corpus?
choices: Pourquoi les tablettes coûtent-elles si cher ?
À quelles conditions le numérique peut-il servir l'école ?
questions.explanation: All three documents agree that the tool alone is not enough and say on what terms it helps: that is the question they answer together. "Le numérique à l'école" is a topic, not a question; "Que dit le document 1 ?" concerns one document; prices are not discussed.

questions.stem: In paragraph 4 of document 2, what do the paediatricians accept?
choices: that pupils in collège and lycée must learn to use digital tools with judgement
banning digital tools from every class
questions.explanation: "Il ne demande pas pour autant de bannir le numérique des classes : au collège et au lycée … apprendre à se servir de ces outils avec discernement fait partie de l'éducation."

questions.stem: In paragraph 3 of document 3, what does the association point out about teenagers?
choices: They all lack a computer at home.
Many who are at ease on social media can't write an e-mail or file their documents.
They teach their parents to use the school's platform.
questions.explanation: "Beaucoup d'adolescents, très à l'aise sur les réseaux sociaux, ne savent ni rédiger un courriel, ni joindre un fichier, ni classer leurs documents": their ease hides unequal skills.

questions.stem: In "L'association rejoint les pédiatres sur ce point", what does "rejoint" mean?
questions.explanation: In a synthesis, "rejoindre quelqu'un sur un point" means to agree with them on it. "Meets up with" is its everyday meaning (Je te rejoins au café), which doesn't fit here.

questions.stem: What does "à l'instar de" mean?
questions.explanation: "À l'instar de la formatrice, l'association …": like the trainer, the association …. It is formal.

questions.stem: Which conclusion respects the rules of the synthesis?
choices: Loin de s'opposer, les documents dessinent un consensus prudent : le numérique n'est profitable qu'encadré.
Le document 3 est de loin le plus convaincant.
À mon avis, il faudrait interdire les tablettes à l'école maternelle.
Pour aller plus loin, il faudrait étudier ce qui se fait dans d'autres pays.
questions.explanation: The conclusion answers the problématique from the documents alone. The other choices give an opinion, judge a document or open the question with an idea of the writer's own.

questions.stem: Complete with a phrase meaning "for its part": "L'association, ___, réclame un accompagnement des familles."
questions.explanation: "Pour sa part" (formal) and "de son côté" both turn to another document; "quant à elle", after the subject, does the same. All change with the person: pour leur part, de leur côté, quant à elles.

questions.stem: Put the steps of the synthesis method in order.
choices: Read each document: source, genre, thesis
Write the introduction, the parts and the conclusion
questions.explanation: Reading gives the material, the grid shows how the documents relate, which gives the common question; the plan answers it; writing comes last but one, and counting and rereading last.

questions.stem: Match each phrase to what it does in a synthesis.
choices: shows one source following another's example
questions.explanation: These are the tools of confrontation. None gives an opinion: a synthesis has none.

questions.stem: Which sentences could appear in a synthesis of the lesson's corpus? Select all that apply.
choices: Selon la formatrice, les outils numériques adaptent les exercices au rythme de chacun.
Je trouve que la formatrice a raison.
Quant à l'association, elle souligne l'illectronisme de certains parents.
Comme chacun sait, les jeunes passent beaucoup trop de temps sur leur téléphone.
Les pédiatres, de leur côté, réclament un recentrage sur l'écrit et le jeu.
questions.explanation: The three right sentences report a document's idea and name its source. "Je trouve" is an opinion; "Comme chacun sait …" brings in a general claim from outside, with a judgement (beaucoup trop).

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this grille de lecture.

image.alt: A reading grid with column headings Doc 1, Doc 2 and Doc 3 and row headings atouts, risques (santé), inégalités and conditions. Marker 1 is on the Doc 3 heading; marker 2 on the right of the atouts row heading; marker 3 on the empty cell where the Doc 3 column meets the risques row; marker 4 at the start of the green conditions row, whose three cells read formation, recentrage, accompagnement.

choices: un document qui n'en dit rien
un point commun aux trois documents
questions.explanation: Documents go in columns and ideas in rows. An empty cell shows that a document is silent on that idea; a full row, here the conditions, is common ground. A grid holds neither quotations to copy nor the writer's opinion.

questions.stem: Listen to two teachers. According to the second, where does the candidate's opinion go?

audio.text: Une synthèse sans opinion, c'est frustrant pour les candidats. — Peut-être, mais c'est justement l'exercice : montrer qu'on a compris les autres avant de parler soi-même. — Et l'opinion, alors ? — Elle vient dans l'essai, juste après.

choices: nowhere: the DALF never asks for it
in the essay that follows the synthesis
in the conclusion of the synthesis
in the introduction of the synthesis
questions.explanation: "Et l'opinion, alors ? — Elle vient dans l'essai, juste après." The synthesis shows that you have understood others before you speak for yourself.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio item. What do the teachers regret?

audio.text: Une association d'enseignants a publié hier les résultats d'une enquête sur les usages numériques au collège. S'ils jugent les outils utiles, les professeurs interrogés regrettent presque tous de ne pas avoir été formés à s'en servir.

choices: that their pupils have no computers
that the tools are not useful
that they were never trained to use the tools
questions.explanation: "S'ils jugent les outils utiles, les professeurs interrogés regrettent presque tous de ne pas avoir été formés à s'en servir."

questions.stem: In FEI's candidate manual (2022), how long must the DALF C1 essay be?
questions.explanation: The manual asks for at least 250 words (an older sample paper said "about 250"); 200 to 240 words is the synthesis. Check the current sample papers and your paper's instructions.

questions.stem: Subject: "Pourquoi tant de salariés restent-ils au bureau sans y être utiles, et comment en sortir ?" Which plan does the lesson recommend?
questions.explanation: The subject asks you to explain a problem and solve it: constat, causes, conséquences, solutions. A dialectical plan suits a yes-or-no question; a comparative plan weighs two options.

questions.stem: Which plan does the lesson recommend for a yes-or-no question such as "Faut-il instaurer la semaine de quatre jours dans la fonction publique ?"
questions.explanation: A yes-or-no question calls for arguments for, arguments against and a nuanced answer: the dialectical plan (French B2, lesson 21).

questions.stem: Which sentence is a problématisation?
choices: Dans une première partie, nous verrons les atouts de la réforme.
De nos jours, le travail est très important.
Mais travailler quatre jours, est-ce travailler mieux, ou seulement plus vite ?
En somme, la réforme me paraît souhaitable.
questions.explanation: A problématisation turns the subject into a real question and shows why it is one. The other sentences announce a plan as a list, open with a vague truth, or conclude.

questions.stem: Which sentence announces the plan the way the lesson recommends?
choices: Je vais vous dire ce que je pense.
Dans une première partie je parlerai des atouts, dans une deuxième partie des limites.
Voici mon plan : un, les atouts ; deux, les limites.
Après en avoir rappelé les atouts, j'en examinerai les limites, avant de proposer des conditions de réussite.
questions.explanation: The lesson recommends announcing the parts in one flowing sentence. The list forms ("dans une première partie", "voici mon plan") are clumsy at C1, and "Je vais vous dire ce que je pense" announces nothing.

questions.stem: Which opening suits a formal letter to a mayor?
choices: Monsieur le Maire, Permettez-moi de vous faire part de quelques réserves.
Salut Monsieur le Maire, j'ai deux mots à vous dire.
Cher ami, je t'écris au sujet de ton projet.
Coucou ! Alors, ce projet de semaine de quatre jours ?
questions.explanation: A formal letter opens with "Monsieur le Maire," and a polite formula (permettez-moi de vous faire part de). The others use familiar greetings, tu, or a chat register.

questions.stem: In careful written French, complete: "La réforme me paraît souhaitable, à condition qu'elle ___ négociée."
questions.explanation: "À condition que" takes the subjunctive: qu'elle soit négociée. The indicative and the conditionnel are not used after it in standard French.

questions.stem: What does "J'abonde dans le sens des syndicats" mean?
choices: I partly disagree with the unions.
I agree wholeheartedly with the unions.
I am reporting what the unions say.
questions.explanation: "Abonder dans le sens de quelqu'un" is to agree wholeheartedly with them.

questions.stem: Why does the model essay mention colleagues at reception and in maintenance?
choices: to show that the reform is already in place for them
to show that they work fewer hours
to show that the reform might not benefit all staff
questions.explanation: They "doivent être présents chaque jour" and risk being "laissés pour compte": the subject asked whether the four-day week is progress for all, and these colleagues test that "all".

questions.stem: Since when has France's right to disconnect (droit à la déconnexion) been in force?
questions.explanation: It came from a law of 8 August 2016 and took effect on 1 January 2017. 1998 and 2000 are the dates of the lois Aubry on the 35-hour week.

questions.stem: What does "le présentéisme" mean?
choices: staying at work to be seen rather than to be useful
presenting a project to the management
questions.explanation: Presenteeism is being at work (late, or ill) to be seen. Being often absent is l'absentéisme.

questions.stem: Which is a mistake in an essay's conclusion?
choices: recalling the conditions of your answer
questions.explanation: A conclusion answers and may open; a new argument belongs in the body, where it can be developed.

questions.stem: Type the French noun for "a counter-proposal", with its article.
questions.explanation: La contre-proposition (plural les contre-propositions), as in "Les syndicats ont avancé une contre-proposition".

questions.stem: Put the parts of an analytical plan in order.
questions.explanation: What is happening, why, what it leads to, and what to do about it. The solutions carry the writer's position.

questions.stem: Match each plan to the kind of subject it suits.
choices: a problem to explain and solve
questions.explanation: The subject decides the plan: yes or no → dialectical; a problem → analytical; two options → comparative, aspect by aspect. An argued essay doesn't tell a story.

questions.stem: Which of these are on the lesson's self-check list? Select all that apply.
choices: moods after à condition que, pour que, bien que
a register consistent with the form
the word count written at the end
questions.explanation: The self-check covers task, plan, moods, agreement, connectors, register and length. Copying the documents is a mistake, not a check.

questions.stem: Name the three numbered moves of this introduction.

image.alt: Three coloured blocks of an introduction, each with a numbered marker on its left. 1: Lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi… et le vendredi pour soi. 2: Mais travailler quatre jours, est-ce travailler mieux, ou seulement plus vite ? 3: Après en avoir rappelé les atouts, j'en examinerai les limites, avant de proposer des conditions de réussite.

questions.explanation: The scene opens (accroche), the question frames the subject (problématisation), and the last sentence announces the parts (annonce du plan). An ouverture ends a conclusion; a transition links two parts.

questions.stem: Listen to two colleagues. Why is the second one against the four-day week?

audio.text: Quatre jours de travail, trois jours de repos : franchement, qui dirait non ? — Moi. Dix heures par jour, avec deux enfants à aller chercher à l'école, ce n'est pas un progrès. — Personne ne t'obligerait à le faire. — Si la règle est la même pour tout le monde, si.

choices: The first speaker would not be allowed to choose.
There would be too many meetings.
Long days would be hard to combine with picking up the children from school.
questions.explanation: "Dix heures par jour, avec deux enfants à aller chercher à l'école, ce n'est pas un progrès." The speaker also fears that the same rule would apply to everyone.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio item. What must the employer do if there is no agreement?

audio.text: Depuis le premier janvier 2017, les entreprises françaises qui négocient chaque année avec les syndicats doivent aborder le droit à la déconnexion. À défaut d'accord, l'employeur doit rédiger une charte.

questions.explanation: "À défaut d'accord, l'employeur doit rédiger une charte." Nothing is said about fines or a fixed hour.

questions.stem: What is "le libellé" of a dissertation?
choices: the third part of the plan
questions.explanation: Le libellé is the wording of the subject, often a quotation and an instruction. Underline and define every keyword before planning.

questions.stem: What is "le dépassement" in a dissertation plan?
choices: a summary of parts I and II
writing more than the word limit
a final part that goes beyond the opposition by changing the question
an example taken from a novel
questions.explanation: The dépassement does not average the first two parts; it changes the question (in Example 1, from "identify or not?" to "what does moving between the two give us?").

questions.stem: For the 2026 session, what do candidates in the general stream choose between in the written épreuve anticipée de français?
choices: a contraction de texte and a commentaire
questions.explanation: The general stream chooses between a commentaire and a dissertation. The contraction de texte followed by an essay is the alternative in the technological stream; the synthesis and essay are DALF tasks. Check eduscol for later sessions.

questions.stem: How long is the written épreuve anticipée de français, as defined for the 2026 session?
questions.explanation: Four hours, for both streams. Two hours thirty is the DALF C1 writing paper.

questions.stem: Which could be a reading axis for the Brévannes passage?
choices: la mémoire plus forte que le réel
le passé simple est réservé à la lecture
questions.explanation: A reading axis is a line of interpretation proved by observations: the final reversal ("plus vrai que celui qu'elle avait devant elle") makes memory stronger than reality. A biography, a grammar rule or a summary is not an interpretation.

questions.stem: In the Brévannes passage, which tense shows changes already completed ("on avait goudronné", "avaient été repeints")?
questions.explanation: Avoir or être in the imparfait + a past participle: the plus-que-parfait, for what had happened before she came back.

questions.stem: Which is good practice in a commentaire de texte?
choices: quoting a few words and saying what they do
questions.explanation: A commentaire shows how the form makes the meaning: brief quotation, then analysis. Paraphrase, a bare list of devices and ignoring the paratexte are the classic mistakes.

questions.stem: In Example 1, why is Madame Bovary used in part II?
choices: because Emma tries to live the novels she reads, and the novel shows the danger of that identification
because the novel is set in Paris
because it is a conte philosophique
because Emma is a student in Paris
questions.explanation: Emma reads romantic novels and tries to live them: Flaubert's novel keeps its reader at a distance from that very identification, which limits the libellé's claim. The conte philosophique is Candide.

questions.stem: Which French word names a doctoral thesis?
questions.explanation: La thèse is a doctoral thesis; la dissertation is a school or university essay.

questions.stem: Type the French noun for the wording of an exam subject, with its article.
questions.explanation: Le libellé (plural les libellés): Lisez le libellé mot à mot.

questions.stem: Match each French exercise to its description.
choices: an argued answer to a question, with examples from works
a written analysis of one passage by reading axes
an oral analysis that follows a passage line by line
questions.explanation: The synthesis of several documents is the DALF task of lesson 19, not one of these school exercises.

questions.stem: Put the moves of a dissertation introduction in order.
questions.explanation: Open, give the subject, analyse its keywords, bring out the problématique, announce the plan: each step prepares the next.

questions.stem: Which of these belong to the paratexte of a passage? Select all that apply.
choices: the third sentence of the passage
questions.explanation: The paratexte is everything around the text that situates it: title, author, date, chapter heading, preface, notes. A sentence of the passage is the text itself; a reading axis is your analysis.

questions.stem: What is the thesis of « Le temps qu'il faut »?
choices: Speed is always harmful and should be resisted.
The slow movements have found the answer.
What we lack is not time but the freedom to choose the right pace for each thing.
We should listen to podcasts at normal speed.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 11: "non pas du temps, mais le droit de choisir l'allure qui convient à chaque chose". Paragraph 10 concedes the benefits of speed, and paragraph 6 criticises the slow movements; the podcasts are an illustration.

questions.stem: In paragraph 1, why does the author mention listening to podcasts at a higher speed?
choices: to recommend it to the reader
to show that podcasts are too long
to illustrate the paradox of saving time and still lacking it
questions.explanation: The twenty minutes "gained" each day went nobody knows where: the anecdote leads to the paradox of the age, many time-saving tools and the feeling of having no time.

questions.stem: In paragraph 2, how does technical acceleration feed the acceleration of the pace of life?
choices: Time saved by machines is spent at once on new tasks.
People refuse to use new machines.
questions.explanation: "Le temps gagné grâce aux machines est aussitôt réinvesti dans de nouvelles tâches", as e-mail brought a hundred messages a day.

questions.stem: Paragraph 3: « Notre impatience n'est qu'un trait de caractère. » True or false, and why?
choices: True: « L'attente … est devenue une anomalie. »
False: « elle est le produit d'un environnement qui a fait disparaître les délais ».
True: « Tout, désormais, doit arriver tout de suite. »
questions.explanation: The text says our impatience is "pas seulement un trait de caractère" but the product of an environment without delays, so the statement is false, and that is the sentence that proves it. The two "true" quotations describe the environment, not a trait of character.

questions.stem: In paragraph 5, what does the watchmaker's question suggest?
choices: that the grandfather should find another watchmaker
that the watch could not be repaired
that a repair done properly matters more than one done fast
questions.explanation: "Une montre réparée vite ou une montre qui marche": the answer is implied, and the watch then worked for twenty years.

questions.stem: In paragraph 6, what ambiguity does the author see in the slow movements?
choices: They are too recent to judge.
Sold as a product, slowness may become a luxury for those with time and money.
questions.explanation: "Devenue argument publicitaire, la lenteur se vend cher … et risque de n'être plus que le luxe de ceux qui ont du temps, c'est-à-dire, bien souvent, de l'argent."

questions.stem: Which tense are "posa", "regarda" and "demanda" in paragraph 5?
questions.explanation: They are passés simples, the past tense of written narration (recognition only): in speech, il a posé, il a regardé, il a demandé.

questions.stem: Paragraph 10 begins "Gardons-nous cependant d'opposer naïvement …". What is its role?
choices: it concedes the benefits of speed to nuance the argument
it gives a new example of slowness
questions.explanation: The paragraph grants that speed saves lives and that imposed slowness is no art of living, then reframes the issue as control of the rhythm. The thesis comes in paragraph 11.

questions.stem: Short answer: which Italian musical term does the author borrow in paragraph 11? (two words)
questions.explanation: Le tempo giusto: the right tempo, neither too fast nor too slow, the one that suits the work.

questions.stem: Type the French noun for aimless strolling, with its article (paragraph 7).
questions.explanation: La flânerie; the verb is flâner and the person le flâneur, la flâneuse.

questions.stem: Match each paragraph of the essay to its content.
choices: the slow movements and their ambiguity
a recipe for a slow meal
questions.explanation: Mapping the plan paragraph by paragraph is the second pass of a long reading. The essay mentions Slow Food but gives no recipe.

questions.stem: Which words does the author use to soften or distance a claim? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Dit-on" (paragraph 9) distances the author from a figure; "peut-être" and "sans doute" (paragraph 11) soften the conclusion. "Précisément" stresses, and "désormais" means from now on: neither hedges.

questions.stem: What does the last sentence of paragraph 9 imply ("une activité qui masque mal leur vacuité")?
choices: that activity is always good for us
that our busy days are often empty of real meaning
that the author dislikes his job
questions.explanation: The author never says "we waste our lives", but "masquer mal leur vacuité" suggests that busyness hides, badly, an emptiness. The text says nothing of the author's job.

questions.stem: According to the lesson, what is the exposé in the DALF C1 speaking test?
choices: a talk that defends your own answer to a question raised by the documents
a summary of the documents in the order they were given
a text prepared at home and read aloud
a free conversation with the jury on any subject
questions.explanation: The exposé starts from the documents but defends the candidate's own argued answer to a problématique, in an announced plan. Summarising the documents is the commonest mistake; nothing is prepared at home, and the discussion with the jury comes after the exposé, on the same subject.

questions.stem: Two documents: free entry raised a museum's attendance, but mostly among people who already visit museums; an outreach worker says free access is not enough. Which is a problématique?
choices: Le musée de Valcourt a instauré l'entrée libre.
La gratuité suffit-elle à démocratiser l'accès à la culture ?
La médiatrice culturelle travaille dans les quartiers.
questions.explanation: A problématique is a real question with more than one defensible answer, built from the tension between the documents (more visitors, but not new ones). The other three are a fact, a title and a detail: you can't argue for or against them.

questions.stem: Why does the lesson advise against giving one part of the exposé to each document?
choices: The jury requires exactly three parts.
It turns the talk into a summary instead of an argument.
Documents must never be mentioned in an exposé.
It always makes the talk too short.
questions.explanation: The plan follows the question, not the documents: a part per document is a summary. Documents are mentioned (briefly, in the introduction and as examples), and the number of parts depends on the question, two or three.

questions.stem: Which kind of accroche is "On n'a jamais autant parlé d'accès à la culture, et les musées n'ont jamais autant accueilli les mêmes visiteurs."?
questions.explanation: Two facts that seem to contradict each other (more talk of access, the same visitors) make a paradox. There is no question, no scene with characters and no definition.

questions.stem: Complete the signpost that opens the second part: "Après ces avantages, ___ aux limites de la gratuité."
questions.explanation: En venir à (B2) is to come to a point: "j'en viens aux limites". "Je viens aux limites" drops the en and sounds like physical movement; "j'en vais" is not French; "J'y viens" (I'm coming to that) is used on its own, without a complement with à.

questions.stem: In "Mon exposé s'articulera en deux temps", what does "s'articulera" mean?
choices: will be linked to the documents
questions.explanation: S'articuler en, autour de = to be structured in, around. L'articulation is also clear pronunciation, but the verb here describes the plan; nothing is said about the documents or a delay.

questions.stem: What does "d'entrée de jeu" mean in "D'entrée de jeu, je voudrais préciser ma position"?
questions.explanation: D'entrée de jeu = right from the start. The words entrée and jeu are not meant literally here; "in the end" is the opposite.

questions.stem: According to the lesson, what should you write out in full on your preparation sheet?
choices: your first two sentences and your conclusion
the key sentences of each document
questions.explanation: Speak from keywords, so the talk doesn't sound read, but write out the opening and the conclusion, the moments nerves take away. A full text can't be written in an hour and sounds flat; copying the documents leads to a summary.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "She gave a talk on the museum"?
choices: Elle a fait un exposé sur le musée.
Elle a exposé sur le musée.
Elle a donné une exposition sur le musée.
questions.explanation: To give a talk is faire un exposé. Exposer is to exhibit (un peintre expose ses toiles) or to set out (exposer ses idées), so the other verb sentences don't mean giving a talk, and une exposition is an exhibition.

questions.stem: Since April 2009, who has had free access to the permanent collections of France's national museums and monuments?
choices: young visitors under 26 from the European Union
questions.explanation: The free admission introduced on 4 April 2009 covers visitors under 26 from the EU (first EU nationals, then, after a July 2009 decision, every young long-term resident of the EU), along with primary and secondary teachers. It is not universal, and it is not limited to French pupils or the elderly.

questions.stem: What is "le mécénat"?
choices: private funding of the arts by companies or individuals
questions.explanation: Le mécénat is sponsorship by mécènes (patrons). State funding is la politique culturelle's budget, the permanent collection is la collection permanente, and exhibition design is la scénographie.

questions.stem: What does "la conservatrice du musée" mean?
questions.explanation: La conservatrice (masculine le conservateur) is a curator. The adjective conservateur, conservatrice also means politically conservative, but "du musée" makes it the job. A sponsor is un or une mécène.

questions.stem: Which advice about pace (le débit) does the lesson give?
choices: Speak as fast as you can to fit more in.
Read your notes aloud word for word.
Avoid every pause: pauses sound like hesitation.
Speak calmly, a little slower than in conversation.
questions.explanation: A calm, steady débit helps the jury follow; nervous speakers speed up. Reading kills eye contact, and a pause before a new part works like a paragraph break: it is better than euh.

questions.stem: What does "en guise de" mean in "En guise de conclusion, je poserai une question"?
questions.explanation: En guise de + noun without an article = by way of, as: en guise d'introduction, en guise d'exemple. The other meanings would be malgré, en plus de and bien après.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio item. What worries the museum's friends' association?

audio.text: Le musée des Beaux-Arts de Lorvel annonce l'entrée libre pour tous le premier dimanche de chaque mois. La conservatrice espère attirer des familles qui ne viennent jamais. Mais l'association des amis du musée s'inquiète : sans médiation, dit-elle, ce seront toujours les mêmes visiteurs.

choices: that without outreach, the same visitors will keep coming
that the museum will lose too much money
that families will stop coming on Sundays
that the curator will leave the museum
questions.explanation: "Sans médiation, dit-elle, ce seront toujours les mêmes visiteurs." Money, families staying away and the curator leaving are not mentioned; the curator hopes to attract families who never come.

questions.stem: Listen to the start of a talk. What will the second part be about?

audio.text: Bonjour à tous. Mon exposé s'articulera en deux temps. Je commencerai par ce que le mécénat apporte aux institutions culturelles, avant d'en venir aux risques qu'il comporte pour leur indépendance.

choices: what sponsorship brings to cultural institutions
the history of arts sponsorship in France
the risks sponsorship poses to institutions' independence
how a museum can find new sponsors
questions.explanation: The plan is announced with "Je commencerai par … avant d'en venir à …": first what sponsorship brings, then "les risques qu'il comporte pour leur indépendance". History and finding sponsors are not mentioned.

questions.stem: Type the missing words of the transition that shows the next part follows from the last (a pronoun and a verb): "Ces limites sont réelles. Ce qui ___ à ma deuxième partie : la médiation."
questions.explanation: The lesson's phrase is "Ce qui m'amène à …" (which brings me to …); "nous amène" and the verbs conduire and mener work the same way. It shows that the new part follows from the last, unlike a plain "J'en viens à …".

questions.stem: Put the sentences of this exposé introduction in order.
choices: On n'a jamais autant parlé d'accès à la culture, et pourtant les musées accueillent souvent les mêmes visiteurs.
À Valcourt, par exemple, l'entrée libre a fait grimper la fréquentation, mais pas auprès de nouveaux publics.
D'où la question : la gratuité suffit-elle à démocratiser l'accès à la culture ?
Je défendrai l'idée qu'elle est nécessaire, mais insuffisante.
Dans un premier temps, je montrerai ce qu'elle permet ; dans un second temps, j'en viendrai à ses limites.
questions.explanation: The model order: the accroche (a paradox), the documents ("par exemple" illustrates the paradox), the problématique introduced by "D'où", the position ("elle" needs "la gratuité" from the question), then the announced plan.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
choices: the running order of a talk
questions.explanation: La gestuelle: gestures, hands, face. L'élocution: clarity and flow of speech. Le déroulé: the order of the parts (your one-sheet plan). La scénographie: the layout, light and route of an exhibition, or stage design. No word here means a permanent collection.

questions.stem: Which of these belong in the introduction of an exposé? Select all that apply.
choices: a new argument kept for the end
questions.explanation: The introduction gives the accroche, the documents in a sentence or two, the problématique, your position and the plan. Arguments come in the parts, and the conclusion at the end: announcing it early leaves nothing to say.

questions.stem: Name the numbered stations of this exposé.

image.alt: A path of six numbered stations from top to bottom, each with a box holding a phrase: 1 "On n'a jamais autant parlé d'accès à la culture…"; 2 "D'où la question… Je commencerai par… avant d'en venir à…"; 3 "Dans un premier temps…"; 4 "Ce qui m'amène à…"; 5 "J'en viens à…"; 6 "Pour conclure… Je vous remercie de votre attention." A dashed arrow labelled fil rouge runs from the last station back to the first.

questions.explanation: The phrase in each box gives it away: a paradox as accroche; "D'où la question" and the announced plan; "Dans un premier temps" opens part one; "Ce qui m'amène à" is the transition; "J'en viens à" opens part two; "Pour conclure" and the thanks end the talk. No station is a digression or an objection.

questions.stem: Which is the most diplomatic way to disagree with an examiner?
choices: Je ne suis pas certain de vous suivre sur ce point.
questions.explanation: Presenting the disagreement as your own difficulty in following is diplomatic. "Vous avez tort" and "C'est faux" are blunt verdicts, and "N'importe quoi" is informal and rude.

questions.stem: What does "Sauf votre respect, …" do?
choices: It thanks the other person for listening.
It softens a blunt remark that comes next, like "with all due respect".
It asks permission to stop talking.
questions.explanation: Sauf votre respect is a set formula that softens a blunt remark or a firm disagreement that follows. The Académie's dictionary marks it as familiar, and it can sound sharp; with a jury, avec tout le respect que je vous dois or je me permettrai de nuancer is safer. It is not an apology, a thank-you or a request to stop.

questions.stem: In careful French, complete: "Je vous accorde que le coût ___ élevé ; il n'en reste pas moins que la mesure est nécessaire."
questions.explanation: Accorder que in the sense of conceding presents the point as true, so it takes the indicative: "je vous accorde que le coût est élevé". The subjunctive soit is not used here, and the infinitive and participle are ungrammatical after que.

questions.stem: What follows "Encore faut-il que …" (still, it would have to be true that …)?
questions.explanation: Falloir que takes the subjunctive, with or without the inversion after encore: "Encore faut-il que les règles soient appliquées."

questions.stem: Which sentence reframes the debate?
choices: Si je vous comprends bien, vous dites que l'État contrôle tout.
Je vous accorde que le financement pose problème.
La vraie question n'est pas de savoir qui paie, mais qui décide.
questions.explanation: Reframing (recadrer) moves the debate to the question that matters: "la vraie question n'est pas … mais …". The others ask for clarification, concede a point and hold the floor.

questions.stem: "Vous dites cela parce que vous travaillez pour la télévision publique." Which fallacy is this?
questions.explanation: The speaker answers the other person's supposed motive instead of the argument: faire un procès d'intention. No authority is cited, no two options are forced, and nothing is generalised from one case.

questions.stem: "Un prix Nobel l'a dit, donc c'est vrai." Which fallacy is this?
questions.explanation: The authority replaces the reasons: l'argument d'autorité. A straw man distorts the other side's view, a false dilemma forces two options, an attack on motives targets intentions.

questions.stem: "Soit on garde la redevance, soit l'audiovisuel public disparaît." Which fallacy is this?
questions.explanation: Only two options are offered when others exist (other ways of funding, for example): le faux dilemme. A polite answer: "Il me semble qu'il existe d'autres options."

questions.stem: A says: "Public broadcasting needs independent management." B replies: "So you want to fund it with no control at all?" What is B doing?
choices: attributing to A a more extreme view than A holds
agreeing with A and adding a condition
changing the subject to the licence fee
questions.explanation: B's rephrasing looks like a clarification but distorts A's view to make it easier to attack: the straw man. The answer is "Ce n'est pas ce que j'ai dit" and a restatement.

questions.stem: What does "Ce reportage est partial" mean?
questions.explanation: Partial means biased; "incomplete" is partiel (une réponse partielle). "Partly true" would be en partie vrai, and "party-political" partisan.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ces commentateurs sont ___."
questions.explanation: Adjectives in -al usually make their masculine plural in -aux: impartial → impartiaux, partial → partiaux. Impartiales is feminine, and the other two forms don't exist.

questions.stem: What does "botter en touche" mean?
choices: to throw someone out of the debate
questions.explanation: From rugby (kicking the ball out of play), informal: to avoid answering. The jury notices at once; the lesson suggests buying a second and answering part of the question instead.

questions.stem: According to the lesson, what is the best way to handle a question you can't fully answer?
choices: Move to another subject without answering.
Invent a figure so as to sound sure.
Say it is a tricky question, answer the part you can, then bring it back to your position.
questions.explanation: Buy a second (C'est une question délicate), answer honestly what you can (Je n'ai pas de chiffres précis, mais …) and return to your position. Dodging, refusing and inventing figures all cost more than a partial answer.

questions.stem: What does "Une auditrice a interpellé le ministre sur la redevance" mean?
choices: A listener thanked the minister for the licence fee.
A listener challenged the minister directly about the licence fee.
A listener ignored the minister's remarks on the licence fee.
A listener wrote to the minister about the licence fee.
questions.explanation: Interpeller quelqu'un is to address or question them directly, often to challenge them. (It can also mean to detain for questioning, but that is the police's job, not a listener's.)

questions.stem: Listen to the exchange. What does the second speaker concede?

audio.text: Une chaîne publique, c'est forcément la voix du gouvernement. — Je me permettrai de nuancer : les journalistes y sont indépendants, et la loi les protège. — Indépendants ? Vous plaisantez ! — Je vous accorde que la nomination des dirigeants pose question. Il n'en reste pas moins que les rédactions travaillent librement.

choices: that the appointment of managers raises questions
that a public channel is the government's voice
that the law doesn't protect journalists
questions.explanation: "Je vous accorde que la nomination des dirigeants pose question", then the turn: "Il n'en reste pas moins que les rédactions travaillent librement." The speaker rejects the other three claims.

questions.stem: Listen to the end of the debate. What does the moderator do?

audio.text: Merci à tous les deux. Je ne trancherai pas ce soir, mais je retiens un terrain d'entente : vous voulez tous deux une information fiable. Nous en reparlerons la semaine prochaine.

choices: She sides with the first guest.
She announces that the programme is ending for good.
She doesn't settle the debate but points out common ground.
She asks the guests to apologise to each other.
questions.explanation: "Je ne trancherai pas ce soir, mais je retiens un terrain d'entente": she won't decide, and notes what both guests share. The programme continues next week.

questions.stem: Type the missing verb: "Je ne suis pas certain de vous ___ sur ce point." (I'm not sure I follow you on this point.)
questions.explanation: Suivre quelqu'un = to follow someone's reasoning: "Je ne suis pas certain de vous suivre." The disagreement is presented as your difficulty, which makes it diplomatic.

questions.stem: Put this answer to an examiner in order.
choices: Si je vous comprends bien, vous estimez qu'une chaîne publique ne peut pas être impartiale.
Je vous accorde que son financement crée un risque.
Il n'en reste pas moins que ce risque peut être limité.
C'est pourquoi la vraie question est de savoir qui nomme les dirigeants.
questions.explanation: Clarify first (the restatement introduces "une chaîne publique"), then concede ("son financement" refers back to the channel), then turn the point ("ce risque" refers back to the concession), and finally reframe, which follows from the turn ("C'est pourquoi").

questions.stem: Match each fallacy to its example.
choices: Un expert l'a dit, donc c'est vrai.
Vous dites ça pour protéger votre emploi.
Soit la redevance, soit la fin du service public.
Un reportage était orienté, donc tous le sont.
Je vous accorde que c'est cher.
questions.explanation: Authority instead of reasons; supposed motives instead of the argument; two options when there are more; one case turned into a rule. "Je vous accorde que c'est cher" is a concession, not a fallacy.

questions.stem: Which of these ask for clarification or rephrase the question? Select all that apply.
choices: Si je vous comprends bien, vous me demandez si …
questions.explanation: The three questions check or restate what was asked, which shows you are listening and gives you a few seconds; FEI's manual says asking for a rephrase is acceptable. "Sauf votre respect" introduces a blunt remark, and "J'y viens" holds the floor.

questions.stem: Name the numbered moves in this chart.

image.alt: An objection in the centre, "Une chaîne publique ne peut pas être impartiale", with arrows to four numbered boxes: 1 top left, "Je vous accorde que…"; 2 top right, "Il n'en reste pas moins que…"; 3 bottom left, "La vraie question est…"; 4 bottom right, "Qu'entendez-vous par… ?".

questions.explanation: Je vous accorde que = concede; il n'en reste pas moins que = turn the point against the objection; la vraie question est = reframe; qu'entendez-vous par = ask for clarification. None of the phrases dodges or interrupts.

questions.stem: In the current format described by FEI's candidate manual, how many times do you hear the long document of the DALF C1 listening paper?
questions.explanation: The long document (an interview, a lecture) is heard twice; the short radio documents of the second exercise are heard once. Check the instructions on the day.

questions.stem: What does a lecturer mean by "J'ouvre une parenthèse"?
questions.explanation: Ouvrir une parenthèse = to make a brief aside; "je referme la parenthèse" ends it. In notes, put brackets round the aside: questions rarely test it.

questions.stem: A lecturer says "j'y reviendrai". What should you do?
choices: ignore it: it is only an aside
note the point and watch for its return
stop taking notes until the end
questions.explanation: J'y reviendrai is a promise to come back to the point later: mark it (a ? or "→ plus tard") and tick it when it returns, as the lecture's §6 does with "comme promis".

questions.stem: Which note-taking symbol means "increases"?
questions.explanation: ↗ = increases (↘ = decreases). ≠ = different from, → = leads to, and cf. = see, compare.

questions.stem: In a student's notes, what does "relire ≠ s'interroger" mean?
choices: See the part on testing yourself.
Rereading is not the same as testing yourself.
questions.explanation: ≠ marks a difference or a contrast. → would be "leads to", = "is the same as", and cf. "see".

questions.stem: What does "pour faire court" announce?
questions.explanation: Pour faire court (to cut a long story short) introduces the speaker's summary, often the sentence a question will test. Digressions open with j'ouvre une parenthèse, examples with prenons le cas de.

questions.stem: "Ce qu'on appelle, parfois à tort, le multitâche." What is the speaker's stance on the word "multitâche"?
choices: She is quoting an official definition.
questions.explanation: "Parfois à tort" (sometimes wrongly) distances the speaker from the term: what we call multitasking is, she says, fast switching. Distancing words like this are a key to a speaker's view.

questions.stem: Which is correct?
questions.explanation: L'hémisphère is masculine, so un and the masculine adjective: un hémisphère entier, l'hémisphère gauche.

questions.stem: According to the lecture, about how many items can working memory hold at once?
questions.explanation: The lecture cites a 2001 review by Nelson Cowan: about four items at once. That is why too much new information at once overloads it (la charge cognitive).

questions.stem: What does the lecture say about multitasking?
choices: The brain can do two thinking tasks at once at no cost.
For tasks that need thought, the brain switches between them, and each switch costs time and adds errors.
questions.explanation: "Le cerveau ne fait pas deux choses à la fois : il passe très vite de l'une à l'autre, et chaque changement coûte du temps et augmente les erreurs." Notifications are stimuli that distract, and sustained attention wears out.

questions.stem: What did the 2006 experiment by Roediger and Karpicke find, as the lecture reports it?
choices: Students who reread a text remembered it better a week later.
Students who recalled a text from memory remembered it better a week later than students who reread it.
Recalling and rereading gave the same results a week later.
The rereaders expected to remember less than the others.
questions.explanation: Recalling (testing yourself) beat rereading a week later, even though the rereaders expected to remember more: the feeling of mastery that rereading gives is misleading.

questions.stem: What is "le sommaire" of a lecture?
choices: the summary judgement of the jury
its contents, the outline of the talk
questions.explanation: Le sommaire is the contents page of a report or magazine, or the outline of a talk: copy it, because it is the plan of your notes. As an adjective, sommaire means brief.

questions.stem: Listen to the start of the lecture. What will the lecturer deal with last?

audio.text: Ce soir, je commencerai par quelques mots sur le cerveau lui-même ; j'aborderai ensuite trois questions : la mémoire de travail, l'attention, et le sommeil. Je terminerai par des conseils pratiques, mais j'y reviendrai.

questions.explanation: "Je terminerai par des conseils pratiques, mais j'y reviendrai": the advice comes last, after the brain, working memory, attention and sleep.

questions.stem: Listen to the aside. What does it say?

audio.text: J'ouvre une parenthèse : vous avez sans doute entendu dire qu'on n'utiliserait que dix pour cent de son cerveau. C'est un mythe. Je referme la parenthèse.

choices: We really do use only 10% of our brain.
The idea that we use only 10% of our brain is a myth.
Ten per cent of our neurons die every year.
The brain stops changing in adulthood.
questions.explanation: "On n'utiliserait que dix pour cent de son cerveau. C'est un mythe." The conditionnel reports a claim the speaker rejects. Dying neurons and adulthood are not mentioned here.

questions.stem: Listen to the part on sleep. What conclusion does the lecturer draw?

audio.text: La nuit, le cerveau ne se contente pas de se reposer. Pendant le sommeil, les souvenirs de la journée sont réactivés et consolidés. Réviser toute la nuit avant un examen est donc un mauvais calcul.

choices: Revising all night before an exam is a bad idea.
It is best to revise during the night.
The brain rests completely at night.
questions.explanation: Memories are reactivated and consolidated during sleep, "Réviser toute la nuit avant un examen est donc un mauvais calcul." The brain does not simply rest.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the lecturer's stance on learning styles?

audio.text: On vous dira que chacun aurait un style d'apprentissage, visuel ou auditif. C'est une idée séduisante, mais les études qui l'ont testée ne la confirment pas.

choices: She recommends teaching each pupil in their own style.
She says most people are visual learners.
She rejects the idea: attractive, but not supported by the studies.
She says the question hasn't been studied.
questions.explanation: The conditionnel "chacun aurait" reports a claim; "séduisante, mais les études … ne la confirment pas" rejects it.

questions.stem: In French notes, "qqch" stands for ___.
questions.explanation: qqch = quelque chose, qqn = quelqu'un. Other common ones: tjrs (toujours), bcp (beaucoup), gvt (gouvernement), pb (problème).

questions.stem: Put the parts of the lecture in the order the lecturer announces them.
questions.explanation: §1: "Je commencerai par quelques mots sur le cerveau lui-même ; j'aborderai ensuite trois questions : la mémoire de travail, l'attention, et le sommeil. Je terminerai par des conseils pratiques."

questions.stem: Match each note-taking symbol to its meaning.
questions.explanation: → links a cause to its effect, ≠ marks a contrast, ↗ a rise (↘ is the fall, the extra answer), and cf. sends you to another point.

questions.stem: Which of these are signposts a lecturer uses to show the structure of a talk? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Signposts (marqueurs de structuration) announce, postpone or close parts of the talk. La charge cognitive and le cortex are topic words from the lecture.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts.

image.alt: A simplified cross-section of the brain: two halves separated by a groove from the top, each with a shaded outer layer; marker 1 sits on one of the halves and marker 2 on the shaded outer layer. To the right, an inset shows two nerve cells; marker 3 sits on the first cell's round body and marker 4 on the small gap where a long fibre from the first meets the branches of the second.

questions.explanation: Each half of the brain is a hemisphere; its outer layer is the cortex; a nerve cell is a neuron, and the junction where one neuron passes signals to another is a synapse. The cerebellum (le cervelet) isn't drawn, and working memory is a function, not a part you can point to.

questions.stem: Where does C1 stand among the CEFR levels?
choices: the lower of the two proficient-user levels
the top level of the scale
questions.explanation: A1–A2 are basic users, B1–B2 independent users, C1–C2 proficient users; C1 is the lower of the last two. B2 is the upper independent level, C2 the top.

questions.stem: In the current format, according to FEI's candidate manual, what does the DALF C1 writing paper involve?
choices: 50 minutes for a summary of one text
2 h 30 for a synthesis of documents and an argued essay
questions.explanation: Production écrite: 2 h 30 for a synthesis (200 to 240 words in the manual) and an essay (at least 250 words). One essay in 1 hour is the DELF B2; 50 minutes is the reading paper; 4 hours is all the collective papers together.

questions.stem: A candidate scores 20, 20 and 20 out of 25 in three parts and 4 out of 25 in the fourth. What is the result?
choices: fail: a mark below 5/25 in any part is eliminatory
fail, because the total is below 50
questions.explanation: The pass rule has two conditions: 50/100 overall and at least 5/25 in every part. The total, 64, is enough, but 4/25 is a note éliminatoire, so the diploma is not awarded.

questions.stem: What is "le seuil de réussite"?
choices: the door of the exam room
the first paper of the day
the time limit of a paper
questions.explanation: Le seuil (B2) is a threshold; le seuil de réussite is the mark you must reach to pass, 50/100 at the DALF.

questions.stem: Why do some books and centre pages mention a choice between "lettres et sciences humaines" and "sciences"?
choices: Candidates must still choose one of the two fields.
Only the reading paper has two fields.
They predate FEI's removal of that choice, from March 2020.
questions.explanation: FEI announced in October 2019 that the choice of field would go from the March 2020 sessions, because both versions tested the same skills. Older material still shows it.

questions.stem: What is "une attestation de réussite"?
choices: a certificate of achievement, usually issued before the diploma
the notice that tells you when to come
questions.explanation: Centres usually issue an attestation de réussite first, because the diploma is printed and sent later. The notice to attend is la convocation, the grid la grille d'évaluation.

questions.stem: According to the lesson, where do you write the word count (le décompte des mots) in the writing paper?
choices: at the end of each text, as the paper asks
only at the end of the essay
at the top of the synthesis
questions.explanation: FEI's manual asks candidates to write the number of words at the end of each text, the synthesis and the essay. How words are counted is set by the instructions on the paper.

questions.stem: Which dictionary may you use while preparing the DALF C1 oral, according to FEI's manual?
choices: a translation app on your phone
a monolingual French dictionary supplied by the centre
questions.explanation: The manual allows a dictionnaire unilingue provided by the centre during the hour of preparation, not your own. Use it to check a word, not to read.

questions.stem: Which is the most formal (soutenu) way to say "I don't know"?
questions.explanation: Savoir in the conditionnel with ne alone (je ne saurais) is soutenu. "Je ne sais pas" is standard courant French, correct everywhere; the two forms without ne are informal.

questions.stem: Which connector adds a point in the most formal register?
questions.explanation: De surcroît (like en outre) is formal. En plus is courant, du coup is informal and marks a consequence, and bref concludes.

questions.stem: What does "valider un module" mean?
questions.explanation: In education, valider is to pass (valider un module, un semestre). "To value" is valoriser or apprécier.

questions.stem: What is "un bilan de compétences" in France?
choices: a results slip from an exam
a proficiency level of the CEFR
a formal assessment of your skills and career options
questions.explanation: A bilan de compétences is a career assessment, often before a career change. A results slip is un relevé de notes; the CEFR's levels are niveaux de compétence.

questions.stem: Which reading strategy does the lesson recommend for the long texte d'idées?
choices: Read the text three times before looking at the questions.
Translate the whole text into your own language first.
Answer from memory without going back to the text.
Read the questions first, then the text once, with a three-word summary of each paragraph in the margin.
questions.explanation: With a text of 1,500 to 2,000 words (in the Sorbonne description) and 50 minutes, a map of the paragraphs lets you find each answer fast. Rereading three times or translating wastes time, and answers must come from the text.

questions.stem: What is "une contre-performance"?
choices: a second attempt at a paper
questions.explanation: Une contre-performance is a result below your usual level. At the DALF it can be made up by the other parts, as long as it stays at 5/25 or above.

questions.stem: Listen to the instructions. When is the speaking test?

audio.text: Bonjour. Vous passerez aujourd'hui les épreuves collectives : compréhension de l'oral, compréhension des écrits et production écrite. N'oubliez pas d'indiquer le nombre de mots à la fin de chacun de vos textes. L'épreuve orale aura lieu demain matin.

questions.explanation: "L'épreuve orale aura lieu demain matin." Today is for the three collective papers.

questions.stem: Listen to the candidate. What did the centre give her?

audio.text: J'ai eu onze en compréhension de l'oral, mais dix-neuf en production orale. Au total, soixante-huit sur cent : j'ai réussi, et le centre m'a donné une attestation en attendant le diplôme.

choices: only a results slip, with no other document
an attestation, while she waits for the diploma
questions.explanation: "Le centre m'a donné une attestation en attendant le diplôme." She passed with 68/100.

questions.stem: To pass the DALF C1 you need at least ___ points out of 100 overall (and at least 5 out of 25 in every part). Give only the number.
questions.explanation: Le seuil de réussite is 50/100, with the second condition that no part is below 5/25.

questions.stem: Match each part of the DALF C1 to its time in the current format (FEI's manual).
choices: up to about 30 minutes, after 1 hour of preparation
about 20 minutes, after 30 minutes of preparation
questions.explanation: Listening about 40 minutes, reading 50, writing 2 h 30, speaking up to about 30 minutes after an hour of preparation. The extra answer is the DELF B2 oral.

questions.stem: Which of these are collective papers (épreuves collectives) of the DALF C1? Select all that apply.
choices: the hour of preparation for the oral
questions.explanation: Listening, reading and writing are sat together in a room, about four hours in all. The speaking test, with its preparation, is the épreuve individuelle.

questions.stem: Put the countdown (le compte à rebours) the lesson suggests in order.
choices: a mock exam in real conditions, three or four weeks before
a second mock exam, a week before
light revision in the last two days
a good night's sleep before the exam
questions.explanation: The lesson's countdown goes from the first mock exam a few weeks ahead to sleep the night before (lesson 23 explains why sleep helps memory).

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the DALF C1.

image.alt: An overview chart of the DALF C1 with the names of the parts replaced by numbered markers. A box of collective papers, about 4 hours in all, holds three parts: 1, about 40 minutes, one long document heard twice and short documents heard once, 25 points; 2, 50 minutes, one long text of ideas, 25 points; 3, 2 hours 30, a synthesis and an argued essay, 25 points. A separate box for the individual test holds 4: 1 hour of preparation, then about 30 minutes at most, an exposé and an interaction, 25 points.
